latestRelease.notes:
# Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (v2026.8.18)

**Release Date:** August 18, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~74 PRs merged since v0.20.3 into a stable tagged release for downstream consumers (Docker images, hosted deployments, fresh installs).

---

## About this release

Since v0.20.3 (v2026.8.16.2, tagged August 17), this window landed **~146 commits** across **~265 files** (+21,697 / −2,217) — **~74 merged PRs** including the desktop glass/translucency surface work (matte glass, frost picker, macOS pre-select), the tabbed SESSIONS|BOTS sidebar with per-bot hide/unhide, Bot Mode group-chat fixes (long-running member turns, Markdown rendering, cross-machine routing), NVIDIA SkillEvaluator Tier 1 advisory scanning on skill installs (license + security checks), cron media-send hardening (configurable timeout, manual-run attachments, missed-fire surfacing), SessionDB event-loop-thread and contention fixes, `hermes update` parked-branch honesty, and kanban native OS notifications.

**Full curated release notes for this window will ship with v0.21.0**, which will document everything from v0.20.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- `hermes update` from an existing install
- Fresh install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v2026.8.16.2...v2026.8.18

signals.title: [Feature]: Support multiple independent questions in clarify tool
signals.text: ## Problem or Use Case The `clarify` tool currently accepts only one `question` parameter (a single string). When the agent needs to ask the user multiple independent questions, the only workaround is to concatenate them into one composite question and offer composite choices (e.g. combining "How do you feel?" + "What color do you like?" into one question with choices like "Feeling good, likes blue" / "Feeling tired, likes red" — each choice encoding answers to both questions). This does not scale: 2 questions x 4 choices each = 16 composite options; 3 questions x 3 choices each = 27. The UX degrades rapidly and the agent effectively cannot batch more than 2 small clarification needs at once. Real-world example from use: agent wants to ask (1) user preference on approach A vs B, and (2) user availability timeline. These are independent dimensions — forcing them into a single composite question is unnatural and the combinatorial explosion of choices makes it impractical. ## Proposed Solution Add an optional `questions` array parameter alongside the existing single-`question` parameter. Each question object has its own `question` text and optional `choices` array. The rendering layer (CLI prompt_toolkit, TUI, gateway adapters) presents them as separate widgets/forms, and the tool returns an array of answers keyed by question index or id. Example schema addition: ```json { "questions": { "type": "array", "description": "Multiple independent questions to ask at once. Use instead of single-question when you have 2+ independent clarification needs.", "maxItems": 5, "items": { "type": "object", "properties": { "id": { "type": "string", "description": "Short identifier for matching responses (e.g. 'approach', 'timeline')" }, "question": { "type": "string", "description": "The question text" }, "choices": { "type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "maxItems": 4, "description": "Up to 4 answer choices. Omit for open-ended text input." } }, "required": ["question"] } } } ``` Backward compatibility: the existing single-`question` parameter remains untouched. When `questions` is present, it takes precedence and the single-question parameter is ignored. ## Alternatives Considered 1. **Composite question + composite choices (current workaround)**: Works for 2 small questions but does not scale. 3+ questions become combinatorially impossible. 2. **Multiple sequential `clarify` calls**: Works but wastes conversation turns and context tokens. The agent cannot efficiently batch multiple independent clarification needs. 3. **Free-text multi-question with no structured choices**: Loses the structured choice UX that makes `clarify` useful. Harder for the agent to parse free-form multi-answer responses reliably. 4. **Agent-side heuristics to skip unnecessary questions**: Not always applicable — sometimes multiple independent decisions genuinely need user input. ## Feature Type New tool ## Scope Medium (few files, under 300 lines) ## Contribution - [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: [Bug]: Chinese reasoning tags ( 思考 / 反思 / 推理 / 推敲) from MiniMax-M3 leak to user output in streaming + final response
signals.text:
## Bug Description When using `MiniMax-M3` via the `minimax-tokenplan` provider (or any MiniMax deployment serving the M3 model) the gateway / CLI / agent emit raw Chinese-language reasoning tokens to the user-visible output. Tags such as ` 思考`, ` 反思`, ` 推理`, and ` 推敲` (which MiniMax M3 uses in place of / alongside the English `<think>` family) are not stripped, so end users in Telegram/Discord see fragments like: > 让我 思考 …right in the middle of the assistant's response. The English-tag filtering path (`<think>`, `<thinking>`, `<reasoning>`, `<REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>`, `<thought>`) works correctly — only the Chinese / non-Latin variants are missing from the filter lists. This is a direct sibling of #17924 (which fixed the *English* inline-tag leak on the CLI) and an extension of the filter-completeness issue tracked in #27288 (mixed-case tag variants in streaming). The Chinese tag families were simply never added to the three hard-coded tag tuples that all consumer code paths consult. ## Environment - **Hermes Agent:** v0.16.0 (local checkout at `a8f404b29` on `main`) - **Provider:** `minimax-tokenplan` (custom provider, `https://api.minimax.io/v1`, `api_mode: chat_completions`, API key from `MINIMAX_API_KEY`) - **Model:** `MiniMax-M3` (1M context, displayed as "MiniMax M3" — the new M3 reasoning model, not M2.7) - **Gateway platform:** Telegram (group topic), streaming mode enabled by default - **Config that reproduces:** ```yaml model: default: minimax-tokenplan/MiniMax-M3 provider: minimax-tokenplan providers: minimax-tokenplan: api: https://api.minimax.io/v1 api_key: ${MINIMAX_API_KEY} api_mode: chat_completions default_model: MiniMax-M3 models: MiniMax-M3: context_length: 1000000 ``` ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a custom `minimax-tokenplan` provider pointed at `https://api.minimax.io/v1` with `MiniMax-M3` registered (see config above). 2. Start the gateway and chat with the model via Telegram, or run `hermes chat -m MiniMax-M3 --provider minimax-tokenplan` interactively. 3. Send any prompt that triggers a reasoning response (basically any non-trivial question — M3 reasons by default). 4. Watch the streaming response. 5. Observe: Chinese reasoning tokens (` 思考`, ` 反思`, ` 推理`, ` 推敲`, etc.) are streamed verbatim to the user and also land in the final stored message. The English `<think>` family, by contrast, is filtered correctly. ## Expected Behavior All inline reasoning content — English **or** Chinese — should be silently filtered before it reaches the user, matching the behavior already in place for the English tag set. ## Actual Behavior The Chinese tag open/close pairs are passed straight through. Example observed in `agent.log` for a Telegram topic: ``` 2026-06-10 19:12:10,048 INFO run_agent: OpenAI client created provider=minimax-tokenplan base_url=https://api.minimax.io/v1 model=MiniMax-M3 2026-06-10 19:12:20,378 INFO agent.conversation_loop: API call #1 model=MiniMax-M3 provider=minimax-tokenplan in=64539 out=523 total=65062 latency=10.3s ``` The 523 output tokens include the raw Chinese tag payloads, which are then sent to Telegram as part of the response (and persisted in the session transcript). ## Root Cause The three filter sites that all consumer code paths consult are hard-coded to the **English** reasoning-tag family only. None of them include the Chinese variants that MiniMax M3 emits. A comment at the top of each list explicitly says they "must stay in sync" — meaning any fix has to be applied in all three places. | # | File | Lines | Symbol | What's stored | |---|------|-------|--------|---------------| | 1 | `gateway/stream_consumer.py` | 101–108 | `GatewayStreamConsumer._OPEN_THINK_TAGS` / `_CLOSE_THINK_TAGS` | Streaming-time state-machine filter that scrubs interim Telegram / Discord edits | | 2 | `cli.py` | 4664–4765 | `HermesCLI._stream_delta` local `_OPEN_TAGS` / `_CLOSE_TAGS` | CLI streaming-time filter for `prompt_toolkit` | | 3 | `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` | 449–510 | `strip_think_blocks()` regexes (5 `re.sub` calls for the English tags) | Final post-processing for stored / sent content | Current contents of all three lists are identical and incomplete: ```python _OPEN_THINK_TAGS = ( "<REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "<think>", "<reasoning>", "<THINKING>", "<thinking>", "<thought>", ) _CLOSE_THINK_TAGS = ( "</REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "</think>", "</reasoning>", "</THINKING>", "</thinking>", "</thought>", ) ``` Note: the `strip_think_blocks()` function applies its `re.sub` regexes case-insensitively (good — covers mixed-case English), but the streaming state machines in the other two files do a plain `str.find()` comparison against the exact tuples above, so even the case-insensitive coverage from `strip_think_blocks` doesn't extend to them. ## Suggested Fix Extend all three tag tuples to include the Chinese families MiniMax M3 uses. The exact set I have observed in the wild is: - ` 思考` (think) - ` 反思` (reflect) - ` 推理` (reason / reason out) - ` 推敲` (deliberate / weigh) A minimal patch that brings all three sites back in sync: ```python _OPEN_THINK_TAGS = ( "<REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "<think>", "<reasoning>", "<THINKING>", "<thinking>", "<thought>", " 思考", " 反思", " 推理", " 推敲", ) _CLOSE_THINK_TAGS = ( "</REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "</think>", "</reasoning>", "</THINKING>", "</thinking>", "</thought>", " 思考", " 反思", " 推理", " 推敲", ) ``` For the streaming state machines in `stream_consumer.py` and `cli.py`, the comparison is currently a case-sensitive `str.find()`. To also cover the mixed-case bug from #27288 in the same change, consider normalising the search buffer (`.lower()` once per delta) while preserving the original text for emission — that way a single change closes both the Chinese-tag gap and the mixed-case tag gap. For `strip_think_blocks()` in `agent_runtime_helpers.py`, add four parallel `re.sub` calls (case-insensitive, `re.DOTALL`) so the post-processing layer can never persist the raw tokens either: ```python content = re.sub(r' 思考.*? 思考', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) content = re.sub(r' 反思.*? 反思', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) content = re.sub(r' 推理.*? 推理', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) content = re.sub(r' 推敲.*? 推敲', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) ``` A small regression test in `tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_chinese_think_tags.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_strip_think_blocks.py` that feeds a known M3 response (e.g. `" 思考
…
 思考
The answer is 42."`) through each filter and asserts the visible output is just `"The answer is 42."` would prevent this from regressing again. ## Workarounds Discovered (no code change) Until the upstream fix lands, three workarounds work reliably: 1. **Disable native reasoning for the model** (drops the tag emission, but also drops the chain-of-thought — works against the "smart" use case but eliminates the leak): ```yaml providers: minimax-tokenplan: extra_body: reasoning: enabled: false ``` 2. **Route the affected chat/topic to `MiniMax-M2.7`** (which doesn't emit Chinese think tags, only the English `<think>` family that the filter already handles). Per-channel override: ```yaml telegram:-1003865674168:13: model: default: minimax-tokenplan/MiniMax-M2.7 ``` ## Related Issues - #17924 — same family, English tags on the CLI (closed / completed — this fix should be the model) - #27288 — same family, mixed-case English tags in streaming (still open — addressing it in the same PR would be ideal) - #9685 — `GatewayStreamConsumer._clean_for_display` did not filter `<think>` blocks (closed — direct ancestor of this bug class) - #27834 — MiniMax XML tool calls rendered as text (related: another MiniMax-specific content-shape issue that falls through the same filter gap) - #41379 — `reasoning_effort: none` silently dropped on Anthropic-protocol third-party providers (MiniMax M3/M2.7) — same provider, adjacent symptom ## Additional Context - API calls themselves are healthy: 89–100% cache hit rate, 3–10 s latency, no upstream errors after the alias fix. - Same M3 response reaches the user correctly on the non-streaming path, because `_strip_think_blocks` runs over the assembled message at the end — the leak is only in the *interim* stream edits the gateway sends during generation, plus the persisted transcript (which does not go through `strip_think_blocks` until later). - The Chinese tag set is specific to MiniMax M3 in my testing; M2.7 continues to use only the English `<think>` family.

signals.title: TUI and dashboard rebuild/reinstall on every launch — monorepo workspace lockfile mismatch
signals.text: ## Bug Description `hermes dashboard` and `hermes --tui` trigger a full TUI npm install and/or frontend rebuild on **every launch**, even when nothing has changed. This adds 30–120s of cold-start time. There are **three independent but related** causes: ### 1. `_tui_need_npm_install` — workspace lockfile scope mismatch `_tui_need_npm_install()` compares the root `package-lock.json` (1505 packages, covering ALL workspaces: desktop, web, bootstrap-installer, etc.) against `node_modules/.package-lock.json` (795 packages, only what `npm ci --workspace ui-tui` installed). The comparison finds ~490 "missing" packages that belong to other workspaces, and returns `True` on every launch. The content-based comparison was added to fix a previous mtime false-positive (see comment at line 1397), but it does not account for npm workspace scoped installs where the hidden lock only reflects the installed subset. ### 2. `_tui_need_rebuild` — `package-lock.json` in build inputs `_TUI_BUILD_INPUT_FILES` includes `"package-lock.json"`. The `_tui_need_rebuild()` function compares these inputs by mtime against `dist/entry.js`. Since `npm run build` updates `package-lock.json`, the dist is always "stale" after a build → rebuild loop. ### 3. `_web_ui_build_needed` — same `package-lock.json` mtime issue `_web_ui_build_needed()` checks if root `package-lock.json` is newer than `hermes_cli/web_dist/`. Same loop as #2: `npm run build` updates the lockfile → always stale → rebuild every time. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. `git clone` hermes-agent, `uv pip install -e .`, `npm install` 2. Run `hermes dashboard` — observe "Installing TUI dependencies…" and/or frontend rebuild 3. Quit, run `hermes dashboard` again — same thing happens ## Expected Behavior - TUI npm install should only run when `@hermes/ink` is actually missing or its version changed - Dashboard/TUI rebuild should only run when source files changed, not when `package-lock.json` was updated by the build itself ## Environment - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 - Python: 3.11.15 (uv-managed venv) - Node.js: v22.22.0 - Hermes Agent: v0.16.0 (editable install via `uv pip install -e .`) ## Root Cause The monorepo has npm workspaces (desktop, web, bootstrap-installer, shared, ui-tui). A scoped `npm ci --workspace ui-tui` only installs ~795 of the 1505 packages in the root lockfile. The staleness checks were written for a single-package layout and do not account for this gap. ## Suggested Fix 1. **`_tui_need_npm_install`**: The `@hermes/ink` sentinel (line 1423) already validates the critical TUI dependency. Replace the full lockfile content comparison with a simple mtime check against the hidden lockfile, relying on the ink sentinel for actual dependency validation. 2. **`_TUI_BUILD_INPUT_FILES`**: Remove `"package-lock.json"` — changes to dependencies are already captured by `"package.json"`. 3. **`_web_ui_build_needed`**: Remove the root `package-lock.json` mtime check (lines 4468–4471) — same reasoning.
signals.author: Asanilo

signals.title: Bug Report: Hermes Client cancels local LLM streams after ~1.5s during prompt evaluation / reasoning (Triggering `<unused49>` token loop)
signals.text: ### Bug Report: Hermes Client cancels local LLM streams after ~1.5s during prompt evaluation / reasoning (Triggering `<unused49>` token loop) #### Summary Following a recent Hermes update, requests routed to a local Ollama backend fail consistently. Hermes issues a client-side cancellation (`cancel task`) after approximately 1.4 to 1.6 seconds while the local model is still evaluating the system prompt / generating initial reasoning chunks. This triggers a broken retry loop (4 continuation attempts) and outputs raw `<unused49>` token artifacts. Direct execution via the Ollama CLI (`ollama run`) runs without issues and produces complete, fluent responses. --- #### Environment - **Host OS:** Linux (x86_64) - **Client:** Hermes Agent (CLI `hermes chat` and Desktop Wrapper) both V 0.20.1 - **Backend:** Ollama (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`) - **Model:** Gemma 4 (26B) with custom parameters (`num_ctx 131072`, `num_predict 16384`) --- #### Timeline & Background 1. **Prior Stable State:** The setup ran out-of-the-box for days with fast response times (~50 tokens/s) and zero stream interruptions. 2. **Trigger:** A routine Hermes update was installed on the morning of August 15. No configurations in Ollama or the underlying GGUF/Modelfile were modified. 3. **Onset:** Beginning midday on August 15 and continuing to date, all chat sessions (CLI and GUI) fail immediately with stream truncation. --- #### Observed Behavior & Logs **Hermes Output:** ```text ● Hallo George, wie ist dein Status? Initializing agent... ──────────────────────────────────────── ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response still truncated after 4 continuation attempts — keeping the partial response received so far. <unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49>... Ollama Backend Log (journalctl -u ollama): Plaintext ollama[14322]: slot operator(): id 1 | task 64 | new prompt, n_ctx_slot = 131072, task.n_tokens = 16862 ollama[14322]: [GIN] | 200 | 1.621478725s | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/v1/chat/completions" ollama[14322]: srv stop: cancel task, id_task = 64 ollama[14322]: slot release: id 1 | task 64 | stop processing: n_tokens = 16894, truncated = 0 Root Cause Analysis Premature Client-Side Timeout / Empty-Chunk Dropping: Hermes sends a large system prompt (~17k tokens from tool schemas / core capabilities). Evaluating ~17k tokens on local hardware naturally takes 1.5–2.5 seconds before the first text token can be emitted. During this initial prefill/thinking window, the stream contains content: "" chunks (or reasoning deltas). Hermes interprets this as an abandoned stream and sends an active abort (cancel task) after ~1.5s. Context Corruption from Auto-Continuation: After the premature client abort, Hermes triggers 4 automated continuation attempts. Because the initial turn was severed mid-generation, the model context becomes corrupted, causing Gemma's tokenizer to emit separator token ID 49 (<unused49>). Expected Behavior Hermes must not drop or cancel active SSE streams during the prompt evaluation (prefill) or reasoning phase of local endpoints. Client-side first-token timeouts should be fully configurable or respect request_timeout / stream_timeout settings rather than enforcing a hardcoded ~1.5s threshold. Incomplete stream handling should fail gracefully instead of corrupting the context into an <unused49> continuation loop. Hermes is unusable this way!

signals.title: [desktop] Renderer process burns 40-70% CPU at idle since early August — thermal throttling on macOS Intel
signals.text: ### Environment - macOS 13.3.1, MacBook Pro 2019 (Intel Core i5-8279U, 4C8T, 16GB) - Hermes v0.20.2 (2026.8.16), Electron 40.10.2, packaged desktop build - GPU disabled via `desktop.disable_gpu=true` (partially mitigates) ### Symptom - `Hermes Helper (Renderer)` consumes **40-73% CPU continuously while idle** (no streaming, no content updates; window focused or not) - `Hermes Helper` main process additionally 16-44% - macOS thermal throttling engaged: `CPU_Speed_Limit` dropped to 24-68 → fans at max, machine sluggish - Started early August 2026; worsening since - **Survives app restart**; **present in v0.20.2** (upgraded 0.19.0 → 0.20.2, 2394 commits) ### Evidence Renderer sampling over 26 min of uptime: **11:01 CPU / 26:31 wall = 41.6% average**, instantaneous 73.3% — with the app sitting on a **blank new conversation** (long-session rendering ruled out). | process | idle CPU (instant) | avg | |---|---|---| | Renderer | 52.8-87.8% | 41-70% | | Helper (main) | 19.4-44.5% | 16-31% | | WindowServer | 37.8% | repaint storm | ### Already ruled out - Not long-session DOM: reproduced on a fresh empty conversation - Not memory pressure: 77% free, 1GB swap - Not corporate VPN agent (aTrust/EAIO): ~0% CPU - Not Macs Fan Control: ActivePreset=Predefined:0 (auto mode) - Not battery: 31°C while charging - `desktop.disable_gpu=true` partially mitigates: ~70% → ~40% (GPU compositor loop is part of the cause, not all) ### Suspects (source scan) High-frequency timers in `apps/desktop/src` that re-render on every tick: - `src/app/hud/hud-shell.tsx:237` — `setInterval(measure, 300)` (HUD) - `src/app/hud/hud-shell.tsx:329` — `setInterval(measure, 500)` - `src/app/chat/chat-swap-overlay.tsx:28` — 80ms frame animation - `src/app/messaging/index.tsx:237` — 6s tick - several 1s `setNow`/`setNowMs` intervals Note: `src/app/shell/hooks/use-status-snapshot.ts` already gates its 60s refresh on `document.hasFocus()`/`visibilityState` correctly; other timers may not. ### Expected - Fix the idle repaint loop (gate timers/animations on focus & visibility) - Or expose a config to disable ambient animations/timers ### Impact Idle machine gets thermally throttled; on Intel Macs severe (CPU_Speed_Limit 24 ≈ 1/4 frequency); fan noise and battery life affected. Started early August 2026 (approx. the 8/6 update window).
signals.author: yuhengliuleo

signals.title: [Feature]: Settle, Snooze, and Wake lifecycle for human attention
signals.text: ## Problem or Use Case Parallel autonomous work can leave many sessions completed or needing attention. Hermes now has a strong Desktop foundation—Inbox-style sidebar cards (#84960, #85109), attention/session state, and persisted unread/read behavior (#86772)—but “I have seen and handled this” is not the same as opening, hiding, archiving, or completing a thread. This becomes especially costly when several background threads finish together: there is no reversible acknowledgement queue, no timed deferral, and no deterministic way for deferred attention to return. This is related to, but intentionally narrower than, the notification/visibility work in #50718: unread answers “what changed?”; this lifecycle answers “what have I intentionally dealt with, or deferred until later?” ## Proposed Solution Add a small human-attention lifecycle for sessions/threads, inspired behaviorally by the public MIT-licensed [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code) experience: - **Settle** — acknowledge a thread without deleting or archiving it. This is reversible, and the thread remains recoverable in a compact settled-history view. - **Snooze(until)** — remove a thread from active attention until a chosen time. - **Wake** — return a snoozed thread on expiry or manual action, surfaced prominently enough not to be mistaken for ordinary history. - **Resurface** — consequential new activity can deterministically wake/unsettle a thread. Incidental metadata changes should not. These are attention actions only. Kanban remains authoritative for workflow state: `review` and `done` must not be overloaded, and Settle/Snooze/Wake must never complete, reopen, cancel, or otherwise mutate a task. The state should survive Desktop/backend restarts and behave consistently across devices. Controls and state must remain keyboard/screen-reader accessible, use non-color cues, and work at mobile widths with touch-sized targets. ### Minimal state transitions | Current | Action/event | Next | | --- | --- | --- | | Active | Settle | Settled | | Active or Settled | Snooze(until) | Snoozed | | Snoozed | Expiry or manual Wake | Active + prominently surfaced | | Settled or Snoozed | Consequential new activity | Active + prominently surfaced | | Settled | Manual restore | Active | ### Acceptance criteria - Settle is reversible and settled items remain discoverable. - Snooze persists an explicit deadline; expiry/manual Wake returns the item exactly once. - A documented rule distinguishes consequential activity that resurfaces an item from changes that do not. - State and deadlines survive restart and converge across devices without silently dropping attention. - Attention transitions do not mutate Kanban/task workflow status. - Desktop and mobile-width UI is keyboard/touch accessible and does not rely on color alone. - Transition and persistence behavior has deterministic tests, including restart and repeated-event/idempotency cases. ## Alternatives Considered - **Archive/hide:** useful for session organization, but too strong and semantically different from acknowledgement or temporary deferral. - **Unread/read only:** identifies unseen activity, but opening a thread is not proof that its outcome was handled. - **Map attention onto Kanban `review`/`done`:** rejected because it would make a presentation concern mutate authoritative execution state. - **Notifications/reminders alone:** transient delivery does not provide a recoverable attention queue. ## Implementation boundary to confirm Before implementation, could maintainers confirm the preferred ownership boundary for durable state and timers—Desktop-local storage, the existing session backend/API, or another shared service? The UX should follow that contract rather than introducing a competing task model. ## Feature Type Other ## Scope Large (new module or significant refactor)
signals.author: kvnloo

signals.title: Design: compact, summary-first information architecture for Kanban
signals.text: ## Summary Hermes Kanban has strong workflow semantics, but the current board presents setup, board administration, orchestration, attention, filtering, and daily task work at nearly the same visual level. This issue proposes a focused information architecture and density pass for Desktop and WebUI. It is a design-quality follow-up to #87244, not a replacement for that responsive usability fix. The goal is simple: help an operator answer "what needs attention, who owns it, and what is blocked?" before exposing setup and executor detail. ## Jobs to be done Frequent: - scan lane state and find high-risk or stale work - understand owner, age, dependencies, and active worker state - open, create, move, and comment on tasks - resolve attention and switch board or active filters - preserve horizontal lane memory Occasional or administrative: - create or archive a board - edit board settings - configure orchestration - inspect model, workspace, skills, goal mode, raw specification, or repository provenance The present UI gives several occasional controls persistent top-level space and renders much executor metadata at the same weight as the task purpose. ## Proposed hierarchy ### Desktop board ```text [global rail] [Board / 24 tasks] [Orchestrating / 3] [Search] [Filters 2] [Attention 2] [...] [New task] [active filter chips] [density / live state] Todo 5 Ready 3 In progress 4 Blocked 2 Review 3 card card card card card ``` - Use one compact board header. Keep board switcher, task count, orchestration state, search, filters, attention count, and one `New task` primary action. - Move Settings, New board, Archive, and manual Nudge into an overflow or board-admin menu. - Replace the full attention region with a severity/count control that opens a focused rail. - Show active filters as removable chips; keep filter construction in one popover. - Start lanes directly below the header and filter row. Keep headers sticky with status, count, optional WIP, and add action. - Keep horizontal board semantics. Empty lanes may collapse to a narrow rail, but must remain discoverable. - Card order: title, machine or human risk state, owner, dependency signal, age. Hide long descriptions and internal IDs until open. - Cream is reserved for the true primary action. Status colors carry semantic meaning only. ### Mobile board and task drawer Use one focused, snap-aligned lane with an explicit lane selector and count. Open task details as a viewport-contained drawer. Drawer hierarchy: 1. human summary: title, status, owner, urgency, blocker or outcome 2. concise purpose and acceptance conditions 3. full-width disclosure rows for `Execution details`, `Repository & provenance`, and `View specification` 4. attachments, comments, activity, and run history by task relevance 5. admin actions in overflow The drawer should use one content grid and one gutter. Labels and values must align; values wrap only inside the value column. Paths use inset monospace blocks aligned to that grid. At 320, 360, 390, and 430px there must be no hanging labels, orphan separators, or arbitrary indentation. Disclosure rows and actions need at least 44px targets. ## Measurable acceptance criteria | Measure | Current observed direction | Target | |---|---:|---:| | Board chrome before lanes at 900px height | multiple stacked control regions | lanes begin by 120px from board content top | | Persistent primary-emphasis actions | several cream controls compete | exactly 1 primary action | | Desktop board controls before overflow | setup and work mixed | 7 or fewer visible work controls | | Visible cards at 1600x900 | low due to chrome and verbose cards | at least 4 compact cards in each populated lane without body scroll | | Drawer metadata | inline wrapping / mixed alignment | stable label-value grid with one gutter | | Touch targets | mixed | 44x44px minimum for primary controls and disclosures | | Horizontal containment | right lanes and drawer can overflow | no page-level overflow at 320/360/390/430/768/1600px | | Keyboard | partial pointer-first flow | search shortcut, lane/card navigation, open, move, create, close, and focus return | | Accessibility | quiet secondary text and tiny controls are risky | WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, visible focus, semantic names, reduced-motion support | | Performance | no explicit redesign budget | no new heavy UI framework; virtualize or incrementally render large lanes; avoid idle animation work | ## Interaction and accessibility details - Preserve drag and drop on desktop, but provide menu and keyboard equivalents for every move. - Return focus to the originating card when the drawer closes. - Announce lane moves and filter result counts to assistive technology. - Do not encode state by color alone. - Mobile does not require drag and drop. Use explicit Move action plus snap navigation. - Density may be `comfortable` and `compact` only if persisted per board; otherwise ship one well-tested compact default. ## Why this fits Hermes The proposal keeps the existing dark-green and cream identity, system tokens, compact mono metadata, status tones, profile identity, live orchestration state, and horizontal workflow model. It changes prominence and grouping rather than importing another product's skin. The current Desktop component boundaries already support a phased pass: `board.tsx`, `drawer.tsx`, `board-switcher.tsx`, `orchestration.tsx`, shared `ui.tsx`, and plugin tokens. WebUI should share the same behavioral contract even where rendering code remains separate. ## Research principles - Progressive disclosure: [Carbon disclosure pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/accordion/usage/) - Minimum target size and focus: [WCAG 2.2 target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html) and [focus appearance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html) - Board and table view customization: [GitHub Projects documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/customizing-the-board-layout) - Keyboard-first command access: [Linear keyboard shortcuts](https://linear.app/docs/keyboard-shortcuts) - Responsive layout and adaptive navigation: [Material 3 adaptive layouts](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/applying-layout/window-size-classes) These are principle references only. The proposed visuals remain original and Hermes-native. ## Suggested phases 1. IA and board chrome: compact header, attention control, filters, lane headers, card hierarchy. 2. Task drawer: summary-first content grid and progressive disclosure of executor/provenance detail. 3. Mobile and keyboard: focused lane selector, drawer behavior, focus management, explicit move actions. 4. Density and scale: persisted density only if needed, large-board rendering budget, shared Desktop/WebUI behavior tests. ## Non-goals - no Kanban state-machine or dispatcher changes - no replacement for #87244 - no redesign of unrelated dashboard pages - no new animation system or heavy component framework - no hidden removal of diagnostics, provenance, runs, or raw task specifications ## Maintainer question Would maintainers prefer the responsive and information-hierarchy contract to live in shared Kanban layout primitives used by Desktop and WebUI, or should the two surfaces keep separate renderers with shared behavior tests?

signals.title: HOTL: typed topology IR and honest badge decoder
signals.text: # Proposed upstream issue: HOTL: typed topology IR and honest badge decoder (#88580 follow-up) Related: #88580, #88061 Hermes currently has strong execution primitives (Kanban parent/child dependencies, runs, leases, retries, review lanes, goal/judge loops, profiles, and evidence gates), but no canonical machine-readable vocabulary for describing an agent network. Terms such as `swarm`, `mesh`, `hierarchy`, `orchestrator`, and `council` conflate graph shape, control policy, communication, role, runtime state, and placement. A badge without a decoder can imply guarantees Hermes does not provide. Proposal: docs/spec first, provisionally HOTL 0.1 (name open for maintainer feedback). The core IR has typed nodes and edges, explicit ports, fan-in/dynamic-fanout policies, coordination substrate, assurance requirements, provenance, annotations, and observations. It classifies from normalized graph + policy and permits composite labels; it never infers swarm/intelligence/consensus from a drawing. Minimal example: ```json {"specVersion":"0.1","graphId":"research-fanin","nodes":[{"id":"r1","role":"worker"},{"id":"synth","role":"orchestrator"}],"edges":[{"id":"e","from":"r1","to":"synth","kind":"dependency"}],"policies":{"fanIn":"all","coordination":"ledger","dynamicFanOut":{"allowed":false,"maxChildren":0}},"provenance":{"source":"example","sourceHash":"<sha256>"}} ``` Safe Kanban subset: one task per node; dependency edges become parent lists; explicit review nodes become review children; bounded goal loops use existing goal/judge mechanisms; dry-run receipts include source hash/version and idempotency keys. Data/message/blackboard/auction/ring/mesh constructs are visualization-only until Hermes has a real runtime contract. Reverse projection reports only structural facts and marks policies unknown. Validation rejects implicit cycles, ambiguous fan-in, unbounded spawn, illegal self edges, unreachable nodes, hidden privileged actions, incompatible ports, and unsupported guarantee claims. Badge glyphs show topology only; state is a separate marker and accessible text. Requested maintainer decision: should this live first as docs/spec, a shared schema module, or a future Kanban API? Proposed phases: schema/docs → validator → read-only projector → dry-run compiler → earned execution subset. Non-goals: scheduler, graph runtime, execution-authority changes, or ranking agents. Standards surveyed include BPMN 2.0, Petri nets, CWL/WDL, Argo/Tekton, Temporal/Step Functions, actor model, LangGraph, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Agents, MCP and A2A. None is a universal agent-topology naming standard; each formalizes a different slice. Intent: `kvnloo` (assignment may be unavailable; please advise if issue ownership is preferred).

signals.title: [Bug] terminal tool crashes: "embedded null character in path" (lifecycle_guard missing ValueError catch)
signals.text: ## 现象 Windows (git-bash/MSYS) 下用 terminal 工具执行 `python -m pytest` 报： `ValueError: open: embedded null character in path` ## 根因（已定位到行） `cron/lifecycle_guard.py` `_read_referenced_script`（第 256-262 行）： ```python try: descriptor = os.open(path, flags) # path 含 null 抛 ValueError except OSError: # 只捕获 OSError，未捕获 ValueError return None, False ``` path 含 null 字符时 os.open() 抛 ValueError（非 OSError），未捕获，异常上抛导致崩溃。 对比同文件第 313-316 行已正确 `except (OSError, ValueError)`（#76762），但第 324 行传给 _read_referenced_script 的是未 resolve 的 script_path（null 残留）。 ## 修复建议（一行） 第 261 行 `except OSError:` → `except (OSError, ValueError):` ## 环境 Windows 10 (git-bash/MSYS 后端)

signals.title: [Bug]: MCP trust gate: readOnlyHint never detected on live-discovered tools (camelCase attr vs snake_case in the SDK) — trust: untrusted gates every read-only tool
signals.text: ### Bug Description With `trust: untrusted` on an MCP server, **every** tool is classified as write-capable — including tools the server correctly annotates with `readOnlyHint: true`. The trust gate then prompts for approval on every read, which makes an untrusted server unusable in practice. **Root cause:** `_annotation_read_only_hint` (`tools/mcp_tool.py:4335`) reads the annotation attribute in **camelCase**, but the MCP Python SDK materializes it in **snake_case** (`read_only_hint`), so the object branch used by live discovery always misses and the function returns `False` unconditionally. Details in the Root Cause Analysis section below. **Secondary issue — the schema cache persists the wrong value and never self-heals:** 1. The cache stores the *result* of the broken computation (`"readOnlyHint": false`) rather than what the server sent, so the otherwise-correct dict branch reads a poisoned value on subsequent loads. 2. `mcp_schema_cache.config_fingerprint` (`tools/mcp_schema_cache.py:31`) hashes only `command`, `args`, `url`, `transport`, `tools_include`, `tools_exclude` — nothing derived from the server tool metadata, so a server-side annotation change never invalidates the cache. Net effect: after a server adds `readOnlyHint` annotations, Hermes keeps classifying its tools as write-capable indefinitely. Clearing the cache entry by hand does not help, because the live-discovery path re-derives the same wrong value. **Impact:** `trust: untrusted` is the documented way to require per-call approval for write-capable MCP tools. Today it cannot distinguish reads from writes, so the only options are "approve every single call" or "disable the gate" — the security control it implements is effectively unavailable. Searched open and closed issues beforehand; no duplicate found. ### Steps to Reproduce Minimal repro (no server required): ```python import mcp.types as T from tools import mcp_tool as M from types import SimpleNamespace t = T.Tool(name="list_things", inputSchema={}, annotations={"readOnlyHint": True}) print(t.annotations) # read_only_hint=True ... print(getattr(t.annotations, "readOnlyHint", "ABSENT")) # ABSENT print(M._annotation_read_only_hint(t)) # False <-- bug # dict branch (schema-cache JSON) is fine: o = SimpleNamespace(name="list_things", annotations={"readOnlyHint": True}) print(M._annotation_read_only_hint(o)) # True ``` End to end: 1. Configure a remote HTTP MCP server whose `tools/list` returns `annotations: {"readOnlyHint": true}` for its read-only tools. 2. Set `trust: untrusted` on that server in `config.yaml`. 3. Run `hermes chat` and let the agent call any read-only tool from that server. 4. The trust gate prompts for approval on every call, claiming the tool is write-capable. ### Expected Behavior Tools the server annotates with `readOnlyHint: true` are classified as read-only, and the `trust: untrusted` gate only prompts for tools that are actually write-capable. ### Actual Behavior Every tool on the server is classified as write-capable and gated: ``` MCP tool 'list_clients' on UNTRUSTED server '<server>' wants to run. This tool is write-capable (no readOnlyHint=true annotation) and may modify external state. ``` Verified against the server with a raw `tools/list` call — the annotations are present and correct on the wire. ### Affected Component Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell Not applicable / not available for this report: the bug reproduces deterministically from a Python REPL against the installed SDK (see Steps to Reproduce) and does not depend on session state or logs. Happy to attach `hermes debug share` links if they would still help. ``` ### Operating System Linux (Ubuntu) — terminal.backend: docker ### Python Version 3.11.16 ### Hermes Version 0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2), git install ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) `tools/mcp_tool.py:4335`: ```python annotations = getattr(mcp_tool, "annotations", None) if annotations is None: return False if isinstance(annotations, dict): hint = annotations.get("readOnlyHint") # wire name — correct for cache dicts else: hint = getattr(annotations, "readOnlyHint", None) # SDK object uses read_only_hint return hint is True ``` The SDK parses the wire field `readOnlyHint` into the Python attribute `read_only_hint`. `ToolAnnotations.model_fields` on the installed SDK: ``` ['destructive_hint', 'idempotent_hint', 'open_world_hint', 'read_only_hint', 'title'] ``` So on the object branch (live discovery) the `getattr` always misses and `_annotation_read_only_hint` returns `False` unconditionally. The dict branch (schema-cache JSON) is correct in isolation, but the cache stores the derived boolean instead of the server annotations, so it persists the wrong value — and `config_fingerprint` in `tools/mcp_schema_cache.py:31` contains nothing server-derived, so the entry is never invalidated. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Accept both spellings on the object branch: ```python if isinstance(annotations, dict): hint = annotations.get("readOnlyHint", annotations.get("read_only_hint")) else: hint = getattr(annotations, "read_only_hint", None) if hint is None: hint = getattr(annotations, "readOnlyHint", None) return hint is True ``` Worth considering alongside it: - Cache what the server actually sent (`annotations` verbatim) instead of the derived boolean, so the cache cannot outlive a classification bug. - Include something server-derived in the cache fingerprint, or drop annotations from the cache entirely and re-derive them at discovery. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: [Bug][Windows] Python backend shell-out creates visible flashing console windows (uv/git) — missing CREATE_NO_WINDOW
signals.text: # 临时 issue body 文件 ## Summary On Windows, when Hermes is running as a **console-less process** (the desktop backend `pythonw`/hidden spawn, or the gateway), any external program spawned via `subprocess.run`/`Popen` **without `creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW` creates a visible console window that flashes briefly** on screen. This is most visible when Hermes invokes `uv` (e.g. installing a tool/dependency) or `git` — the user sees a black `cmd` window pop up and disappear. This is a Windows-only cosmetic/user-experience bug that has been observed on v0.20.1. ## Affected Code The root cause pattern is in `hermes_cli/managed_uv.py` (13 `subprocess.run([uv, ...])` calls with no `creationflags`). A general scan of core runtime directories found **~77 files / 200+ call sites** that shell out via `subprocess` on Windows without `creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, including (highest count first): - `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` (78) - `hermes_cli/main.py` (41) - `tools/environments/docker.py` (19) - `hermes_cli/clipboard.py` (14) - `tools/environments/ssh.py` (11) - `hermes_cli/banner.py` (8), `agent/proxy_sources/iron_proxy.py` (8) - `hermes_cli/service_manager.py` (7), `tools/voice_mode.py` (7) - and ~40 more (setup, doctor, uninstall, plugins, gateway, etc.) Note: `subprocess` inherits the parent's console when the parent HAS one; it only creates a *new visible* console when the parent is console-less (typical for the desktop backend / gateway). So even with `capture_output=True`, spawned children still pop a window on those hosts. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Run Hermes Desktop on Windows (backend is a hidden, console-less python process). 2. Trigger any operation that makes Hermes invoke `uv` (e.g. `hermes` installing a skill/tool dependency) or `git` (e.g. repo status/scan). 3. Observe a black console window flash and close. ## Expected Behavior External programs spawned by the Hermes backend should never create a visible console window on Windows — they should use `creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (or `DETACHED_PROCESS`). ## Proposed Fix There is already a helper in `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py`: - `windows_hide_flags()` → returns `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (0x08000000) - `windows_detach_popen_kwargs()` → detached process kwargs Recommended: 1. Route the **batch of common shell-out call sites** (managed_uv, update_cmd, main, clipboard, banner, service_manager, doctor, uninstall, profiles, plugins_cmd, setup, npm_engine, relaunch, _install_repair, …) through a shared wrapper that injects `creationflags=windows_hide_flags() if os.name == 'nt' else 0` — exactly what was done for `managed_uv.py` locally (a `_run()` alias). 2. **Do not** blanket-apply to `tools/terminal_tool.py` and similar tools that intentionally display a terminal. 3. Scope the sweep to the windowless-runner paths (backend/gateway/desktop), not the interactive CLI. ## Environment - OS: Windows 10 (19045) - Hermes: v0.20.1 - Repro: Desktop app backend (hidden console process) spawning `uv`/`git`

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop Restore after in-place compaction refused with 4030 (live-scrollback ordinal ≠ resolved row_id)
signals.text: ### Bug Description After **in-place** context compaction (same `session_id`, no parent), Desktop **Restore** on a still-active user turn is refused with **4030**: ``` truncate_before_user_ordinal (N) does not match truncate_before_row_id target turn (M) prefix_user_count=0 ``` `truncate_before_row_id` **resolves correctly**. The cut is refused only because Desktop also sends a client ordinal counted over **live scrollback that survived compact**. Same error code as #88082, different trigger: | | #88082 / #88092 | this report | |---|---|---| | When | cold-open, transcript longer than the 120-row prefetch | live session; compaction just ran; pre-compact bubbles still on screen | | Ordinal direction | client **smaller** than durable (window missing prefix) | client **larger** than the gateway **tip** (scrollback still includes compacted / handoff user rows) | | `prefix_user_count` | 0 | 0 | | Would #88092 fix it? | yes, when `possiblyTruncated` | **no** — live scrollback is treated as complete, so the ordinal is still sent | No history is deleted (4030 fail-closed is doing its job). Restore on those still-active turns stays dead. Related, not this bug: #87547 is **4004** (ordinal-only, missing `row_id`). Compacted-away turns correctly return **4018** and are out of scope. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Hermes Desktop, durable session, `compression.in_place` left at default (on). 2. Stay in the session long enough for in-place compaction to fire. Do not cold-open. Do not click “Show earlier messages”. 3. Confirm pre-compact user bubbles are still visible, plus a `[CONTEXT COMPACTION]` handoff. 4. Restore / rewind a user turn that is **still in the tip** (not one compacted away). 5. Actual: 4030, `prefix_user_count=0`, client ordinal ≠ tip ordinal for the same resolved `row_id`. 6. Retry: same refusal. ### Expected Behavior Restore aimed by `truncate_before_row_id` succeeds. If a client ordinal is sent, it must be in the same space the gateway uses — or omitted once a durable id is present. ### Actual Behavior Gateway returns **4030**. Transcript unchanged. Restore remains unusable for those still-active turns. Example shape (sanitized): client ordinal **greater than** tip ordinal for the resolved row (observed 2 or 4 vs tip 1), `prefix_user_count=0`. Log line: `REFUSED truncation due to ordinal mismatch` / `Stale truncate_before_user_ordinal detected`. The ordinal is not stale; it is display-lineage. ### Affected Component - Other (Hermes Desktop + local TUI gateway `prompt.submit`) - Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (not a messaging adapter — Desktop UI talking to the local gateway) ### Debug Report [hermes-gui-89244-sanitized.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31185841/hermes-gui-89244-sanitized.log) ### Operating System macOS 27.0 (arm64) ### Python Version 3.11.15 ### Hermes Version 0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2), local gateway. Desktop packaged 0.17.0 (not source-mode). ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ``` prompt.submit: REFUSED truncation due to ordinal mismatch (ordinal=<client>, truncate_before_row_id_ordinal=<tip>, truncate_before_row_id=<resolved>, prefix_user_count=0). Stale truncate_before_user_ordinal detected. ``` Row id resolved. Client ordinal > tip ordinal. No session id / row id / transcript text included. ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) Two ordinal spaces, plus a translation that only exists on the **fork/parent** compact path: 1. Desktop `visibleUserOrdinal` (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions`) counts `role === 'user' && !hidden` over the renderer list. After in-place compact, Desktop keeps the pre-compact bubbles (`includeCompacted` in `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts`; `compactedTurnRef` in `use-message-stream` skips a post-compact reload). The compaction handoff is hidden in the UI but is still a `role=user` row without `hidden` / without `display_kind`. 2. Gateway `_history_user_indices` / `_reconcile_client_ordinal` (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py`) count the **tip** only: `role == "user" and not display_kind`. In-place compact does not create a parent and does not fill `display_history_prefix` (`get_ancestor_display_prefix` is empty when there is no parent). 3. #87563 accepts `tip_ordinal + prefix_user_count` as agreement. That count is taken from `display_history_prefix`. On in-place that list is empty → `prefix_user_count=0` → any display-vs-tip disagreement is treated as #82756 drift → 4030. 4. #82756 / #82959 / #83785 correctly refuse when ordinal and row_id disagree. The check is right; the client should not ship a display-space ordinal next to a durable id. Gateway already supports the safe shape: `client_ordinal is None` + resolved `truncate_before_row_id` aims the cut by id. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Smallest: when `truncate_before_row_id` or a real durable `truncate_before_message_id` is present, **omit** `truncate_before_user_ordinal`. Keep 4030 as a real-conflict guard. Do **not** ignore a mismatched ordinal on the gateway when a row_id resolves (#82756). #88092 is the same idea gated on tail-only prefetch. This case needs the rule whenever a durable address exists, including a complete live transcript after in-place compact. Optional later (not required to unblock Restore): make in-place populate `display_history_prefix` so the #87563 translation applies. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? Open to but I do think the fix is only a workaround so I am open for real fix instead

signals.title: [Bug]: shared primary profile routes reload session history from the root store after #88734
signals.text: ## Bug Description A shared primary messaging adapter routed to a secondary profile under `gateway.multiplex_profiles` creates a split session after the scope-aware DB fix from #88734: - gateway routing/session metadata is read from the root/default `state.db`; - the routed `AIAgent` persists the real transcript to the secondary profile's `state.db`; - every following turn reloads an empty history from the root store, so the bot has same-session amnesia. This reproduces on current `main` (`e02d1e41fc`) with the default profile owning one WhatsApp/Baileys connection and an exact `gateway.profile_routes` rule routing a group to a secondary profile whose own WhatsApp adapter is disabled. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Enable `gateway.multiplex_profiles` on the default gateway. 2. Let the default profile own a shared primary WhatsApp adapter. 3. Add an exact `profile_routes` entry mapping one WhatsApp group to a served secondary profile. 4. Send a first message that causes several tool calls and a final response. 5. Reply in the same group with a follow-up that depends on the prior turn. 6. Inspect `agent.log` and both SQLite stores. Observed log shape on every follow-up: ```text Agent cache invalidated ... message_count changed (1 -> N), possible cross-process write conversation turn: session=<same-id> ... history=0 ``` For the same session id, the root store contained one metadata row while the secondary profile store contained the full transcript (64 rows in the live reproduction). No compression ran or failed. ## Expected Behavior After route resolution and authorization, session creation, transcript loading, turn leases, and agent persistence should all resolve the same secondary-profile store. A follow-up turn should receive the prior conversation history. The primary adapter's owner-scoped authorization/secret gate should remain under the default profile; only the routed conversation/session lifecycle should enter the target profile scope. ## Actual Behavior The first routed turn answers correctly because `_run_agent()` enters the secondary profile scope. The next turn calls `async_session_store.load_transcript()` while the shared primary handler is still pinned to the default profile, returns no replayable messages, and passes `conversation_history=[]` to the agent. A representative conversation became: ```text assistant: [returns the requested account] user: activate that account with the quarterly plan assistant: several accounts match; which exact one? user: [exact account name] assistant: what do you need for that account? ``` The last response occurred because the model only received the current message and quoted reply, not the preceding activation request. ## Affected Component Gateway (WhatsApp), Agent Core session history, multi-profile routing. ## Messaging Platform WhatsApp (the bug shape applies to any shared primary adapter using `profile_routes`). ## Debug Report A public debug upload is intentionally omitted because the live logs and transcript contain private business/account data. The reproduction evidence was collected locally from `agent.log`, `gateway.log`, and both SQLite stores, with identifiers redacted above. A hermetic regression test against temporary profile homes will accompany the PR. ## Operating System macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) ## Python Version Python 3.11.15 ## Hermes Version Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), current main `e02d1e41fc` ## Root Cause Analysis #88734 correctly changed `SessionStore._db` and `GatewayRunner._session_db` to resolve the active `HERMES_HOME` scope per access. Its invariant is sound, but the shared-primary route reaches the profile scope too late: 1. `_make_default_profile_message_handler()` intentionally pins the whole ingress/auth path to the default home (introduced by `76cf19fee1` so the primary adapter's token and prompt gate remain owner-scoped). 2. `_handle_message()` resolves/stamps `source.profile`, then calls `_handle_message_with_agent()` while still in that default scope. 3. `_handle_message_with_agent()` calls `get_or_create_session()` and `load_transcript()` before `_run_agent()`. 4. `_run_agent()` is the first point that enters `_profile_runtime_scope(_resolve_profile_home_for_source(source))`. 5. Therefore the gateway-side session lifecycle reads/writes root, while `AIAgent` writes the transcript to the routed profile. The existing `test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py` tests direct access inside an already-active profile override. It does not cover the shared-primary adapter path where the active scope remains default until the agent call. ## Proposed Fix Add a routed-profile wrapper around `_handle_message_with_agent()` (after ingress authorization and route stamping, before any session-store access), keeping its current implementation in an inner method. This scopes the complete session lifecycle without moving primary-adapter authorization/secret checks out of the owner profile. Add regression coverage that: - starts from the default/root scope; - routes a source to a secondary profile; - proves the session/runner DB handles seen by the inner turn are the secondary profile's handles; - proves the test fails with the wrapper removed; - keeps multiplex-off and primary/default routing behavior unchanged. ## Related Work / Duplicate Sweep - #88532 / #88734 fixed frozen-at-init DB handles and established physical per-profile stores. - #66887 tracks the broader historical storage-scope problem. - #69042 originally explored shared-WhatsApp profile isolation but narrowed to adapter startup only. - No open PR found for this post-#88734 residual shared-primary history-loading seam. ## PR - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR.
signals.author: cpena28

signals.title: [Feature]: Tracking: add a read-only hierarchical Roadmap projection to Kanban
signals.text: ## Problem or Use Case Kanban operators can inspect execution one board at a time, but cannot see a compact, evidence-backed rollup of how authorized work relates across scopes, what dependency is critical, or which decision is next. For example, an operator overseeing several projects should be able to move from a portfolio summary to the blocked task and its evidence without introducing another scheduler or source of truth. This is adjacent to #88571's compact Kanban information architecture, not a replacement or duplicate: that issue improves the existing board; this issue tracks an optional hierarchical Roadmap projection over it. ## Proposed Solution Add an optional `Board | Roadmap` view to the existing Kanban API and its Desktop/WebUI clients. ### Authority and minimal scope - Kanban tasks, dependencies, runs, reviews, and events remain the execution ledger and scheduler. - Roadmap is a read projection only. It cannot create, schedule, approve, close, or redefine work. - Add optional stable scope entities with parent references. The supported vocabulary is `company → portfolio → workstream (client | product | experiment) → project → epic → sprint → board`; task/subtask remain existing Kanban tasks. - Levels may be omitted. Scope ancestry never gates dispatch, and task dependencies remain in the existing dependency graph. - Extend the existing Kanban plugin API rather than adding a service or standalone app. Desktop and standalone WebUI consume one versioned contract and fixture corpus while adapting layout per surface. ### Compatibility Existing `project_id`, `tenant`, board identity, task links, and unscoped tasks continue to work. Scope metadata and task/board bindings are nullable and additive. When metadata is absent, existing APIs and board behavior remain unchanged; legacy project/board/tenant values may be projected through documented read-only fallback precedence without rewriting task rows. An unavailable scope catalog must not damage or hide task/run/event truth. ### Deterministic progression - Status, health, critical path, blockers, and momentum are computed from authorized visible records and expose their raw components, freshness, and provenance. - Verified outcomes are deduplicated by stable task revision/evidence/event identity. Creation volume, tool calls, runtime, agent count, and raw done-card count score zero. - Momentum may use a documented time window and decay formula, but must never rank agents or scopes. - Dependency cycles, partial reads, stale data, unauthorized scopes, empty scopes, and unavailable external maturity/evidence authorities fail closed and remain visibly distinct. - Achievements, if rendered, require versioned definitions and structured evidence references. No prose matching, blind increments, leaderboard, XP economy, streak pressure, or reuse of activity-volume achievement state as authority. - Optional generated narrative is default-off, provenance-labelled, and presentation-only; it cannot write task, metric, evidence, or approval state. ### Responsive interaction Use one compact, summary-first hierarchy at every width. Wider viewports add comparative columns, an aligned timeline, and a selected-evidence detail pane rather than inflating cards. Narrow viewports retain the same-density list and open context in a drawer/sheet. Roadmap rows and evidence links should return to a removable Board filter. Preserve 44px touch targets, visible focus, semantic names, reduced motion, Back/Escape dismissal with focus return, and no page-level horizontal overflow. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Fresh and upgraded board fixtures preserve existing unscoped behavior with no automatic row rewrite. - [ ] Invalid parent order, cycles, dangling references, and concurrent first-open migration are deterministic and fail closed. - [ ] Board/profile authorization is applied before aggregation; hidden sibling boards affect neither counts nor denominators, and unauthorized scope lookup does not leak existence. - [ ] Rollups expose source revision/event IDs, freshness, warnings, raw metric components, and deterministic replay/idempotency behavior. - [ ] Outcome deduplication, zero-volume scoring, decay/window boundaries, negative rework, dependency ties/cycles, empty/partial/stale states, and evidence-gated achievements have focused tests. - [ ] Existing board create/patch, `/board`, events WebSocket, CLI, dispatcher, and worker flows pass unchanged when scope capability is absent. - [ ] Desktop and standalone WebUI share contract fixtures and state/action semantics; capability mismatch degrades to Board without data mutation. - [ ] Interaction and overflow evidence covers 320, 360, 390, 430, and 1280px, including hierarchy navigation, timeline/detail enhancement, contextual sheet, keyboard/touch paths, Back/Escape focus return, stale/error retry, and non-empty seeded data. - [ ] The projection batches by authorized board rather than task (no N+1 task reads) and remains responsive on a documented large fixture. Suggested implementation slices: 1. Versioned scope/projection contract, additive compatibility layer, canonical authorization/aggregation, and thin API adapter. 2. Desktop and WebUI adapters sharing contract fixtures and semantics. 3. Optional reporting only if separately justified after the deterministic projection is useful. ## Alternatives Considered - Reusing task dependencies for hierarchy conflates context with execution gating. - Encoding hierarchy in tenant strings, project records, or every board's metadata lacks stable shared ancestry or creates divergent copies. - A second roadmap task/event ledger risks conflicting lifecycle truth. - Reusing activity-based achievement state rewards volume without evidence. - An LLM-first summary is non-deterministic and cannot safely own progress or approval. ## Non-goals - No second ledger, scheduler, nested dispatcher, or duplicate task table. - No mandatory hierarchy, automatic migration, or hierarchy inferred from names, paths, tenants, or dependencies. - No replacement of Projects, boards, tenants, dependencies, workflows, or the existing achievements dashboard. - No worker competition, leaderboards, arbitrary XP, streaks, confetti, or generated-prose mutation. - No broad Kanban redesign beyond the compact Roadmap controls; #88571 remains the board IA predecessor. - No standalone app or new service. ## Feature Type Other ## Scope Large (new module or significant refactor) ## Contribution - [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: [Bug] Desktop: re-opening the already-focused session from the Bots panel hangs forever (never times out)
signals.text: # [Bug] Desktop: re-opening the already-focused session from the Bots panel hangs forever (never even times out) ## Summary Clicking a session row in the Bots panel freezes the pane with no error and no recovery when the target session is the one **already focused on the main surface**. It does not fail — it never settles at all, so it does not even reach the 20s hydration timeout. For an actively-used profile this is the *common* case, not an edge case: the bot roster previews the profile's most recent session, which is exactly the session the user has open. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), desktop build 2026-08-18T22:24Z - Windows 11, local gateway, 4 local profiles (multiplex, Telegram) - Reproduced across app restarts and a full machine reboot ## Repro 1. Open a chat in profile `X` on the main surface and leave it focused. 2. Open the Bots panel and select agent `X` → its session list. 3. Click the row for that same session (it is the newest, so it is at the top). **Expected:** the conversation is shown (it is already open — a no-op is fine). **Actual:** the pane freezes indefinitely. No error toast, no Retry, no timeout. Gateway log for the click — connection accepted, never closed: ``` 20:15:54 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:50522 (no matching "ws closed" — the open never settles) ``` Contrast with a click that *does* fail (different pinned session, not focused), which reaches the timeout and surfaces the stranded-session UI: ``` 20:10:00 ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:58150 20:10:43 ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:58150 ← ~43s: hydration timeout path ``` ## Root cause `apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts` — `waitForFocusedSessionHydration()` resolves only from inside `check()`, and `check()` runs on atom **change**: ```ts unbinds.push($activeGatewayProfile.listen(check)) unbinds.push($selectedStoredSessionId.listen(check)) unbinds.push($activeSessionId.listen(check)) unbinds.push($messages.listen(check)) ``` These are **global** atoms (`store/session.ts:567`), so when the requested session is the focused one they already hold their target values. The initial `check()` at the end of the function does fire, but `openSession()` was called with `intent: 'main'` on a surface that is already in that exact state, so no atom transitions and no listener fires again. The awaited promise therefore never settles. The `setTimeout` that would reject it is armed, but the pane is already wedged by the in-flight open, so the user sees an indefinite freeze rather than the intended timeout → Retry surface. Callers: `plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js:7425` (`openProfileSession`) and `plugin.js:2993` (`openStoredBotChat`), both with `awaitHydration: true`. ## Fix Settle immediately when the requested open is already satisfied, before awaiting a transition that cannot happen. The guard uses the *same* four-part predicate as the hydration check, so a genuinely stale or blank surface still takes the resume path (i.e. it does not reintroduce #89206): ```ts if ( options.awaitHydration && normalizeProfileKey($activeGatewayProfile.get()) === targetProfile && $selectedStoredSessionId.get() === storedSessionId && Boolean($activeSessionId.get()) && (!expectHistory || $messages.get().length > 0) ) { return } ``` ## Verification - `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean. - `node --test src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/*.test.mjs` — 279/279 pass (276 before, plus 3 new). - New test `reopen-focused-session-hang.test.mjs` is sabotage-verified: 3/3 **fail** with the guard removed, 3/3 pass with it. - `npx vitest run --project ui` — 4866/4870 pass. The 4 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (locale thousands separators under pt-BR, e.g. `1.234.567` vs `1,234,567`); verified identical on a pristine checkout of the same commit. ## Related - #89206 (closed) — blank Bot Chat; same surface, opposite direction. The fix there added the hydration wait this bug hangs on. - #68594 — desktop profile switch resumes previous session.

signals.title: Desktop: profile switching hangs silently after atomically-published gateway switch refactor (Windows)
signals.text: ## Environment - Windows 11, Hermes Desktop (packaged, git install), v0.20.4 · upstream c69b6471e6 ## Symptom Clicking a profile in the sidebar rail (e.g. architect) does nothing: no UI change, no loading state, no error, and **no new WebSocket connection to the target backend** (netstat shows 0 ESTABLISHED on the pooled backend's port). Every subsequent profile click also fails — the app is stuck on the current profile until Desktop is restarted. ## Regression window Works on 86b2057a (2026-08-17). Broken after the "publish gateway/profile/connection atomically" series: - d57f94a330 publish gateway, profile, and connection descriptor atomically on a profile switch - 053eb7aab0 publish a gateway switch in one nanostores batch - 4e520f0850 guard the profile publication on its activation result too - (plus 20ccf88acd / d0e0951cf1 agent-side analogues) ## Evidence - All pooled backends boot fine: each profile's `serve` announces HERMES_BACKEND_READY and the port keeps LISTENING - Clicking the profile never dials the backend: target port has 0 ESTABLISHED connections (a working profile shows active WS connections) - Renderer console is silent — the failure is swallowed by the empty `.catch(() => {})` at the end of `ensureGatewayProfile` (store/profile.ts), which comments "the user can retry the switch" but the retry never works because `gatewaySwitch` is a module-global promise: once one switch hangs, every later `ensureGatewayProfile` awaits the same never-settling promise at the serialization point ## Suspected root cause `Promise.all([resolveConnectionForProfile(target), prepareGatewayForProfile(target)])` never settles (or `activate()` returns false on an epoch mismatch) and the rejection/hang is swallowed, leaving `gatewaySwitch` permanently pending. The new "rejected activation publishes NOTHING" guard (4e520f08) turns a failed/busy activation into a silent no-op with no retry path. Happy to run any diagnostic or test a proposed fix on this Windows machine.

signals.title: [Windows] Hermes kills svchost.exe via stale-PID taskkill /F /PID → repeated 0xEF (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED) blue screens
signals.text: # [Windows] Hermes kills `svchost.exe` via stale-PID `taskkill /F /PID` → repeated 0xEF (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED) blue screens **Environment:** Windows 11 24H2 (build 10.0.26200.9168), Hermes Desktop (CI build 2026-08-18, commit 8a770aae0d550bb92eb021913bd102a61ccc40af), 32 GB RAM ## Summary On Windows, Hermes terminates processes with bare `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` without verifying that the PID currently belongs to the intended process. PIDs recorded before a reboot (persisted ownership files, stale `.pid` files, or **hardcoded PIDs in scripts**) are routinely recycled by Windows to unrelated processes — in our case repeatedly to `svchost.exe`. Killing a protected critical process triggers `bugcheck 0xEF (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED)`, i.e. a full blue screen. **Observed:** 8 identical BSODs in 48 hours, all `0x000000EF` with WER bucket `0xEF_svchost.exe_BUGCHECK_CRITICAL_PROCESS_TERMINATED_BY_taskkill.exe_1_svchost.exe!unknown_function`. ## Evidence ### 8 blue screens, all the same signature WER reports (`Microsoft-Windows-WER-SystemErrorReporting`, Event 1001): | Time | Bugcheck | WER bucket | |---|---|---| | 2026-08-17 16:48 | 0xEF | `0xEF_svchost.exe_BUGCHECK_CRITICAL_PROCESS_TERMINATED_BY_taskkill.exe...` | | 2026-08-17 16:54 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-17 18:47 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-17 23:30 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 07:18 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 16:11 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 16:42 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 17:19 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 17:23 | 0xEF | same | Every crash's `Response.BucketId` contains `BUGCHECK_CRITICAL_PROCESS_TERMINATED_BY_taskkill.exe` — Windows itself attributed the death of `svchost.exe` to a `taskkill.exe` invocation. Bugcheck params: Param1 = EPROCESS of the dying process, Param2/Param4 = 0. The crash that followed the desktop auto-update is particularly damning: the app was rebuilt at 17:16 (install-stamp / `app.asar` mtime), and the machine blue-screened at 17:19 and again at 17:23. ### Unsafe `taskkill /PID` call sites (no ownership verification) 1. **Desktop `forceKillProcessTree`** — `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` (and compiled `app.asar.unpacked/dist/electron-main.mjs`): ```ts function forceKillProcessTree(pid) { if (!IS_WINDOWS) return; if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return; try { execFileSync('taskkill', ['/PID', String(pid), '/T', '/F'], ...); } catch {} } ``` Called from `stopBackendChild(child)` / single-instance / orphan-backend cleanup paths. The PID can come from persisted state (`backend-ownership.json`, `gateway.pid`) recorded in a previous boot. 2. **Hardcoded stale PID in a restart script** — `gateway-service/restart_gateway.bat`: ```bat taskkill /F /PID 33796 ``` `33796` was the gateway's PID at some earlier point. It is long dead; Windows has since recycled that number. Any invocation of this script now kills whatever process currently owns PID 33796 — our system did not have 33796 assigned at inspection time, i.e. it is a loaded gun. 3. **Python-side kills** — `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py` (`kill_process_tree`), `hermes_cli/dashboard_procs.py` (`taskkill /PID <pid> /F`), `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` (`_stop_process_trees`: `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`) — same pattern, no check that the target is a Hermes process. ### Crash mechanism (reproduction) 1. During some run, a Hermes/gateway PID gets persisted (`gateway.pid`, `backend-ownership.json`) or hardcoded (`restart_gateway.bat`). 2. Machine reboots. Windows allocates PIDs sequentially; the stale PID is quickly handed to another process — with dozens of `svchost.exe` instances running, the recycled PID often *is* an `svchost.exe` (protected critical process). 3. On boot, Hermes Desktop starts (autostart / user launch), runs single-instance / orphan-backend cleanup → `forceKillProcessTree(<stale pid>)`. Or the gateway watchdog re-runs `restart_gateway.bat` → `taskkill /F /PID <stale>`. 4. `svchost.exe` is killed → kernel detects a critical process died → `bugcheck 0xEF` → BSOD. This matches the observed pattern: every crash occurred shortly after boot or right after an auto-update, when the desktop app starts and reconciles old process records. ### Why it escaped detection - Kernel dumps were written as full-memory dumps (`CrashDumpEnabled=0x3`, `PAGEDU64` header with `dumpfve.sys` filter), which generic minidump tooling can't parse locally — the WER bucket string was the reliable signal. - The failure is timing-dependent (PID reuse) and only fires during startup/update cleanup, so it's hard to reproduce on demand. - User-side patches applied on 2026-08-17 were silently wiped by the CI auto-update on 2026-08-18, and the machine blue-screened again 3 minutes later. ## Suggested fix 1. **Verify PID ownership before every `taskkill`.** On Windows, query `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>"` and only kill when `CommandLine`/`ExecutablePath` matches the expected Hermes process (path contains `hermes`, venv, `gateway run`, etc.). If the PID is missing or doesn't match, skip. This is the minimal, robust guard for all five call sites (and any future one). 2. **Never hardcode PIDs in scripts.** Use process discovery by command line (the existing `find_gateway_pids` / `kill_gateway.ps1` pattern) or a `.pid` file with a start-time fingerprint that is re-validated before use. 3. **Reuse the existing identity checks.** The codebase already has `startMarker` / `processIdentityMatches` / `backendIdentityMatches` guards for orphan-backend cleanup — route `forceKillProcessTree` through the same verification instead of its own bare path. A user-side hotfix implementing (1) and (2) for all five call sites is applied locally and has been verified (guard skips non-Hermes PIDs, including the stale `33796`); it can be shared as a reference patch if useful. ## Impact On affected Windows machines: repeated unannounced blue screens, potential data loss from unsaved work, and (for less lucky PID recycling) the possibility of killing other unrelated processes. Any Windows user who reboots frequently, uses the desktop app autostart, or triggers the update path is exposed to the same crash.
