signals.title: Telegram typing indicator reappears during genuinely idle windows in long-running sessions
signals.text: ## Bug Description The Telegram "typing…" indicator sticks/reappears intermittently even when the agent is completely idle (no active turn, no tool calls, no API calls in flight). It is not permanently stuck — it clears briefly during interactive prompts (e.g. while a `clarify` button is awaiting the user's tap) but reappears afterward with no corresponding agent activity in the logs. `/stop` does clear it once when invoked, confirming the underlying mechanism *can* be cleared, but it recurs on its own afterward without any new inbound message or agent activity. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Run a long-lived Telegram DM session with the agent (observed at ~300K+ tokens of conversation history, many prior turns). 2. Have a turn complete normally (final response delivered, confirmed via `gateway.run: response ready` log line). 3. Wait ~1-3 minutes with no further interaction. 4. Observe the Telegram chat header: the "typing…" indicator is visible despite zero agent activity in `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` during that window. 5. Sending `/stop` clears it for that instance, but it returns on a subsequent idle window. ## Expected Behavior Typing indicator should only be visible while the agent is actively processing a turn (API calls in flight, tool execution, or streaming a response), and should reliably clear the moment `gateway.run: response ready` fires — with no reappearance until a new inbound message starts a new turn. ## Actual Behavior Typing indicator reappears during idle windows with no corresponding log activity for the session. Suspected root cause candidates identified via static code review (not confirmed via live debugger attach): - `agent/turn_finalizer.py` spawns a background review thread (`_spawn_background_review`, comment: *"runs AFTER the response is delivered so it never competes with the user's task for model attention"*) that forks a new `AIAgent` and runs asynchronously in a separate thread named `bg-review`. This fork is invisible to the user (no visible response expected in the common case), but its execution window may overlap with the `run_generation`/typing-refresh bookkeeping in `gateway/run.py`, and if any refresh call outlives the true end of the visible turn, this could explain the observed reappearance. - The typing-refresh loop in `gateway/run.py` (`send_typing` calls around lines ~4727, ~4813, ~27151) is guarded by `ctx._run_still_current()` / `self._is_session_run_current(session_key, run_generation)`, which appears correctly designed to stop stale refreshes — but I was not able to fully trace whether the background-review thread's lifecycle is bound to the same `run_generation` token or has its own untracked typing calls. I want to flag explicitly: the above is code-reading analysis, not a confirmed root cause from a live repro with debugger attached. Happy to provide full session logs privately if that helps triage. ## Environment - Hermes Agent version: v0.20.2 (2026.8.16) - Platform: Telegram (DM) - Model: claude-sonnet-5, provider=anthropic - Session size at time of observation: ~296K-310K tokens, 400+ messages, long-running single session (not `/new`'d in a while) - Background review: enabled (default), triggered repeatedly during the session (visible in logs as `thread=bg-review`) - OS: macOS ## Additional context Log evidence (redacted chat id) showing idle gaps with no activity between a completed turn and the next inbound message, during which the indicator was reported stuck by the user: ``` 2026-08-19 07:57:17 INFO gateway.run: response ready: ... time=41.5s 2026-08-19 07:57:27 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Sending response (23 chars) ... 2026-08-19 07:58:12 INFO ... Cached user photo ... <- next inbound message, ~45s idle gap in between ``` User confirmed via live observation: indicator clears briefly *only* while an interactive `clarify` prompt is pending (user attention genuinely required, agent genuinely idle), then reappears once that resolves — even with zero subsequent inbound messages. Related to the documented "phantom is thinking" issue referenced in `gateway/slash_commands.py` (comment cites issue #32295) — that fix (`/stop` force-clearing on no-active-agent) does address a one-shot clear, but does not appear to prevent recurrence in a still-idle session.

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop Bot Mode times out loading session history when opening a Bot
signals.text: ## Bug Description Opening any Bot from the Hermes Desktop Bot Mode roster often fails with a session-history timeout. The error appears during the initial “waking up” flow: > Couldn't open the Bot's chat > Timed out loading the Bot profile's session history Clicking Retry usually opens the Bot successfully. This reproduces with newly created Bots, so it does not appear to be caused by a corrupted Bot Chat or a large conversation history. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Run Hermes Desktop on Windows 11. 2. Create a fresh Bot using Bot Mode. 3. Use a custom SOUL.md or a short role description. 4. Disable Composio MCP. 5. Leave the Bot's default canonical `Bot Chat` session. 6. Close and reopen Hermes Desktop. 7. Click the Bot in the Bots roster. 8. Observe the session-history timeout. 9. Click Retry. 10. The Bot opens successfully. ## Expected Behavior Clicking a Bot should open its canonical `Bot Chat` directly after the Bot backend becomes ready. A temporary profile-backend wake-up delay should be retried internally and should not surface as a session-history error to the user. ## Actual Behavior The Desktop Bot Mode UI times out while loading the Bot profile's session history. Retry usually succeeds. ## Evidence - The issue reproduces with more than one newly created Bot. - Composio MCP was disabled, but the issue remained. - The Bot profile's state database contained only 1 session and 4 messages. - The same canonical Bot Chat opened successfully through the CLI: `hermes -p hongsam chat --in C:/Users/hyj53 -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q` - The CLI returned `HONGSAM_BACKEND_OK`. - This indicates that the Bot profile, model authentication, session database, and canonical session are valid. - The failure appears specific to the Desktop Bot Mode open/resume path. ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 - Hermes version: 0.20.4 - Surface: Hermes Desktop - Feature: Bot Mode - Provider: openai-codex - Model: gpt-5.6-luna - Bot profile: hongsam - MCP: Composio disabled ## Related Issues Possibly related to #88146, but the current problem reproduces with fresh Bots and presents specifically as a session-history loading timeout. ## Additional Investigation The local Bot Mode plugin's `openBotCanonicalChat` path was tested with a local patch that attempts to open the stored canonical session directly before calling `session.list`. The timeout behavior was still observed after creating a fresh Bot, suggesting this may involve the Desktop plugin/runtime version or profile-backend prewarm path rather than only the session-list fallback logic.

signals.title: [Bug]: Fresh install.sh aborts - git clone fails with HTTP 429 (packfile throttled for this repo)
signals.text: ## Human disclosure This bug report was logged by Opus 5 after fixing this specific issue for me for the current 1 line install script as of 2026-08-19 After the fix it applied things worked. I read the report and it makes sense, if you send this to an agent they should be able to reproduce and fix this issue. I also instructed my agent to check for duplicates and didn't find any when looking manually. Please forgive me I don't have time to write this by hand and I hope this is still useful. --- ### Bug Description Running the documented installer one-liner on a clean macOS machine fails at the **Download Hermes Agent** stage. Both the SSH and HTTPS clone paths fail, `install.sh` exits 1, and no usable install is produced (`~/.hermes` is left with `bin/`, `skills/`, `config.yaml` but no `hermes-agent` checkout). ``` → Installing to /Users/madda/.hermes/hermes-agent... → Trying SSH clone... → SSH failed, trying HTTPS... Cloning into '/Users/madda/.hermes/hermes-agent'... error: RPC failed; HTTP 429 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 429 fatal: expected 'packfile' ✗ Failed to clone repository ``` **This is not a client-side IP rate limit.** At the same moment: - an anonymous `git clone` of a small public repo (`octocat/Hello-World`) succeeded normally, and - `https://api.github.com/rate_limit` reported `core: 60/60 remaining`. So GitHub appears to be throttling *packfile generation for this specific repo*, which is large — 9,644 files at HEAD, plus the "thousands of auto-generated branches" that `install.sh`'s own comments call out. The single `git clone --depth 1` the installer issues asks the server to build one big pack in one shot, which is exactly the expensive operation being throttled. Related: #89287 reports the same HTTP 429 against the `hermes update` path. This report is about the **fresh-install `clone_repo()` path in `install.sh`**, which has no retry and no fallback. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Start on a machine with no existing `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` checkout, no GitHub SSH key, and no valid GitHub credentials. 2. Run the documented installer: `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash` 3. Installer passes prerequisites and reaches the "Download Hermes Agent" stage. 4. SSH clone fails fast (no key registered). 5. HTTPS fallback fails with `RPC failed; HTTP 429`. 6. Installer prints `✗ Failed to clone repository` and exits. Reproduced consistently on repeated attempts over several minutes. ### Expected Behavior `install.sh` completes the clone — or degrades gracefully by retrying with backoff and/or falling back to a cheaper clone strategy — so a fresh install succeeds on an ordinary unauthenticated machine. ### Actual Behavior `git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git` dies mid-packfile with HTTP 429, `clone_repo()` hits its `log_error "Failed to clone repository"` branch and `exit 1`s. Nothing is installed. ### Workaround that did work Staging the clone so the server never builds one large packfile: ```bash git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --filter=blob:none \ https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git ~/.hermes/hermes-agent cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent git reset --hard HEAD # materializes blobs; may need one retry ``` Then re-running `install.sh` takes the "Existing installation found, updating..." branch and proceeds normally. The follow-up incremental `git fetch origin main` completes in seconds — only the initial bulk clone is throttled. ### Suggested fixes 1. **Retry the clone with exponential backoff on 429.** #88475 already added retry for downloading the install script itself; the clone deserves the same treatment. 2. **Use `--filter=blob:none --single-branch` for the initial clone**, then materialize the tree. Much cheaper server-side, and it is what got past the throttle here. 3. **Make the ZIP/tarball fallback first-class**, as already proposed in #39529. ### Two smaller things noticed while working around this - **An invalid `gh` token makes the failure opaque.** git here is configured with `credential.https://github.com.helper = !gh auth git-credential`. With an expired token, every clone additionally emits `fatal: failed to store: 100001` next to the 429, which sends you chasing the wrong problem. Worth surfacing in `install.sh` / `hermes doctor`. - **The repo has a macOS case-collision.** `git ls-files` shows both `contributors/emails/agent@Agents-Mac-mini.local` and `contributors/emails/agent@agents-Mac-mini.local`. On a case-insensitive filesystem only one can exist, so `git status` is permanently dirty and `install.sh`'s update path stashes on every single run. ### Affected Component Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Setup / Installation ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell Not available — `hermes debug share` cannot be run because the install itself is what fails, so there is no hermes binary, venv, or log directory on this machine. ``` ### Operating System macOS 27.0 (build 26A5406e), Apple Silicon / arm64 ### Python Version 3.11.13 (installer-detected); system python3 is 3.14.6 ### Hermes Version n/a - install never completed ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.text: ## Bug In Bot Mode (desktop app with multiple bot profiles), the Routines (cron jobs) pane always shows the **default profile's** cron jobs regardless of which bot is selected in the roster. ## Setup - 7 profiles configured as bots via `ui_meta.hermes-bots` in `profile.yaml` - 4 bot profiles (blog-writer, apk-dev, ops, research) have their own launchd gateways with `HERMES_HOME` pointing to their profile directory - Each bot profile has cron jobs in its own `cron/jobs.json` - The default profile (Rowan) has 14 cron jobs; bot profiles have 1-2 each - All gateways running and reachable ## Expected behavior When clicking **Blog Writer** in the bot roster, the Routines pane should show Blog Writer's cron jobs (1 job: "Weekly Real Estate Blog Post"). ## Actual behavior The Routines pane always shows the default profile's 14 cron jobs, no matter which bot is selected. Sending a message to the bot (which connects to the bot's gateway does not fix it either. ## Root cause In (plugin.js, line ~7232): (the active gateway connection profile) takes precedence over (the bot the user clicked). When the user clicks a bot in the roster, updates to blog-writer but remains default because the chat connection is still routed through the default profile's gateway. This means is called with , so sends with no param, and the gateway returns the default profile's cron store. Even if the desktop connects to the bot's gateway (after sending a message), may still report default if the connection routing doesn't fully switch. ## Suggested fix The Routines pane should use (the bot the user clicked) for the cron query, not . The cron RPC already supports profile scoping via and the gateway honors it by setting override. The Routines pane just isn't passing the right profile. Option A (minimal): Option B (correct): The Routines pane should always use the selected bot for cron scoping, since cron jobs live in the profile's regardless of which gateway the chat is connected to. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop app (Electron) - macOS 26.6.2 - 7 bot profiles, 4 with launchd gateways - All profiles on Ollama Cloud provider BODY )

signals.title: [Feature] Smart web search routing with result cleaning/ranking + link click → external browser by default
signals.text: ## Summary Two related feature requests to improve web search UX and link navigation in Hermes Desktop. --- ## Feature 1: Smart Web Search Backend Routing with Result Cleaning & Ranking ### Current Behavior `web.backend` accepts only a **single** backend. Users must manually switch via `hermes tools` or UI when: - A backend's quota is exhausted (e.g., Tavily 1000/month limit hit) - Chinese-language queries return poor results from English-optimized backends - Network conditions make a backend temporarily unreachable (e.g., DuckDuckGo/Brave blocked in China) Issue #32159 requests ordered failover chains, but goes only halfway — it handles failure recovery, not intelligent routing. ### Proposed Behavior **Smart routing** that selects the best backend per-query based on: | Signal | Example | |--------|---------| | Query language | Chinese query → prefer Bocha/Tavily; English query → prefer Exa/Brave | | Backend health | Quota remaining, recent error rate, avg latency | | Network reachability | Auto-detect if backend is reachable from user's region | | Capability match | Need content extraction? → skip search-only backends (Brave, DDG, xAI) | **Result cleaning & ranking** after aggregation: - Deduplicate results across backends (same URL from Tavily + Exa = one entry) - Re-rank by relevance score, source authority, freshness - Clean snippets (remove tracking params, trim to meaningful text) - Return a unified, ranked result list regardless of which backend(s) were used This saves users: - **Token cost** — cleaner, deduped results = less noise fed to LLM - **Reading effort** — ranked results put the best answer first - **Manual switching** — no more UI dropdown toggling when quota runs out ### Config Surface (proposed) ```yaml web: search_backends: [tavily, exa, firecrawl] # ordered preference routing: auto: true # enable smart routing language_match: true # prefer backends matching query language health_check: true # skip unhealthy backends automatically results: deduplicate: true # merge same-URL results re_rank: true # relevance-based re-ranking max_snippet_length: 200 # trim long snippets ``` Backwards compatible: if `search_backends` is absent, fall back to existing single `backend` / auto-detect behavior. --- ## Feature 2: Link Click Behavior — Default to External Browser, Modifier for In-App Preview ### Current Behavior Source code analysis (v0.20.4) shows inconsistent link click behavior: - **Chat message links** (`artifacts/index.tsx`): click → `openExternal()` → system browser ✅ - **Tool result preview rows** (`preview-row.tsx`): plain click → in-app preview pane; Ctrl/Cmd+click → also in-app preview - **Search result cards**: open in preview pane, not in system browser Users who want to continue browsing in their own browser (with their cookies, logins, extensions) must manually copy URLs. ### Proposed Behavior Swap the modifier logic for tool result / search result links: | Action | Current | Proposed | |--------|---------|----------| | Plain click | In-app preview pane | **External browser** (system default, with user's cookies/sessions) | | Ctrl/Cmd + click | In-app preview pane | **In-app preview pane** | Rationale: - Most users want to **continue browsing** in their own browser where they're logged in - In-app preview pane is a **read-only webview** with separate cookies — not suitable for login flows, downloads, or interactive sites - The modifier (Ctrl/Cmd) is the standard pattern for "open in background/alternative" across browsers and IDEs - Zero config change needed — just swap the condition in `preview-row.tsx`'s `onActivate` handler ### Implementation In `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/preview-row.tsx`, swap the click logic: ```tsx // BEFORE (current): onActivate={event => { if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) { void togglePreview() // modifier → in-app preview } else { void openDefaultTarget() // plain click → also in-app preview (via openPreview) } }} // AFTER (proposed): onActivate={event => { if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) { void togglePreview() // modifier → in-app preview (power user) } else { void openExternal() // plain click → external browser (user's Chrome with cookies) } }} ``` --- ## Environment - Hermes Desktop v0.20.4 - Windows 11 - Multiple search backends configured (Tavily + Exa + Firecrawl) ## Related - #32159 — Ordered failover chains for web search/extract backends (this issue's Feature 1 is a superset) - #36838 — Web search automatic fallback (not merged) - #53149 — Add Bocha/Baidu/Serper search providers (not merged)

signals.title: [Windows] Smart App Control blocks unsigned Python DLL (_sqlite3.pyd) → Hermes backend fails to start
signals.text: Environment: Windows 11 24H2 (build 10.0.26200.9168), Hermes Desktop (CI build 2026-08-18, commit 8a770aae0d550bb92eb021913bd102a61ccc40af), Smart App Control enabled ## Summary With Windows Smart App Control (SAC) enabled, the Hermes Desktop backend cannot start: Python's _sqlite3.pyd (an unsigned DLL) is blocked by SAC, the backend exits before it becomes ready, and the desktop app shows "Hermes couldn't start" with no usable recovery. ## Symptoms Desktop shows: Hermes couldn't start The background gateway didn't come up. Error invoking remote method 'hermes:connection': Error: Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1). Backend log (desktop.log): ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _sqlite3: 应用程序控制策略已阻止此文件。 (application control policy blocked this file) ## Root cause 1. Hermes Desktop's backend runs a bundled Python (uv-managed cpython-3.11 + venv). Its C-extension DLLs — e.g. DLLs/_sqlite3.pyd — carry no Authenticode signature (verified: Get-AuthenticodeSignature → NotSigned). 2. Smart App Control, when On, enforces reputation-based code integrity: unsigned binaries with no cloud reputation are blocked, and no exception list is available (unlike Defender exclusions). 3. _sqlite3 is imported by the stdlib at backend startup, so the backend aborts immediately. ## Why it appears "suddenly" SAC typically starts in evaluation mode, which learns over a period and then auto-enables itself (or disables itself) when the evaluation period ends. The file in question existed unchanged for weeks (installed 2026-08-02) and loaded fine during evaluation mode; after SAC auto-enabled, the same file is blocked on the next backend launch. This is not a Hermes regression — it is SAC switching to strict enforcement. ## Impact Any Windows 11 user with SAC enabled cannot run Hermes Desktop at all (backend will not start). Since SAC cannot be disabled and re-enabled freely (once turned off it cannot be turned back on without resetting Windows), affected users are forced to choose between SAC protection and Hermes. ## Suggested fix 1. Sign the Windows components (the bundled Python interpreter, venv, and all .pyd DLLs) with a code-signing certificate so they pass SAC's trust checks. This is the proper fix and benefits all SAC users. 2. If signing is not feasible short-term, document the incompatibility in the Windows install instructions (e.g. "Smart App Control must be off; it has no allowlist") so users aren't surprised by a broken first launch. 3. Consider bundling a signed Python distribution (e.g. python.org installer-based CPython, whose binaries are signed) instead of the current unsigned uv-managed interpreter. ## Verification performed - Get-AuthenticodeSignature <python>/DLLs/_sqlite3.pyd → Status: NotSigned - Hermes backend starts normally as soon as SAC is turned off; fails consistently when SAC is on.

signals.title: vision_analyze: support public-image (URL) mode for providers that reject base64 inline images (e.g. SenseNova)
signals.text: ## Summary `vision_analyze` cannot recognize images when the vision provider only accepts public HTTP(S) image URLs (e.g. SenseNova 商汤). The tool always encodes local images to `data:image/png;base64,...` before sending, which SenseNova 6.8 rejects with `400 image download failed`. ## Root Cause In `agent/image_routing.py`, `_file_to_data_url()` always base64-encodes a local image into an inline data URL. The auxiliary vision path (`auxiliary_client.py`) forwards that data URL to the provider. Providers like SenseNova 6.8 / U1 Fast do **not** accept base64 inline images — they only accept a publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL and return: ``` {"error": {"message": "image download failed", "type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "3"}} ``` Direct curl to SenseNova with a public URL image succeeds in ~2s; the same image as a base64 data URL is rejected. ## Proposed Enhancement Add a **public-image mode** so an image input can be sent as an external URL when the provider supports it: 1. When the input to `vision_analyze` is already a public `http(s)://` image URL, pass it through as-is (do NOT base64-encode it). The main-agent path in `image_routing.build_native_content_parts` already supports `image_urls` passthrough — the auxiliary vision path does not. 2. Optionally, allow a config flag (e.g. `auxiliary.vision.public_url_only: true`) so providers that only accept URLs (SenseNova, etc.) can be used without a local ephemeral HTTP server. ## Environment - Hermes version: latest (tested 2026-08-19) - Vision provider: SenseNova 6.8 Flash Lite (`sensenova-6.8-flash-lite`) on `token.sensenova.cn` - OS: Windows 11

signals.title: [Bug]: Models analytics returns duplicate rows for identical model/provider pairs
signals.text: ### Bug Description The Dashboard Models page renders duplicate cards for the exact same `(model, provider)` pair. The duplication is already present in the `/api/analytics/models` response, so this is not only a frontend layout issue. In one profile, the page displayed five cards although the response reported only two distinct models: - `gpt-5.6-terra / openai-codex` appeared three times. - `gpt-5.4 / openai-codex` appeared twice. The duplicated cards had different `sessions` and `last_used_at` values. Adding the card-level session counts would give 13, while `totals.total_sessions` was 6. This appears related to #71778 because both affect `_get_models_analytics()` and the Models dashboard aggregation, but #71778 describes stale provider/token attribution after mid-session model switches rather than exact duplicate rows. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Use more than one model in sessions associated with a Hermes profile. The affected profile also uses the `openai-codex` provider and auxiliary tasks are left on automatic model selection. 2. Open `/models?profile=<profile>` with the 30-day window. 3. Observe repeated cards with the same rendered model and provider. 4. Request `GET /api/analytics/models?days=30&profile=<profile>` using the dashboard session normally. 5. Compare `totals.distinct_models` and `totals.total_sessions` with the returned `models` array. Minimal redacted response shape observed: ```json { "totals": { "distinct_models": 2, "total_sessions": 6 }, "models": [ {"model":"gpt-5.6-terra","provider":"openai-codex","sessions":4}, {"model":"gpt-5.4","provider":"openai-codex","sessions":2}, {"model":"gpt-5.6-terra","provider":"openai-codex","sessions":2}, {"model":"gpt-5.6-terra","provider":"openai-codex","sessions":3}, {"model":"gpt-5.4","provider":"openai-codex","sessions":2} ] } ``` No credentials, session identifiers, prompts, or message content are needed to reproduce the mismatch. ### Expected Behavior The API should return at most one aggregate row per exact `(model, provider)` pair for the selected profile and time window. The page should therefore render two unique cards in this example. Aggregate totals and per-model session counts should have documented, internally consistent semantics. ### Actual Behavior The API returns multiple rows with identical `model` and `provider` values, and the UI renders every row as a separate card. `totals.distinct_models` reports 2 while `models.length` is 5. The frontend also keys cards by `${model}:${provider}`, so duplicate API rows produce duplicate React keys as well as duplicate visible cards. ### Affected Component Other — Dashboard Models page and `/api/analytics/models`. ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (dashboard/API only). ### Debug Report ```shell Not uploaded because the issue is reproducible from the bounded, redacted API response above and a debug-share upload would disclose unrelated local configuration and logs. ``` ### Operating System macOS 26.5.2 ### Python Version Python 3.14.7 ### Hermes Version Dashboard status reports `0.20.1`; installation is based on release `v2026.8.18`. ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell No exception is emitted. The endpoint returns HTTP 200 with duplicate aggregate rows. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) The exact root cause has not been confirmed. The response shape suggests that independently aggregated usage rows (for example main and auxiliary/session-derived rows) may be concatenated without a final coalescing step by `(model, provider)`. The totals appear to be computed with distinct-model semantics, while the returned list preserves duplicate groups. This should be verified in `_get_models_analytics()` rather than assumed. ### Proposed Fix (optional) - Make the backend aggregation produce one canonical row per `(model, provider)` after all usage sources are combined. - Define whether `sessions` means distinct sessions per model or another count and compute it consistently. - Add a regression test asserting unique `(model, provider)` pairs and consistency between `distinct_models` and the model list. - Optionally guard in the frontend by detecting duplicate keys, but do not hide inconsistent backend totals by silently dropping rows. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
signals.author: aprudkin

signals.title: [Bug] Hermes Desktop reasoning pane dead for MiniMax-M3 (Plus subscription) — reasoning inline in content, never extracted to reasoning_content
signals.text:
## Bug Description On Hermes Agent v0.20.2 (current release as of 2026-08-16), the desktop model's reasoning pane is **not populated** when the model is `MiniMax-M3` served from `https://api.minimax.io/v1` via a first-class `providers:` entry using an API key. The reasoning is happening — it's just inlined into `message.content` as a literal `<think>…</think>` block and rendered as part of the visible assistant reply, with no visual separation and no way to collapse/hide it via the reasoning-pane toggle on the bubble. This is a **stale-but-still-reproducing** confirmation of #43827 (filed 2026-06-10 against v0.16.0) and a related report to #43836 (PR that proposed the fix, **closed without merge** — `mergedAt: null`). I'm filing a separate issue because: 1. The original #43827 was filed against v0.16.0; this is reproducible on the current release (v0.20.2) and on `origin/main` (verified 2026-08-19, after 4 commits past v0.20.2). 2. The original report described the symptom as a "leak"; the more accurate framing for the desktop app is "**reasoning field is never populated**, so the pane is dead." That's a different user-visible bug even though the root cause overlaps. 3. The proposed fix in #43836 (Chinese-tag filter addition) addresses part of the symptom (preventing raw reasoning from reaching the visible text on M3 generations that emit Chinese tags) but does **not** address the structured-field extraction the desktop pane needs. The desktop reasoning pane will remain non-functional even with #43836 merged, because the API never returns a `reasoning_content` field — the reasoning has to be *extracted* from the streaming content into a structured field by the Hermes client. Filing as a **new** issue (per user's one-time explicit override of the usual "comment on existing, don't file duplicate" guidance) so the report gets a fresh `updated_at` and cross-link visibility against both #43827 and #43836. ## Environment - **Hermes Agent:** v0.20.2 (`df4b65147d`, 2026-08-16) — also confirmed on `origin/main` (4 commits ahead as of 2026-08-19) - **Profile:** `tech-officer` - **Host:** macOS 26.5.2, Apple Silicon - **Provider config:** ```yaml # config.yaml providers: minimax: name: MiniMax (Plus subscription) base_url: https://api.minimax.io/v1 api_key: ${MINIMAX_API_KEY} discover_models: true ``` - **Model:** `MiniMax-M3` (Plus Token Plan subscription, served from `https://api.minimax.io/v1`) - **Surface affected:** Hermes Desktop reasoning pane (right-edge bubble toggle, `display.show_reasoning: true`) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure the `minimax` provider as above with a valid `MINIMAX_API_KEY` (the MiniMax Plus Token Plan subscription key works as an API key against `https://api.minimax.io/v1`). 2. Open Hermes Desktop, select `MiniMax (Plus subscription)` / `MiniMax-M3` from the model pulldown. 3. Confirm `display.show_reasoning: true` in `config.yaml` (default). 4. Send any prompt that triggers reasoning — e.g. `"What is 17 * 24? Think step by step."` 5. Observe the assistant's response in the chat bubble. 6. Click the reasoning-pane toggle on the right edge of the bubble. Observe: nothing happens. The toggle is dead. 7. Observe the visible content: it begins with a literal `<think>…</think>` block, embedded inline, that the user has to scroll past to see the actual answer. ## Expected Behavior The reasoning tokens should be: 1. **Extracted from the streaming content** into a structured field (e.g. `message.reasoning_content` or an OpenAI-format `reasoning` field) at the Hermes client layer. 2. **Displayed in the desktop reasoning pane** (the collapsible section that appears when `display.show_reasoning: true`). 3. **Stripped from the visible `content`** so the user only sees the post-reasoning answer. 4. **Counted separately** in `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` so users on a Plus subscription can see what their quota is being spent on. ## Actual Behavior The reasoning tokens appear inline at the start of `content` as a literal `<think>…</think>` block, with no separation, no extraction, and no accounting. ## Direct API Reproduction ```bash curl -sS -X POST https://api.minimax.io/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MINIMAX_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "MiniMax-M3", "max_tokens": 200, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 * 24? Think step by step."}] }' ``` Returns (relevant fields): ```json { "choices": [{ "finish_reason": "length", "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "<think>The user is asking for a simple multiplication: 17 × 24…
…408

Let " } }], "usage": { "total_tokens": 389, "prompt_tokens": 189, "completion_tokens": 200, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 128} } } ``` - `message` keys: `["content", "role"]` — **no `reasoning_content` field at all** - `content` begins with a literal `<think>` block containing the chain-of-thought - `usage` has no `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` — the 200 completion tokens billed include the inline reasoning, not separately accounted for - Same shape with `reasoning_effort: "high"` (only difference: `finish_reason: "stop"` because the response didn't hit the max_tokens cap; reasoning still inline in `content`) ## Root Cause The desktop reasoning pane is driven by a `message.reasoning_content` field on the OpenAI-format response stream. MiniMax-M3 does not emit that field — its reasoning is in `content` wrapped in literal `<think>` / `</think>` tags (and, in earlier M3 generations, the Chinese-tag family reported in #43827: `思考`, `反思`, `推理`, `推敲`). Hermes has no automatic extraction of inline-tag reasoning into the structured `reasoning_content` channel for this provider path. The `strip_think_blocks` function in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` does remove the tags from `content` for the English set, but: 1. The desktop reasoning pane needs the reasoning **available** as a structured field, not just stripped from the visible text. 2. Per #43827, the Chinese-tag family is not in the filter at all — so on M3 generations that emit those, the inline reasoning leaks through to the user entirely. ## Suggested Fix Two complementary changes: ### 1. Extract inline-tag reasoning into `reasoning_content` at the stream-consumer layer (provider-agnostic) The cleanest place is probably `gateway/stream_consumer.py` or the OpenAI-format adapter that wraps the streaming chunks. The shape would be: - As the stream accumulates, watch for the first `<think>` (or any registered inline-tag open) at a block boundary (start of stream or after a newline). - Once seen, accumulate the subsequent tokens into a `reasoning_content` accumulator instead of `content`. - When the matching close tag is seen, stop accumulating and emit the accumulated `reasoning_content` as a structured field on the assistant message. The post-close text continues to accumulate into `content`. - If the stream ends without a matching close, treat the entire unreleased remainder as reasoning. This is provider-agnostic and would also benefit GLM-5, Kimi K2.5, DeepSeek R1, Qwen3-thinking, and any other inline-thinking model. It does **not** require provider-specific configuration — the inline tag set can be a single shared constant. ### 2. Re-land #43836's filter additions (defense-in-depth) The four-file, +162/-2 patch in #43836 (adding `思考`, `反思`, `推理`, `推敲` to the three filter sites in `gateway/stream_consumer.py`, `cli.py`, and `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`) is the right shape. Even if step 1 lands first, this is a backstop that ensures raw reasoning never reaches the user. A regression test in `tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_chinese_think_tags.py` already exists from that PR branch — it should be carried over. ### Optional third change: surface a usage breakdown Compute `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` locally by counting the tokens that went into the extracted reasoning block. This is what Anthropic, OpenAI, and DeepSeek do at the API level; the MiniMax API doesn't break it out, but Hermes can compute it locally for any model that uses inline-tag thinking. Users on a Plus subscription quota would then see exactly what their monthly budget is being spent on. ## Workaround Living with the inline `<think>…</think>` block in the visible reply. The reasoning is happening; it's just not visually separated. Not a blocker, but a real UX papercut and a real correctness issue when the model switches to the Chinese-tag family (which then leaks raw). ## Related - #43827 — original bug report, filed against v0.16.0, still open - #43836 — proposed-fix PR, closed without merge (`mergedAt: null`) - #27288 — closed (`sweeper:implemented-on-main`), mixed-case English-tag fix (healthy path) - #17924 — closed, English-tag fix on CLI (the historical precedent for this class) 🤖 Generated with [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/)

signals.title: [Feature]: configurable default scope for /reasoning changes
signals.text: ### Problem or Use Case `/reasoning <level>` is intentionally session-scoped by default, while `/reasoning <level> --global` persists the value to `agent.reasoning_effort`. That default is safe and should remain unchanged for existing users. However, users who normally want every interactive reasoning-level change to become the new global default must remember to append `--global` each time. There is currently no configuration preference that changes the command's default scope. A one-time `/reasoning <level> --global` is sufficient when the preferred level is static. It does not cover workflows where the user frequently changes levels and expects each selection to persist across new CLI/TUI/Desktop/gateway sessions. This is distinct from the already implemented `--global` support discussed in #14617: the request is not to add `--global`, but to make persistence the configurable default while retaining an explicit session-only escape hatch. ### Proposed Solution Add an opt-in configuration option, for example: ```yaml agent: reasoning_command_scope: global # session (default) | global ``` Expected behavior: - Default remains `session` for backward compatibility. - With `reasoning_command_scope: global`, `/reasoning high` behaves like today's `/reasoning high --global` and persists `agent.reasoning_effort`. - `/reasoning high --session` always creates a session-only override, regardless of the configured default. - Explicit `--global` always persists, regardless of the configured default. - Bare `/reasoning` reports the effective command default scope so the behavior is discoverable. - The behavior is consistent across interactive CLI, Ink TUI/Desktop gateway RPC, and messaging gateway implementations. - `show`/`hide` and display-only commands keep their existing persistence semantics; this option controls effort-level changes only. A boolean such as `agent.reasoning_persist_by_default: true` would also work, but an enum leaves room for clearer validation and status output. ### Alternatives Considered 1. Continue requiring `--global` on every change. This works today but does not satisfy users who consistently prefer persistence and is easy to forget in pickers or frequent model-tuning workflows. 2. Change `/reasoning <level>` to global for everyone. Rejected because it would be a breaking behavioral change and could unexpectedly alter future sessions. 3. Use per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides`. Useful when levels are fixed per model, but not equivalent to making interactive changes persist by default. 4. Add a separate command such as `/reasoning-global`. This duplicates the existing command surface and is less composable than a default-scope preference plus explicit `--session`/`--global` flags. ### Feature Type Configuration option ### Scope Medium (few files, < 300 lines) ### Contribution A maintainer decision on the config key/name and cross-surface scope would be useful before implementation.

signals.title: cron: thread_id delivery diagnostic logs WARNING on correct configuration (20 jobs, 10-24/day)
signals.text: ### Summary `cron.scheduler` logs a `WARNING` whenever a cron job's `origin` is a thread but its `deliver` target is a plain channel. That is a valid, ordinary configuration — "run this job that I created in a thread, but post the result to a shared channel" — so the warning fires continuously on a correct setup. On one host it has fired every day since 2026-07-25, 10–24 times a day, across **20 distinct jobs**. ### Where `cron/scheduler.py`, in the per-target delivery loop. The block is explicitly labelled a diagnostic: ```python # Diagnostic: log thread_id for topic-aware delivery debugging origin = _resolve_origin(job) or {} origin_thread = origin.get("thread_id") if origin_thread and not thread_id: logger.warning( "Job '%s': origin has thread_id=%s but delivery target lost it " "(deliver=%s, target=%s)", job["id"], origin_thread, job.get("deliver", "local"), target, ) elif thread_id: logger.debug(...) ``` Observed on `v0.20.1` (`v2026.8.13`). Note this host runs a lightly patched build, so line numbers may not match upstream exactly; the block above is quoted verbatim. ### Why it looks like a false positive 1. **It gates nothing.** It is a bare `logger.warning` in a diagnostic block. Delivery proceeds to the configured target; `last_delivery_error` is `None` on every affected job. 2. **The condition is a normal configuration, not a fault.** A job created inside a Discord thread stamps `origin.thread_id`. Pointing `deliver` at a different channel is a deliberate fan-out. The message "delivery target lost it" reads as data loss, but nothing was lost — the target simply was never the origin lane. 3. **The one behaviour that is thread-sensitive is gated independently.** `_target_matches_origin()` correctly refuses to mirror into a non-origin lane, but `_cron_mirror_delivery_enabled()` already defaults to `False`, so on a default install the mirror is off regardless of `thread_id`. The warning implies a consequence that does not occur unless the operator opted into `cron.mirror_delivery` *and* the target genuinely is the origin chat. The practical cost is that a real thread-routing problem is indistinguishable from the steady-state noise, and `WARNING` on a healthy host trains operators to ignore the level. ### Suggested fix Either: - demote to `logger.debug`, matching the sibling `elif thread_id:` branch and the "Diagnostic" label; or - keep `WARNING` but narrow the predicate to the case that actually has a consequence — mirroring enabled **and** the target's `platform`/`chat_id` equal the origin's, with only `thread_id` missing. That is the genuine "same conversation, wrong lane" case; everything else is a broadcast. Happy to send a PR for either if you have a preference. ### Frequency data Daily counts of the warning on one host, `2026-07-25` through `2026-08-18`: 2, 4, 6, 4, 3, 2, 3, 3, 11, 9, 9, 10, 14, 17, 10, 14, 14, 24, 6, 13, 14, 17, 8, 21, 18.

signals.title: fix(qqbot): authorize approval clicks for dm session keys
signals.text: ## Problem PR #30737 added authorization checks for approval button clicks in QQBot, but the check hardcodes `chat_type == "c2c"` while C2C sessions are actually created with `chat_type="dm"` (`build_source` at L1278, L1488). This causes all DM approval buttons to be rejected as unauthorized: ``` WARNING [QQBot] Rejected unauthorized approval click for session agent:main:qqbot:dm:<user_id> (operator=<user_id>) ``` The agent waits for approval that never resolves, then times out after 300s. ## Root Cause The codebase has two parallel chat_type systems: - **Routing layer** (`_chat_type_map` / `_guess_chat_type`): uses `"c2c"` for QQ C2C - **Session layer** (`build_source(chat_type=...)`): uses `"dm"` for all direct messages The session key is built from the session layer, so it becomes `agent:main:qqbot:dm:<id>`. The authorization check used the routing layer semantics instead. ## Fix `_is_authorized_interaction_for_session` now accepts both `"c2c"` and `"dm"` for direct-message session keys, matching the actual chat_type used when creating C2C sessions. ## Testing Added `test_approval_click_dm_session_authorizes_owner` — verifies that a `dm`-typed session key with matching operator is accepted. Existing tests still pass (they use `c2c` in button_data which remains valid).

signals.title: fix(bedrock): inherit modalities from foundation models for inference profiles
signals.text: `discover_bedrock_models()` hardcodes inference profiles (`us.*`, `global.*`) to TEXT-only modalities. Foundation models report their real `inputModalities`/`outputModalities` from `ListFoundationModels`, but `ListInferenceProfiles` doesn't return that field, so the profile entries were just stamped with `["TEXT"]`. The practical effect: Claude profiles like `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` support IMAGE input, but they show up as text-only. Anything that filters models by vision capability in the `/model` picker silently drops them. ## Fix After foundation models are discovered, build a small `{model_id: modalities}` map. When walking the inference profiles, resolve each one back to its base foundation model and inherit those modalities: 1. Pull the model ID out of the profile's ARN (`arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/<id>`) 2. If there's no ARN, strip the regional prefix (`us.anthropic.claude-v2` -> `anthropic.claude-v2`) 3. If neither resolves, keep the TEXT-only default ## Tests Three new cases in `TestInferenceProfileModalityInheritance` -- ARN-based inheritance, the regional-prefix fallback, and the no-match default. Full `test_bedrock_adapter.py` passes (121 tests) on Python 3.11. Reported by @ptlally in #7920.

signals.title: feat(bedrock): support service_tier and performanceConfig for cost/latency control
signals.text: Bedrock's Converse API accepts `serviceTier` and `performanceConfig` as top-level request fields, but Hermes never passed them through. This means users who relied on `service_tier=flex` in OpenClaw (or other frameworks) lose that ~50% cost savings when they migrate to Hermes. ## What this adds Two new config keys under `bedrock:` in config.yaml: ```yaml bedrock: service_tier: flex # priority | default | flex | reserved latency: optimized # standard | optimized ``` Both are optional. When empty/omitted, Bedrock uses its defaults (standard tier, standard latency). The values flow through the full stack: ``` config.yaml -> runtime_provider -> agent_init -> chat_completion_helpers -> transport -> build_converse_kwargs -> boto3 converse() ``` ## Files changed - `hermes_cli/config.py` -- new config keys with docs - `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` -- read config, attach to runtime dict - `agent/agent_init.py` -- store on agent at init time - `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` -- pass to transport - `agent/transports/bedrock.py` -- forward to build_converse_kwargs - `agent/bedrock_adapter.py` -- emit `serviceTier` and `performanceConfig` in API kwargs - `tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py` -- 4 new tests ## Testing 125 bedrock_adapter tests passing (Python 3.11 + 3.14). Closes #31322

signals.title: fix(tui): preserve composer draft on prompt overlay
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #46278. This preserves an in-progress TUI composer draft when a clarify/approval prompt overlay blocks and unmounts `TextInput` before the deferred fast-echo parent sync fires. The bug is in the fast-echo path: simple ASCII input can update local refs immediately while deferring `onChange` for a frame. The old unmount cleanup cleared the parent-change timer without flushing the pending value, so prompt overlays could drop the newest draft text. The fix makes `flushParentChange` stable and calls it during unmount cleanup before timer state is discarded. Real environment tested Real `TextInput` mounted through Ink's renderer with stdin driven through the Ink input path. Exact steps or command run after this patch `node /Users/harjothk/Documents/cowork/hermes-agent/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run ui-tui/src/__tests__/textInputUnmountFlush.test.ts` Evidence after fix The regression test confirms `onChange` does not fire immediately for the fast-echo key, then unmount cleanup flushes the pending value. signals.title: fix(cli): accept available_models in custom provider config
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Makes `available_models` a recognized model-declaration key for custom providers, so a provider that declares its models under that key is actually routable by `/model`. **This PR has been re-scoped against current `main` — see "What changed" below.** ## Related Issue Fixes #52266 ## The bug on current `main` `_normalize_custom_provider_entry()` (`hermes_cli/config.py`) is the single chokepoint every custom-provider path runs through. It recognized only `models`, so a hand-written entry like the one in #52266: ```yaml custom_providers: - name: tokenplan api_mode: chat_completions base_url: https://token-plan.example/compatible-mode/v1 model: qwen3.7-plus available_models: [qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.7-max, deepseek-v4-flash, ...] ``` normalizes to an entry with **no `models` key at all**, and emits: ``` providers.tokenplan: unknown config keys ignored: available_models ``` Every downstream consumer reads the normalized `models` key, so the provider lists **(0) models** in the picker and no `/model <id>` against it resolves. ## What changed since this PR was opened The original version of this PR also added configured-provider colon parsing (`tokenplan:deepseek-v4-flash`, `custom:tokenplan:qwen3.7-max`). **That half is now fixed on `main`** by the "single-owner `/model` request parsing" consolidation in `model_switch.py` — all three forms from the issue parse cleanly there today, including the reported `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`. So this PR is re-scoped to the one thing still broken: the unrecognized declaration key. The diff is now one file plus tests, instead of the previous four-file change to `model_switch.py` and `config.py`. Reviewers: the earlier approval predates this rework and no longer describes the current diff — fresh eyes welcome. ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/config.py` - Merge `available_models` and `models` in `_normalize_custom_provider_entry()`. Fixing it at the chokepoint means typed routing, the picker list, and validation fallback all pick it up without each learning the alias. - `models` metadata wins for ids declared under both keys. - Extract the list/mapping coercion into `_declared_models_to_mapping()` so the alias inherits the same `[{id: ...}]` row handling `models` already had, instead of duplicating it. - Add `available_models` to `_KNOWN_KEYS` so it no longer trips the unknown-key warning. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_custom_provider_available_models.py` (new) - The issue's provider config verbatim; `[{id: ...}]` rows via the alias; `models`-wins-on-conflict; `models`-only entries unchanged; neither key leaves `models` unset; and a no-mutation check (entries alias the shared read-only config cache). ## How to Test 1. Configure a custom provider declaring models under `available_models` with hyphenated ids, as above. 2. Run `/model tokenplan:deepseek-v4-flash` (or `custom:tokenplan:qwen3.7-max`, or `/model deepseek-v4-flash --provider tokenplan`). 3. The switch resolves to `custom:tokenplan` and the requested model; the picker lists all declared models rather than (0). Verified on this branch: - `tests/hermes_cli/test_custom_provider_available_models.py` → **6 passed** - `test_config_validation.py`, `test_custom_provider_normalize_no_mutate.py`, `test_custom_provider_extra_headers.py`, `test_provider_config_validation.py`, `test_runtime_provider_resolution.py`, `test_config.py` → **142 passed** - `tests/hermes_cli/ -k "model_switch or picker or custom_provider or inventory"` → **218 passed** - `ruff check` on both changed files → **passed** ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Prevents xAI Grok Imagine media-generation models from being selected or saved as Hermes' main agent model. These models have small media/backend context windows and can fail the next agent initialization after `/model` reports a successful switch. The fix removes `grok-imagine-*` entries from the main xAI model picker, records their below-floor context defaults centrally, and makes xAI model validation a hard rejection when the resolved context is below Hermes' main-agent minimum. ## Related Issue Fixes #52595 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Added central context defaults for Grok Imagine image/video model IDs so they do not fall through to the generic Grok chat fallback. - Filtered all known below-floor xAI models out of the main-model catalog used by `/model`, using models.dev entry metadata with Hermes' offline defaults as fallback. - Added hard-reject validation for xAI/Grok models below Hermes' main-agent context floor, including live exact matches, autocorrect paths, hidden model soft-accept paths, configured-provider overrides, and custom endpoints verified as `api.x.ai`. - Added regression coverage for xAI OAuth, direct xAI, picker filtering, configured-provider override, below-floor live model rejection, custom xAI endpoints, and the shipped Grok Imagine video aliases. ## How to Test 1. `switch_model()` does not allow configured-provider overrides to bypass the hard rejection. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A ## Screenshots / Logs Focused proof: ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_xai_main_model_context_floor.py -q 13 passed in 0.87s ``` Adjacent proof: ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_xai_main_model_context_floor.py tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_live_curated_merge.py tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_configured_provider_routing.py tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_custom_providers.py tests/hermes_cli/test_xai_retirement.py tests/hermes_cli/test_user_providers_model_switch.py -q 137 passed in 146.05s ``` ## 2026-07-10 shepherding refresh Rebased the original human-authored commit onto current `main` (`7acaff5ef`) after 2,250 upstream commits of drift. Current main still allows models.dev `grok-imagine-*` entries into the xAI picker and still soft-accepts plausible hidden Grok slugs, so #52595 remains reproducible in the validation path. signals.title: fix(tools): clarify execute_code terminal approval guidance
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Clarifies the approval interaction between direct `terminal` calls, `execute_code` wrappers, and raw subprocesses so the model does not wrap a single command to avoid review. A one-command `execute_code` wrapper obscures the command's intent and, in gateway/ask sessions, adds whole-script approval. A wrapped `hermes_tools.terminal()` call still runs the normal terminal command-level checks, while raw subprocess commands cannot be inspected individually. The schema therefore recommends calling `terminal` directly for one command. Interactive CLI sessions are not claimed to add an outer approval prompt. The standalone terminal schema carries equivalent generic guidance without naming `execute_code`, so it remains valid when the code-execution toolset is disabled. The `execute_code` schema names `terminal` only when that tool is actually enabled. ## Related Issue Fixes #52738 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [x] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `tools/code_execution_tool.py`: adds one precise, dynamically gated warning against single-command terminal/subprocess wrappers, with gateway/ask approval scope stated explicitly. - `tools/terminal_tool.py`: recommends direct terminal use for one command using cross-tool-safe, deployment-neutral wording. - `tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py`: covers the registered schema, both execution modes, mutually exclusive tool-availability branches, no duplicate guidance, terminal-disabled sessions, and an explicitly empty tool set. - `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py`: pins the standalone terminal guidance and absence of a hard-coded `execute_code` reference. ## How to Test 1. Run the focused approval/schema suites: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_code_execution.py tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py ``` Result: 144 passed. 2. Run static and cross-platform checks: ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check tools/code_execution_tool.py tools/terminal_tool.py tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py .venv/bin/python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py tools/code_execution_tool.py tools/terminal_tool.py tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py git diff --check origin/main...HEAD ``` Result: Ruff passed, no Windows footguns found, diff check clean. 3. Duplicate-work checks: ```bash gh pr list --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --state all --search "52738" gh pr list --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --state all --search "execute_code terminal approval inner shell command schema guidance" ``` Both searches find no competing implementation. ## 2026-07-11 shepherding refresh Rebased both original human-authored commits onto current `main` (`6142203bd7`) after 2,217 upstream commits. Current main still lacks this approval-interaction guidance, so #52738 remains reproducible. Two private Grogu passes identified and this refresh repaired four concrete gaps in the original branch: duplicate wording inside the `execute_code` schema, an imprecise claim that wrapped `hermes_tools.terminal()` calls skip command-level checks, the missing standalone-terminal side of #52738, and an overbroad claim that whole-script approval applies outside gateway/ask contexts. Commit `b1fcac808` contains those corrections and expanded contract coverage. The issue's suggested inline annotation was implemented as a single paragraph before the available-tools list instead: this avoids repeating the same paid schema guidance beside the terminal stub while keeping it visible before tool selection. The existing user-facing approval-dialog text in `check_execute_code_guard` remains unchanged because it is constructed only after the gateway/ask gates where its one-shot description is accurate. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix - [x] I've run focused tests and all pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant tool descriptions/schemas are updated - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update N/A - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` update N/A - [x] Cross-platform impact considered and checked - [x] No dependency or configuration changes ## Screenshots / Logs Not applicable; this is model-facing schema guidance covered by tests.

signals.title: fix(cron): reject missing no-agent scripts
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? **Rewritten and rebased on current `main`.** Most of the original patch has since landed upstream, so this PR is now reduced to the one part that is still missing. A `no_agent` cron job runs its script instead of an agent, so the script *is* the job. `create_job()` already rejects a missing `script` argument, but a script filename that is not on disk was still accepted — scheduling a job that fails on every fire instead of failing once, loudly, at create time. What changed since this PR was opened: - `no_agent=True requires a script` — **already on `main`** (`tools/cronjob_tools.py:662`). - Script path shape and traversal containment — **already on `main`** (`_validate_cron_script_path`, `tools/cronjob_tools.py:492`), and stricter than this PR's original version: `main` now rejects absolute and `~` paths outright at the API boundary as a prompt-injection guard. - **Script existence — still missing.** That is all this PR now does. The original patch also introduced its own path validator that would have *re-allowed* absolute and `~` paths when they resolved inside the scripts directory. Rebasing that as-is would have relaxed a security boundary `main` deliberately tightened, so it is dropped entirely. `main`'s validator stays authoritative. Existence is enforced for `no_agent` jobs only. An agent job may legitimately reference a script it writes later, and the scheduler resolves those at fire time. ## Related Issue Fixes #53037 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) ## Changes Made - `cron/jobs.py` — in `create_job()`, next to the existing "no_agent requires a script" invariant, reject a `no_agent` job whose script does not resolve to an existing file. Relative paths resolve under `HERMES_HOME/scripts/`, matching the scheduler. - `tests/cron/test_cron_no_agent.py` — regression test for the missing-script case. Production diff is +15 lines; tests +18. ## How to Test 1. Reproduce on `main` — the new test fails with `DID NOT RAISE <class 'ValueError'>`: ``` scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_cron_no_agent.py ``` 2. With the fix, the same file passes: ``` === Summary: 1 files, 6 tests passed, 0 failed (100% complete) in 1.1s (16 workers) === ``` 3. signals.title: fix: /goal turn counter stuck at 0 when streaming is enabled
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes a bug where `/goal` turn counter stays at `0` forever when streaming is enabled (the default). When `streaming.enabled=true`, `_handle_message_with_agent()` delivers the response via streaming chunks and returns `None`. The goal continuation hook in `_handle_message()` then tries to extract `_final_text` — but `None` is neither `dict` nor `str`, so `_final_text` stays empty and the entire goal evaluation block is skipped: - `evaluate_after_turn()` is **never called** - `turns_used` stays **0 forever** - `/goal status` always shows `0/N turns` - Goal judge never runs → goal never completes ## Root Cause `gateway/run.py` — streaming path `return None` discards the response text that the goal hook needs. The goal continuation hook only handles `dict` and `str` return types, missing the `None` case. ## Fix Three changes in `gateway/run.py`: 1. **`__init__`** (~L5654): Initialize `self._last_streamed_response: Dict[str, str]` — a one-shot, session-scoped stash. 2. **`_handle_message_with_agent` streaming exit** (~L17299): Before `return None`, stash `response` text keyed by `session_key`. 3. **`_handle_message` goal hook** (~L14937): When `_agent_result is None`, recover text via `pop(_quick_key, "")` — one-shot consumption ensures no stale entries. This preserves the existing behavior (return `None` to avoid double-delivery) while making the response text available to the goal continuation hook. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) ## How to Test 1. Enable streaming (`streaming.enabled=true`) 2. Set a goal: `/goal complete this task` 3. Send a message to the agent 4. Check `/goal status` — before fix: `0/N turns`, after fix: `1/N turns` 5. Goal judge now runs and can reach `done` verdict ## Verification Tested on live instance + unit tests: - Before fix: `turns_used=0`, `last_turn_at=0.0`, no goal judge calls in logs - After fix + gateway restart: `turns_used` increments normally, goal can reach `done` verdict - 6 tests pass (including 2 new regression tests for the streaming `None` path) ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] N/A — no config keys, tool schemas, or architecture changes

signals.title: fix: bind prompt retries to durable sessions
signals.text: ## Summary Prompt retries now carry a client request ID and the durable stored-session destination. The gateway validates that destination before mutating history, then claims the request ID atomically so a lost acknowledgement cannot execute the same prompt twice after `session.resume` replaces the live runtime ID. This update is rebuilt on current `main` and keeps the route-pinning behavior already merged in #62413. The remaining desktop change is the request-ID/backend-contract layer. Ambiguous timeout replay is enabled only after the desktop sees backend contract v5, so older gateways keep the conservative no-replay behavior. The prompt-intent ledger is now SQLite-backed instead of using a process-wide 8,192-entry ceiling. It stores only request and payload digests, survives gateway restarts, prunes claims after the session retry TTL, and admits unrelated new prompt IDs while exact duplicate and conflicting reuse detection remains active. Queued prompt retries retain their original request IDs and rebind to the active transport after reconnect. Rewind/edit/regenerate submissions keep their truncation semantics rather than being converted into appended queued messages. ## Validation - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_prompt_intents.py tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py tests/test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py -q`: 458 passed, 0 failed. - Focused desktop Vitest: 96 passed, 0 failed. - Desktop TypeScript typecheck passed. - Desktop ESLint passed with 0 errors; the merged `main` test file retains one existing hooks-dependency warning. - Ruff passed on all changed Python implementation and test files. - Python `compileall` passed for the prompt ledger and gateway server. - The ledger regression admits 8,193 live IDs, then separately proves restart persistence and TTL pruning. ## Related Related: #62134, #62413 --- [![Compound Engineering](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built_with_Compound_Engineering-6366f1)](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin) ![GPT-5.5](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPT--5.5-000000)

signals.title: fix(mcp): skip dynamic tool refresh when session is closed or superseded
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? `tools/list_changed` refresh can queue behind shutdown or reconnect. A non-`None` `ClientSession` is not proof the transport is still live: teardown is not serialized by `_rpc_lock`, so a dying connection can still look open and a stale `tools/list` response can land after the session has been replaced or closed. This PR rebases the original snapshot + superseded-response discard onto current `main`'s collision-safe refresh body, then binds the fetch to a **session generation** snapshotted under `_rpc_lock`. **This PR now guarantees:** - Session pointer, generation, and `InitializeResult` capabilities are snapshotted only after `_refresh_lock` + `_rpc_lock`. - Closed (`session is None`) refreshes are a no-op. - Capability is taken from the locked generation, so a prompt/resource-only replacement is not asked for `tools/list`. - Teardown / recycle / reconnect / shutdown bump the generation *before* `ClientSession.__aexit__` starts closing the transport. - A closed-transport failure (`ClosedResourceError` / session-expired markers) on a **dying** generation is a clean skip: no error log, no registry mutation, no leaked refresh task. - Genuine `tools/list` protocol/server errors still propagate and still log `dynamic tool refresh failed`. - A superseded in-flight response is discarded and does not mutate the registry. - Current `main` collision-safe registry updates are preserved (ownership checks, normalization-ambiguous cleanup). **This PR does not invent a second ownership / publish model.** Discarding a superseded response does **not** publish the replacement session's tools. That authoritative reconnect / `list_changed` reconciliation belongs to #68808. In-flight RPC cancellation on teardown belongs to #48069. The generation counter is a refresh-liveness signal only and is compatible with both. ## Related Issue Related to MCP dynamic-refresh races on closed / superseded / dying sessions. Canonical narrow repair after #83354 closed as a duplicate of this PR. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `tools/mcp_tool.py`: - `_session_generation` + `_invalidate_session_generation()` / `_adopt_session()` / `_refresh_generation_stale()` - `_refresh_tools()` snapshots session/generation/capabilities under the locks; skips closed sessions; treats dying-transport errors as a clean skip; discards superseded responses - `_advertises_tools(init_result=...)` can evaluate a locked snapshot - generation bump on stdio recycle, lifecycle return (shutdown/reconnect), `shutdown()`, `run()` finally, and new session adopt - registry mutation body is current `main`'s collision-safe path - `tests/tools/test_mcp_dynamic_discovery.py`: closed, queued-reconnect, superseded-discard, locked capability, dying-transport (stdio + HTTP), genuine-error, and generation-invalidation tests ## How to Test ``` scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_dynamic_discovery.py tests/tools/test_mcp_capability_gating.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py -q ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] Conventional Commits (`fix(mcp):`) - [x] Only MCP refresh lifecycle changes - [x] Tests for closed / superseded / dying-transport refresh paths - [x] Focused MCP suite after rebase: 33/33 on discovery+capability; session-expired / pagination / failure-class / transport-group / reconnect-signal green; `test_mcp_tool.py` 93 passed (4 failures are missing `httpx`/`dotenv` in this environment, unrelated to this diff) - [x] `ruff check`, `compileall`, `git diff --check`, Windows-footgun scan clean on the touched files ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] N/A for docs / config / AGENTS.md / tool schemas
