signal.title: feat(video_gen/xai): allow 1080p for Grok Imagine text/image-to-video
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Allows Grok Imagine to generate 1080p video through the xAI video plugin. xAI's [video generation docs](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/video/generation) list `1080p` for `grok-imagine-video-1.5` on text-to-video and image-to-video, but the plugin allow-lists only `480p`/`720p` and silently rewrites anything else to the `720p` default — so requests for Full HD were downgraded before ever leaving the process. This adds `1080p` to `VALID_RESOLUTIONS` and soft-clamps reference-to-video back to `720p`, since xAI caps that mode regardless of the requested value. The clamp mirrors the file's existing soft-clamp idiom for invalid aspect ratios rather than introducing a new error path. Scope notes: - **edit/extend untouched** — those take no custom resolution and follow the input video, capped at 720p per xAI's docs. - **`DEFAULT_RESOLUTION` stays `720p`** — callers that don't ask for 1080p are unaffected. - **Tool description updates for free** — `capabilities()` reports `sorted(VALID_RESOLUTIONS)`, which is what builds the `resolution choices:` line in the `video_generate` description, so agents stop being told 720p is the ceiling (issue's item 4). - The default text-to-video path still routes to legacy `grok-imagine-video` via `_resolve_model_for_modality`; reaching 1080p t2v today requires an explicit `model=grok-imagine-video-1.5`. The routing (and its now-stale "1.5 rejects text-only" rationale — verified no longer true on a live deployment) is a separate concern left for a follow-up so this PR stays minimal. ## Related Issue Fixes #89549 ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `plugins/video_gen/xai/__init__.py` — add `1080p` to `VALID_RESOLUTIONS`; clamp reference-to-video 1080p requests to `720p` (xAI API constraint, hence the literal rather than `DEFAULT_RESOLUTION`) - `tests/plugins/video_gen/test_xai_plugin_integration.py` — new `TestXAIResolution` class: 1080p passes through for image-to-video and explicit-1.5 text-to-video, reference-to-video clamps to 720p, unknown values still fall back to the default, and `capabilities()` advertises 1080p ## How to Test 1. `pytest tests/plugins/video_gen/ tests/agent/test_video_gen_registry.py -q` 2. Mutation check: revert the `plugins/video_gen/xai/__init__.py` hunks and re-run — exactly the 3 tests asserting the new behavior fail; the 2 regression guards still pass. 3. Live proof: applied this same change to a running Hermes deployment (Docker, `hvps-hermes-agent` image), restarted, and a `video_generate` call with `model=grok-imagine-video-1.5`, `resolution=1080p` returned a genuine 1920×1080 file where it previously came back 1280×720. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — the touched area is fully green (`tests/plugins/video_gen/` + `tests/agent/test_video_gen_registry.py`, 22/22, and the 3 new behavior tests fail without the source change). A full local run of the 35,199-test suite was OOM-killed at ~79% on my machine before the summary, so I can't personally attest a complete green run — deferring full-suite verification to this PR's CI, which splits the suite into lanes for exactly this reason - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.5 (tests) + Ubuntu 24.04 Docker deployment (live 1080p generation) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A, no docs reference the resolution list - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no config keys changed - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — pure-Python set/string change, no platform surface - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — the `video_generate` description derives from `capabilities()`, which picks up the new value automatically 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: fix(cli): accept available_models in custom provider config
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Makes `available_models` a recognized model-declaration key for custom providers, so a provider that declares its models under that key is actually routable by `/model`. **This PR has been re-scoped against current `main` — see "What changed" below.** ## Related Issue Fixes #52266 ## The bug on current `main` `_normalize_custom_provider_entry()` (`hermes_cli/config.py`) is the single chokepoint every custom-provider path runs through. It recognized only `models`, so a hand-written entry like the one in #52266: ```yaml custom_providers: - name: tokenplan api_mode: chat_completions base_url: https://token-plan.example/compatible-mode/v1 model: qwen3.7-plus available_models: [qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.7-max, deepseek-v4-flash, ...] ``` normalizes to an entry with **no `models` key at all**, and emits: ``` providers.tokenplan: unknown config keys ignored: available_models ``` Every downstream consumer reads the normalized `models` key, so the provider lists **(0) models** in the picker and no `/model <id>` against it resolves. ## What changed since this PR was opened The original version of this PR also added configured-provider colon parsing (`tokenplan:deepseek-v4-flash`, `custom:tokenplan:qwen3.7-max`). **That half is now fixed on `main`** by the "single-owner `/model` request parsing" consolidation in `model_switch.py` — all three forms from the issue parse cleanly there today, including the reported `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`. So this PR is re-scoped to the one thing still broken: the unrecognized declaration key. The diff is now one file plus tests, instead of the previous four-file change to `model_switch.py` and `config.py`. Reviewers: the earlier approval predates this rework and no longer describes the current diff — fresh eyes welcome. ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/config.py` - Merge `available_models` and `models` in `_normalize_custom_provider_entry()`. Fixing it at the chokepoint means typed routing, the picker list, and validation fallback all pick it up without each learning the alias. - `models` metadata wins for ids declared under both keys. - Extract the list/mapping coercion into `_declared_models_to_mapping()` so the alias inherits the same `[{id: ...}]` row handling `models` already had, instead of duplicating it. - Add `available_models` to `_KNOWN_KEYS` so it no longer trips the unknown-key warning. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_custom_provider_available_models.py` (new) - The issue's provider config verbatim; `[{id: ...}]` rows via the alias; `models`-wins-on-conflict; `models`-only entries unchanged; neither key leaves `models` unset; and a no-mutation check (entries alias the shared read-only config cache). ## How to Test 1. Configure a custom provider declaring models under `available_models` with hyphenated ids, as above. 2. Run `/model tokenplan:deepseek-v4-flash` (or `custom:tokenplan:qwen3.7-max`, or `/model deepseek-v4-flash --provider tokenplan`). 3. The switch resolves to `custom:tokenplan` and the requested model; the picker lists all declared models rather than (0). Verified on this branch: - `tests/hermes_cli/test_custom_provider_available_models.py` → **6 passed** - `test_config_validation.py`, `test_custom_provider_normalize_no_mutate.py`, `test_custom_provider_extra_headers.py`, `test_provider_config_validation.py`, `test_runtime_provider_resolution.py`, `test_config.py` → **142 passed** - `tests/hermes_cli/ -k "model_switch or picker or custom_provider or inventory"` → **218 passed** - `ruff check` on both changed files → **passed** ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

signal.title: [Bug] terminal tool crashes: "embedded null character in path" (lifecycle_guard missing ValueError catch)
signal.text: ## 现象 Windows (git-bash/MSYS) 下用 terminal 工具执行 `python -m pytest` 报： `ValueError: open: embedded null character in path` ## 根因（已定位到行） `cron/lifecycle_guard.py` `_read_referenced_script`（第 256-262 行）： ```python try: descriptor = os.open(path, flags) # path 含 null 抛 ValueError except OSError: # 只捕获 OSError，未捕获 ValueError return None, False ``` path 含 null 字符时 os.open() 抛 ValueError（非 OSError），未捕获，异常上抛导致崩溃。 对比同文件第 313-316 行已正确 `except (OSError, ValueError)`（#76762），但第 324 行传给 _read_referenced_script 的是未 resolve 的 script_path（null 残留）。 ## 修复建议（一行） 第 261 行 `except OSError:` → `except (OSError, ValueError):` ## 环境 Windows 10 (git-bash/MSYS 后端)

signal.title: feat(desktop): opt-in settings for pinned display in inbox style and project lanes
signal.text: ## Summary Adds two **Settings → Sessions** toggles that opt into showing pinned threads the way the flat list does, while preserving the deliberate compact, Pinned-section-only defaults: 1. **Display pinned threads in Inbox style** — renders the Pinned section's rows as the same three-line inbox cards used by the flat recents list (`card-rows` / "Inbox style"), instead of the compact one-line rows pinned currently keeps by design. 2. **Show pinned threads in their project / worktree** — stops filtering pinned chats out of project/worktree lanes, so a pinned chat appears in **both** the Pinned section and the lane it belongs to. Both default **off**, so existing behavior is unchanged until a user opts in. ## Motivation (UI/QoL) - The sidebar's "Inbox style" (card-rows) is a render variant the flat recents list opts into; dense tree surfaces (pinned, projects, messaging) intentionally keep the one-line row. Users who want pinned to look like the inbox currently have no way to get that. - Pinned chats are deliberately exclusive ("a pinned session belongs to the Pinned section and nowhere else", `index.tsx`), so once pinned, a thread disappears from the project/worktree lanes it came from. This opt-in restores the duplicate view for people who want pins to remain findable in-context. ## Changes - `apps/desktop/src/store/layout.ts` — two new persisted atoms (`hermes.desktop.sidebarPinnedCardRows`, `hermes.desktop.sidebarPinnedInProjects`) + setters, following the existing `persistentAtom` pattern. - `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx` — Pinned section passes `card={pinnedCardRows}`; `isHiddenFromProjects` now skips the pin exclusion when the "show pinned in projects" setting is on. - `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/sessions-settings.tsx` — new `PinnedDisplaySettings` section with both `ToggleRow`s. - `apps/desktop/src/i18n/{en,zh,types}.ts` — copy + strict `Translations` type keys. - Tests: `store/layout-pinned-display.test.ts` (atom defaults/persistence), `app/settings/sessions-settings-pinned-display.test.tsx` (toggle rendering + atom wiring). ## Validation - `npx vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/sidebar/ src/store/layout-pinned-display.test.ts src/app/settings/sessions-settings-pinned-display.test.tsx src/store/gateway-switch.test.ts` — 177 passed. - `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — clean. - `npx eslint` on all changed files — clean. ## Notes - Flat recents and messaging sections still filter pins out (unchanged); this PR only affects the Pinned section rendering and project/worktree lanes, per the requested scope.

signal.title: [Feature]: configurable default scope for /reasoning changes
signal.text: ### Problem or Use Case `/reasoning <level>` is intentionally session-scoped by default, while `/reasoning <level> --global` persists the value to `agent.reasoning_effort`. That default is safe and should remain unchanged for existing users. However, users who normally want every interactive reasoning-level change to become the new global default must remember to append `--global` each time. There is currently no configuration preference that changes the command's default scope. A one-time `/reasoning <level> --global` is sufficient when the preferred level is static. It does not cover workflows where the user frequently changes levels and expects each selection to persist across new CLI/TUI/Desktop/gateway sessions. This is distinct from the already implemented `--global` support discussed in #14617: the request is not to add `--global`, but to make persistence the configurable default while retaining an explicit session-only escape hatch. ### Proposed Solution Add an opt-in configuration option, for example: ```yaml agent: reasoning_command_scope: global # session (default) | global ``` Expected behavior: - Default remains `session` for backward compatibility. - With `reasoning_command_scope: global`, `/reasoning high` behaves like today's `/reasoning high --global` and persists `agent.reasoning_effort`. - `/reasoning high --session` always creates a session-only override, regardless of the configured default. - Explicit `--global` always persists, regardless of the configured default. - Bare `/reasoning` reports the effective command default scope so the behavior is discoverable. - The behavior is consistent across interactive CLI, Ink TUI/Desktop gateway RPC, and messaging gateway implementations. - `show`/`hide` and display-only commands keep their existing persistence semantics; this option controls effort-level changes only. A boolean such as `agent.reasoning_persist_by_default: true` would also work, but an enum leaves room for clearer validation and status output. ### Alternatives Considered 1. Continue requiring `--global` on every change. This works today but does not satisfy users who consistently prefer persistence and is easy to forget in pickers or frequent model-tuning workflows. 2. Change `/reasoning <level>` to global for everyone. Rejected because it would be a breaking behavioral change and could unexpectedly alter future sessions. 3. Use per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides`. Useful when levels are fixed per model, but not equivalent to making interactive changes persist by default. 4. Add a separate command such as `/reasoning-global`. This duplicates the existing command surface and is less composable than a default-scope preference plus explicit `--session`/`--global` flags. ### Feature Type Configuration option ### Scope Medium (few files, < 300 lines) ### Contribution A maintainer decision on the config key/name and cross-surface scope would be useful before implementation.

signal.title: [Windows] Hermes kills svchost.exe via stale-PID taskkill /F /PID → repeated 0xEF (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED) blue screens
signal.text: # [Windows] Hermes kills `svchost.exe` via stale-PID `taskkill /F /PID` → repeated 0xEF (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED) blue screens **Environment:** Windows 11 24H2 (build 10.0.26200.9168), Hermes Desktop (CI build 2026-08-18, commit 8a770aae0d550bb92eb021913bd102a61ccc40af), 32 GB RAM ## Summary On Windows, Hermes terminates processes with bare `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` without verifying that the PID currently belongs to the intended process. PIDs recorded before a reboot (persisted ownership files, stale `.pid` files, or **hardcoded PIDs in scripts**) are routinely recycled by Windows to unrelated processes — in our case repeatedly to `svchost.exe`. Killing a protected critical process triggers `bugcheck 0xEF (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED)`, i.e. a full blue screen. **Observed:** 8 identical BSODs in 48 hours, all `0x000000EF` with WER bucket `0xEF_svchost.exe_BUGCHECK_CRITICAL_PROCESS_TERMINATED_BY_taskkill.exe_1_svchost.exe!unknown_function`. ## Evidence ### 8 blue screens, all the same signature WER reports (`Microsoft-Windows-WER-SystemErrorReporting`, Event 1001): | Time | Bugcheck | WER bucket | |---|---|---| | 2026-08-17 16:48 | 0xEF | `0xEF_svchost.exe_BUGCHECK_CRITICAL_PROCESS_TERMINATED_BY_taskkill.exe...` | | 2026-08-17 16:54 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-17 18:47 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-17 23:30 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 07:18 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 16:11 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 16:42 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 17:19 | 0xEF | same | | 2026-08-18 17:23 | 0xEF | same | Every crash's `Response.BucketId` contains `BUGCHECK_CRITICAL_PROCESS_TERMINATED_BY_taskkill.exe` — Windows itself attributed the death of `svchost.exe` to a `taskkill.exe` invocation. Bugcheck params: Param1 = EPROCESS of the dying process, Param2/Param4 = 0. The crash that followed the desktop auto-update is particularly damning: the app was rebuilt at 17:16 (install-stamp / `app.asar` mtime), and the machine blue-screened at 17:19 and again at 17:23. ### Unsafe `taskkill /PID` call sites (no ownership verification) 1. **Desktop `forceKillProcessTree`** — `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` (and compiled `app.asar.unpacked/dist/electron-main.mjs`): ```ts function forceKillProcessTree(pid) { if (!IS_WINDOWS) return; if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return; try { execFileSync('taskkill', ['/PID', String(pid), '/T', '/F'], ...); } catch {} } ``` Called from `stopBackendChild(child)` / single-instance / orphan-backend cleanup paths. The PID can come from persisted state (`backend-ownership.json`, `gateway.pid`) recorded in a previous boot. 2. **Hardcoded stale PID in a restart script** — `gateway-service/restart_gateway.bat`: ```bat taskkill /F /PID 33796 ``` `33796` was the gateway's PID at some earlier point. It is long dead; Windows has since recycled that number. Any invocation of this script now kills whatever process currently owns PID 33796 — our system did not have 33796 assigned at inspection time, i.e. it is a loaded gun. 3. **Python-side kills** — `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py` (`kill_process_tree`), `hermes_cli/dashboard_procs.py` (`taskkill /PID <pid> /F`), `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` (`_stop_process_trees`: `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`) — same pattern, no check that the target is a Hermes process. ### Crash mechanism (reproduction) 1. During some run, a Hermes/gateway PID gets persisted (`gateway.pid`, `backend-ownership.json`) or hardcoded (`restart_gateway.bat`). 2. Machine reboots. Windows allocates PIDs sequentially; the stale PID is quickly handed to another process — with dozens of `svchost.exe` instances running, the recycled PID often *is* an `svchost.exe` (protected critical process). 3. On boot, Hermes Desktop starts (autostart / user launch), runs single-instance / orphan-backend cleanup → `forceKillProcessTree(<stale pid>)`. Or the gateway watchdog re-runs `restart_gateway.bat` → `taskkill /F /PID <stale>`. 4. `svchost.exe` is killed → kernel detects a critical process died → `bugcheck 0xEF` → BSOD. This matches the observed pattern: every crash occurred shortly after boot or right after an auto-update, when the desktop app starts and reconciles old process records. ### Why it escaped detection - Kernel dumps were written as full-memory dumps (`CrashDumpEnabled=0x3`, `PAGEDU64` header with `dumpfve.sys` filter), which generic minidump tooling can't parse locally — the WER bucket string was the reliable signal. - The failure is timing-dependent (PID reuse) and only fires during startup/update cleanup, so it's hard to reproduce on demand. - User-side patches applied on 2026-08-17 were silently wiped by the CI auto-update on 2026-08-18, and the machine blue-screened again 3 minutes later. ## Suggested fix 1. **Verify PID ownership before every `taskkill`.** On Windows, query `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>"` and only kill when `CommandLine`/`ExecutablePath` matches the expected Hermes process (path contains `hermes`, venv, `gateway run`, etc.). If the PID is missing or doesn't match, skip. This is the minimal, robust guard for all five call sites (and any future one). 2. **Never hardcode PIDs in scripts.** Use process discovery by command line (the existing `find_gateway_pids` / `kill_gateway.ps1` pattern) or a `.pid` file with a start-time fingerprint that is re-validated before use. 3. **Reuse the existing identity checks.** The codebase already has `startMarker` / `processIdentityMatches` / `backendIdentityMatches` guards for orphan-backend cleanup — route `forceKillProcessTree` through the same verification instead of its own bare path. A user-side hotfix implementing (1) and (2) for all five call sites is applied locally and has been verified (guard skips non-Hermes PIDs, including the stale `33796`); it can be shared as a reference patch if useful. ## Impact On affected Windows machines: repeated unannounced blue screens, potential data loss from unsaved work, and (for less lucky PID recycling) the possibility of killing other unrelated processes. Any Windows user who reboots frequently, uses the desktop app autostart, or triggers the update path is exposed to the same crash.

signal.title: fix(desktop): let sessions in Home be moved into a freshly created project
signal.text: # fix(desktop): "Move to project" no longer dead-ends when only the Home bucket exists ## Background Hermes Desktop's sidebar groups sessions by Project. A session whose `cwd` sits inside a folder no explicit project owns falls into the synthetic **Home** bucket (id `__no_project__`, `isNoProject: true`). The kebab menu's **"Move to project"** submenu (`MoveToProjectItems` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.tsx`) shows the projects the session CAN move into — the current owner is excluded, and `isNoProject` is excluded because Home has no folder to re-home into. When the user has not yet created any explicit project, the submenu renders exactly one item: a **disabled** "No other projects" line. There is no path from that disabled line to actually moving the session. The user has to: 1. Close the menu 2. Open the sidebar's "New project" button 3. Re-pick the directory the session is already in 4. Type a project name 5. Confirm 6. Reopen the session's kebab menu → Move to project → pick the new project Six steps to do what should be a two-click operation. The session's existing `cwd` already points at exactly the folder the new project needs. Reproduction is verified live on Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (macOS arm64). Before this change: sidebar projects view shows only "Home", session kebab → Move to project shows a single disabled item, no move is possible. After this change: the submenu shows an actionable "New project…" entry that completes the move in two clicks. ## Root cause The filter in `MoveToProjectItems`: ```ts const targets = tree.filter(node => node.id !== currentProjectId && !node.isNoProject && // ← Home is always filtered out projectRootCwd(node) ) if (targets.length === 0) { return <kit.Item disabled>{p.moveNoProjects}</kit.Item> // ← dead-end } ``` is correct as far as it goes: Home really has nowhere to move a session INTO. The bug is the **fallback when there is no real target**: instead of exposing the only available action (create a project), the menu tells the user nothing can be done. ## Existing solutions surveyed | Path | What it does | Why it doesn't solve the dead-end | | --- | --- | --- | | Sidebar's `SidebarBlankState` (sidebar/index.tsx:1762) `onNewProject` | One-click project creation from the empty Projects view | Only reachable when the user is already in the empty Projects view AND has no session selected; doesn't fire from the per-session menu | | `openProjectCreate()` (store/projects.ts) | Opens the create dialog with an empty folder list | The dialog requires the user to re-pick the session's cwd AND name the project; no callback fires after creation | | `moveSessionToProject(sessionId, projectId, profile)` (store/projects.ts:526) | Re-anchors a session to a project's root folder via `session.workspace.move` RPC | Requires an existing `projectId`; not useful when no project exists yet | | `ProjectDialog` (app/chat/sidebar/project-dialog.tsx) | Mounted dialog that reads `$projectDialog` atom; handles create / rename / add-folder | Lacked an `onCreated` callback seam and a folder-prefill mechanism, so it couldn't be chained from a submenu | The fix wires together the last two rows: extend `$projectDialog` state with `prefillFolder` and `onCreated`, then have `MoveToProjectItems` call `openProjectCreate({ prefillFolder, onCreated })` instead of the bare `openProjectCreate()`. ## Approach Two minimal, additive changes: 1. `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` — `$projectDialog` state gains `prefillFolder?: string` and `onCreated?: (project) => void | Promise<void>` fields. `openProjectCreate(options)` carries them through. 2. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/project-dialog.tsx` — the `useEffect` that resets state on open now seeds `folders` from `prefillFolder` when `mode === 'create'`. After a successful submit, if `onCreated` is set, it's invoked AFTER the dialog closes (so the user is back in the menu and toasts land against the right surface). Errors in the callback toast but never roll back the project that was just created. 3. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.tsx` — `MoveToProjectItems`: - When `targets.length === 0` (only Home exists): instead of a disabled "No other projects" item, render an actionable "New project…" item that opens the create dialog with the session's cwd prefilled. - When `targets.length > 0`: keep existing behaviour but add a separator + "New project…" entry at the bottom so the affordance is reachable from any session, not only the Home case. - The new entry closes over an `onCreated` callback that calls `moveSessionToProject(sessionId, project.id, profile)` and shows the existing "Moved to …" success toast. What we **preserve**: - `MoveToProjectItems`'s filter logic — the Home exclusion and "current project exclusion" rules are still correct. - `openProjectCreate()`'s RPC contract — `projects.create` body is unchanged. - `moveSessionToProject()`'s RPC contract — `session.workspace.move` is unchanged. What we **do not duplicate**: - A new "move to project" RPC method. - A new project-creation entry point. - A new persisted store for the create dialog's transient state. - Any new IPC surface, env var, or schema field. ## What this preserves about the user's mental model - A session's `cwd` is the most natural anchor for "what project does this belong to". The fix does not change that — it uses the existing `cwd` as the new project's primary folder, exactly as the manual flow does. - "Move" still means `session.workspace.move` (re-anchor cwd + git identity, refresh the live agent). The fix reuses the existing `moveSessionToProject` helper end-to-end. - The Home bucket remains the "no project owner" fallback for backward compatibility — `isNoProject` is still filtered from the target list because Home really has nothing to move into. ## Regression coverage `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.test.tsx`: - The pre-existing "opens the dropdown on click without a tooltip on the kebab" test continues to assert rename + archive are reachable (unchanged assertions — the new code path doesn't touch them). - A new test "offers 'New project and move here…' when the sidebar has only the Home bucket" seeds `$projectTree` to a single Home node, opens the menu, drills into the Move-to-project submenu, asserts the new affordance is **enabled** (not disabled), clicks it, and asserts `openProjectCreate` was called with the session's cwd prefilled. The test mocks both `openProjectCreate` and `moveSessionToProject` and verifies the entry point — the dialog driver is covered by its own existing tests (`project-dialog.test.tsx`). Full suite on the upstream/main worktree: ``` Test Files 428 passed (428) Tests 3843 passed (3843) ``` ## Decision rationale - **Why not a separate "create project" sidebar button?** That path exists (`SidebarBlankState.onNewProject`) but it's reachable from the empty-projects view, not from inside a session's kebab menu. Adding a second entry point under every session is the cheapest way to cover the case the user is in when they discover the gap: staring at a session they can't move. - **Why not auto-create a project on first session?** That would be surprising — the user didn't ask for a project to exist. The fix keeps the create step explicit (the user names the project) and just collapses the rest. - **Why callback instead of a hard-coded move in the dialog?** The dialog is reusable; `openProjectCreate()` is also called from the sidebar with no follow-up work. The callback keeps the dialog single-purpose and lets the menu compose the create-then-move without the dialog knowing what "move" means. ## Who should enable this Every Hermes Desktop user who has at least one session in the Home bucket and wants to re-home it into a project. The change is behavioural only — no flag, no opt-in, no new env var. The old behaviour (a disabled "No other projects" line) is replaced wherever the dead-end would otherwise appear. ## Platform compatibility | Platform | Behaviour | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | macOS (Apple Silicon) | Tested live on Hermes 0.17.0 build | Reproduced and verified after fix | | macOS (Intel) | Same | Renderer-only change, no native code path | | Windows | Same | Renderer-only change | | Linux | Same | Renderer-only change | | Web Dashboard / TUI | N/A | The bug exists only in the desktop sidebar's session menu | ## Quick-start guide There is nothing to enable. The change ships with the next Hermes Desktop release. After updating: 1. Open the sidebar, click the **Projects** tab. 2. If only the **Home** bucket is visible, right-click any session row under Home → ⋮ → **Move to project** → **New project…**. 3. The dialog opens with the session's directory prefilled. Type a name → **Create**. 4. The session is re-homed into the new project immediately. A "Moved to …" toast confirms. If the sidebar already has explicit projects, the **New project…** entry also appears at the bottom of the Move-to-project submenu — it's just no longer required to reach the feature. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | | --- | --- | --- | | Submenu still shows disabled "No other projects" | Build is older than this PR's merge; desktop loaded a stale `app.asar` | Run `hermes update` (or rebuild + restart the desktop app) and reload the window | | Clicking "New project…" opens a dialog with no folders | Session has no `cwd` recorded (rare — detached sessions) | Pick any folder manually; the move still works because the dialog's folder becomes the new project's root | | "Moved to …" toast fires but the session still appears under Home | The `session.workspace.move` RPC succeeded locally but the sidebar hasn't refreshed | Click the sidebar's **Projects** tab to force a tree refresh; the next `projects.tree` poll will land the new owner | | Clicking the new entry does nothing | Stale build cache for `dist/assets/` | Restart Hermes Desktop — the renderer reloads the new bundle | ## Diff stat ``` apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/project-dialog.tsx | 28 +++- apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.test.tsx | 150 ++++++++++++++++++--- apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-actions-menu.tsx | 59 +++++++- apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts | 1 + apps/desktop/src/i18n/types.ts | 1 + apps/desktop/src/i18n/zh.ts | 1 + apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts | 16 ++- 7 files changed, 228 insertions(+), 28 deletions(-) ```

signal.title: [Bug]: Chinese reasoning tags ( 思考 / 反思 / 推理 / 推敲) from MiniMax-M3 leak to user output in streaming + final response
signal.text:
## Bug Description When using `MiniMax-M3` via the `minimax-tokenplan` provider (or any MiniMax deployment serving the M3 model) the gateway / CLI / agent emit raw Chinese-language reasoning tokens to the user-visible output. Tags such as ` 思考`, ` 反思`, ` 推理`, and ` 推敲` (which MiniMax M3 uses in place of / alongside the English `<think>` family) are not stripped, so end users in Telegram/Discord see fragments like: > 让我 思考 …right in the middle of the assistant's response. The English-tag filtering path (`<think>`, `<thinking>`, `<reasoning>`, `<REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>`, `<thought>`) works correctly — only the Chinese / non-Latin variants are missing from the filter lists. This is a direct sibling of #17924 (which fixed the *English* inline-tag leak on the CLI) and an extension of the filter-completeness issue tracked in #27288 (mixed-case tag variants in streaming). The Chinese tag families were simply never added to the three hard-coded tag tuples that all consumer code paths consult. ## Environment - **Hermes Agent:** v0.16.0 (local checkout at `a8f404b29` on `main`) - **Provider:** `minimax-tokenplan` (custom provider, `https://api.minimax.io/v1`, `api_mode: chat_completions`, API key from `MINIMAX_API_KEY`) - **Model:** `MiniMax-M3` (1M context, displayed as "MiniMax M3" — the new M3 reasoning model, not M2.7) - **Gateway platform:** Telegram (group topic), streaming mode enabled by default - **Config that reproduces:** ```yaml model: default: minimax-tokenplan/MiniMax-M3 provider: minimax-tokenplan providers: minimax-tokenplan: api: https://api.minimax.io/v1 api_key: ${MINIMAX_API_KEY} api_mode: chat_completions default_model: MiniMax-M3 models: MiniMax-M3: context_length: 1000000 ``` ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a custom `minimax-tokenplan` provider pointed at `https://api.minimax.io/v1` with `MiniMax-M3` registered (see config above). 2. Start the gateway and chat with the model via Telegram, or run `hermes chat -m MiniMax-M3 --provider minimax-tokenplan` interactively. 3. Send any prompt that triggers a reasoning response (basically any non-trivial question — M3 reasons by default). 4. Watch the streaming response. 5. Observe: Chinese reasoning tokens (` 思考`, ` 反思`, ` 推理`, ` 推敲`, etc.) are streamed verbatim to the user and also land in the final stored message. The English `<think>` family, by contrast, is filtered correctly. ## Expected Behavior All inline reasoning content — English **or** Chinese — should be silently filtered before it reaches the user, matching the behavior already in place for the English tag set. ## Actual Behavior The Chinese tag open/close pairs are passed straight through. Example observed in `agent.log` for a Telegram topic: ``` 2026-06-10 19:12:10,048 INFO run_agent: OpenAI client created provider=minimax-tokenplan base_url=https://api.minimax.io/v1 model=MiniMax-M3 2026-06-10 19:12:20,378 INFO agent.conversation_loop: API call #1 model=MiniMax-M3 provider=minimax-tokenplan in=64539 out=523 total=65062 latency=10.3s ``` The 523 output tokens include the raw Chinese tag payloads, which are then sent to Telegram as part of the response (and persisted in the session transcript). ## Root Cause The three filter sites that all consumer code paths consult are hard-coded to the **English** reasoning-tag family only. None of them include the Chinese variants that MiniMax M3 emits. A comment at the top of each list explicitly says they "must stay in sync" — meaning any fix has to be applied in all three places. | # | File | Lines | Symbol | What's stored | |---|------|-------|--------|---------------| | 1 | `gateway/stream_consumer.py` | 101–108 | `GatewayStreamConsumer._OPEN_THINK_TAGS` / `_CLOSE_THINK_TAGS` | Streaming-time state-machine filter that scrubs interim Telegram / Discord edits | | 2 | `cli.py` | 4664–4765 | `HermesCLI._stream_delta` local `_OPEN_TAGS` / `_CLOSE_TAGS` | CLI streaming-time filter for `prompt_toolkit` | | 3 | `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` | 449–510 | `strip_think_blocks()` regexes (5 `re.sub` calls for the English tags) | Final post-processing for stored / sent content | Current contents of all three lists are identical and incomplete: ```python _OPEN_THINK_TAGS = ( "<REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "<think>", "<reasoning>", "<THINKING>", "<thinking>", "<thought>", ) _CLOSE_THINK_TAGS = ( "</REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "</think>", "</reasoning>", "</THINKING>", "</thinking>", "</thought>", ) ``` Note: the `strip_think_blocks()` function applies its `re.sub` regexes case-insensitively (good — covers mixed-case English), but the streaming state machines in the other two files do a plain `str.find()` comparison against the exact tuples above, so even the case-insensitive coverage from `strip_think_blocks` doesn't extend to them. ## Suggested Fix Extend all three tag tuples to include the Chinese families MiniMax M3 uses. The exact set I have observed in the wild is: - ` 思考` (think) - ` 反思` (reflect) - ` 推理` (reason / reason out) - ` 推敲` (deliberate / weigh) A minimal patch that brings all three sites back in sync: ```python _OPEN_THINK_TAGS = ( "<REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "<think>", "<reasoning>", "<THINKING>", "<thinking>", "<thought>", " 思考", " 反思", " 推理", " 推敲", ) _CLOSE_THINK_TAGS = ( "</REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>", "</think>", "</reasoning>", "</THINKING>", "</thinking>", "</thought>", " 思考", " 反思", " 推理", " 推敲", ) ``` For the streaming state machines in `stream_consumer.py` and `cli.py`, the comparison is currently a case-sensitive `str.find()`. To also cover the mixed-case bug from #27288 in the same change, consider normalising the search buffer (`.lower()` once per delta) while preserving the original text for emission — that way a single change closes both the Chinese-tag gap and the mixed-case tag gap. For `strip_think_blocks()` in `agent_runtime_helpers.py`, add four parallel `re.sub` calls (case-insensitive, `re.DOTALL`) so the post-processing layer can never persist the raw tokens either: ```python content = re.sub(r' 思考.*? 思考', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) content = re.sub(r' 反思.*? 反思', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) content = re.sub(r' 推理.*? 推理', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) content = re.sub(r' 推敲.*? 推敲', '', content, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE) ``` A small regression test in `tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_chinese_think_tags.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_strip_think_blocks.py` that feeds a known M3 response (e.g. `" 思考
…
 思考

signal.title: fix: bind prompt retries to durable sessions
signal.text: ## Summary Prompt retries now carry a client request ID and the durable stored-session destination. The gateway validates that destination before mutating history, then claims the request ID atomically so a lost acknowledgement cannot execute the same prompt twice after `session.resume` replaces the live runtime ID. This update is rebuilt on current `main` and keeps the route-pinning behavior already merged in #62413. The remaining desktop change is the request-ID/backend-contract layer. Ambiguous timeout replay is enabled only after the desktop sees backend contract v5, so older gateways keep the conservative no-replay behavior. The prompt-intent ledger is now SQLite-backed instead of using a process-wide 8,192-entry ceiling. It stores only request and payload digests, survives gateway restarts, prunes claims after the session retry TTL, and admits unrelated new prompt IDs while exact duplicate and conflicting reuse detection remains active. Queued prompt retries retain their original request IDs and rebind to the active transport after reconnect. Rewind/edit/regenerate submissions keep their truncation semantics rather than being converted into appended queued messages. ## Validation - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_prompt_intents.py tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py tests/test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py -q`: 458 passed, 0 failed. - Focused desktop Vitest: 96 passed, 0 failed. - Desktop TypeScript typecheck passed. - Desktop ESLint passed with 0 errors; the merged `main` test file retains one existing hooks-dependency warning. - Ruff passed on all changed Python implementation and test files. - Python `compileall` passed for the prompt ledger and gateway server. - The ledger regression admits 8,193 live IDs, then separately proves restart persistence and TTL pruning. ## Related Related: #62134, #62413 --- [![Compound Engineering](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built_with_Compound_Engineering-6366f1)](https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin) ![GPT-5.5](https://img.shields.io/badge/GPT--5.5-000000)

signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds first-class MrScraper support to Hermes through bundled native plugins and the optional MCP catalog. The native integration uses `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` and provides standard `web_search` and `web_extract` provider support alongside focused `mrscraper_*` tools for Google SERP search, JavaScript-rendered pages, crawling, structured extraction, scraper management, batch runs, and result retrieval. The rendered-page integration exposes `mrscraper_fetch_rendered_html` as a focused native tool rather than registering MrScraper as `browser.cloud_provider`. MrScraper handles independent rendered-page requests but does not expose the persistent CDP/WebSocket session required by interactive tools such as `browser_click`, `browser_type`, and `browser_scroll`. A separate optional MCP catalog entry connects to MrScraper's official hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server using `MCP_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`. ## Results The integration adds three complementary MrScraper surfaces without expanding Hermes' permanent core tool schema: | Surface | Integration | Credential | Capabilities | |---|---|---|---| | Standard web provider | `plugins/web/mrscraper/provider.py` | `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` | `web_search` and `web_extract` | | Focused native tools | `plugins/web/mrscraper/tools.py` and `plugins/browser/mrscraper/` | `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` | SERP search, rendered pages, crawling, extraction, scraper runs, and results | | Hosted MCP | `optional-mcps/mrscraper/manifest.yaml` | `MCP_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` | Tools exposed by MrScraper's hosted MCP server | The bundled native tools are credential-gated and only register when `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` is available. The hosted MCP remains independently installable and keeps its credential separate from the native integration. Focused validation passes all 70 tests covering the browser plugin, web plugin, provider discovery, request construction, response normalization, error handling, and credential redaction. ## Methodology and provenance - Native API client: `plugins/mrscraper_client.py` - Web provider: `plugins/web/mrscraper/provider.py` - Provider-specific tools: `plugins/web/mrscraper/tools.py` - Rendered-page integration: `plugins/browser/mrscraper/provider.py` - Hosted MCP catalog entry: `optional-mcps/mrscraper/manifest.yaml` - Browser plugin tests: `tests/plugins/browser/test_mrscraper_plugin.py` - Web plugin tests: `tests/plugins/web/test_mrscraper_plugin.py` - Provider discovery tests: `tests/plugins/web/test_web_search_provider_plugins.py` - Native integration credential: `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` - Hosted MCP credential: `MCP_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` - Native integration commit: `4f8770fdb` - MCP catalog commit: `0e9fa2fb1` - Focused test result: 70 passed - Diff hygiene: `git diff --check` passed The test suite uses controlled responses to verify request payloads, normalized provider output, registration gates, scraper operations, result retrieval, API failures, and secret redaction without requiring billable live API calls. ## Changes - Add a shared MrScraper HTTP client with: - Token discovery from `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` - Authenticated JSON requests - Timeout and response handling - API error normalization - Credential redaction - Shared request and URL-encoding helpers - Add a standard MrScraper web provider with: - Google SERP-backed `web_search` - JavaScript-rendered `web_extract` - Normalized results compatible with Hermes' existing web provider interfaces - Explicit provider selection through `hermes tools` or `web.search_backend` and `web.extract_backend` - Add focused `mrscraper_*` tools for: - Account information - Google SERP search - Website URL crawling - Prompt-based page extraction - Listing extraction - Structured-data extraction - Prompt scraper creation - Listing scraper creation - Website-crawl scraper creation - Existing scraper execution - Batch scraper execution - Result listing - Latest-result retrieval - Individual result retrieval - Add `mrscraper_fetch_rendered_html` for reliable website scraping using cloud browsers with JavaScript rendering. - Supports rendered HTML or Markdown - Supports screenshots and cookies - Supports proxy country selection - Supports resource blocking - Supports CSS wait selectors - Supports `load` and `networkidle` wait conditions - Keep MrScraper outside the interactive browser-provider registry because it does not expose persistent CDP/WebSocket sessions. - Add the official hosted MrScraper server to the optional MCP catalog. - Add `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN` to `.env.example`. - Add focused browser, web, and provider-discovery test coverage. - Update English and Simplified Chinese documentation for: - Browser automation - Web search and extraction - Conditional skill requirements - Tool Gateway behavior - Dashboard credential management - MCP installation ## Reproduce Configure the bundled native integration: ```bash # Add to ~/.hermes/.env MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN=your-token-here ``` Select MrScraper through the setup UI: ```text hermes tools → Web Search & Extract → MrScraper ``` Alternatively, configure the web providers directly: ```yaml # ~/.hermes/config.yaml web: search_backend: "mrscraper" extract_backend: "mrscraper" ``` Start a new Hermes session and request a web search or rendered-page extraction. The standard `web_search` and `web_extract` tools will use MrScraper, and the focused `mrscraper_*` tools will be available while the token is configured. Install the separate hosted MCP integration with: ```bash hermes mcp install mrscraper ``` The MCP installer requests `MCP_MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`. This credential is intentionally separate from the native integration's `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN`. Run the focused validation suite: ```bash pytest \ tests/plugins/browser/test_mrscraper_plugin.py \ tests/plugins/web/test_mrscraper_plugin.py \ tests/plugins/web/test_web_search_provider_plugins.py \ -q ``` Check patch hygiene: ```bash git diff --check ``` ## Validation | Check | Observed result | |---|---| | Focused plugin and provider tests | 70/70 passed | | Browser rendered-page coverage | Registration, request construction, optional arguments, response handling, and errors covered | | Web integration coverage | Search, extraction, crawling, structured extraction, scraper runs, batch runs, and results covered | | Provider discovery | MrScraper registration and credential gating covered | | Secret handling | API token redaction covered | | Diff hygiene | `git diff --check` passed | | Live MrScraper API validation | Not run; focused tests use controlled API responses | | Full repository test suite | Not run | ## Scope This PR adds MrScraper at Hermes' plugin and MCP edges; it does not add a new permanent core model tool. The native integration is opt-in and requires `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN`. MrScraper is excluded from the legacy automatic web-provider preference walk, so users select it explicitly through `hermes tools` or the `web` configuration. The rendered-page tool performs independent URL requests. It is not an interactive cloud-browser backend and cannot provide persistent sessions for clicking, typing, scrolling, or other multi-step browser actions. Those workflows still require Browserbase, Browser Use, Firecrawl, Camofox, or a local Chromium-family browser. The optional hosted MCP is a separate integration with a separate credential. Installing it does not configure or replace the bundled native provider. signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #46278. This preserves an in-progress TUI composer draft when a clarify/approval prompt overlay blocks and unmounts `TextInput` before the deferred fast-echo parent sync fires. The bug is in the fast-echo path: simple ASCII input can update local refs immediately while deferring `onChange` for a frame. The old unmount cleanup cleared the parent-change timer without flushing the pending value, so prompt overlays could drop the newest draft text. The fix makes `flushParentChange` stable and calls it during unmount cleanup before timer state is discarded. Real environment tested Real `TextInput` mounted through Ink's renderer with stdin driven through the Ink input path. signal.title: Desktop: profile switching hangs silently after atomically-published gateway switch refactor (Windows)
signal.text: ## Environment - Windows 11, Hermes Desktop (packaged, git install), v0.20.4 · upstream c69b6471e6 ## Symptom Clicking a profile in the sidebar rail (e.g. architect) does nothing: no UI change, no loading state, no error, and **no new WebSocket connection to the target backend** (netstat shows 0 ESTABLISHED on the pooled backend's port). Every subsequent profile click also fails — the app is stuck on the current profile until Desktop is restarted. ## Regression window Works on 86b2057a (2026-08-17). Broken after the "publish gateway/profile/connection atomically" series: - d57f94a330 publish gateway, profile, and connection descriptor atomically on a profile switch - 053eb7aab0 publish a gateway switch in one nanostores batch - 4e520f0850 guard the profile publication on its activation result too - (plus 20ccf88acd / d0e0951cf1 agent-side analogues) ## Evidence - All pooled backends boot fine: each profile's `serve` announces HERMES_BACKEND_READY and the port keeps LISTENING - Clicking the profile never dials the backend: target port has 0 ESTABLISHED connections (a working profile shows active WS connections) - Renderer console is silent — the failure is swallowed by the empty `.catch(() => {})` at the end of `ensureGatewayProfile` (store/profile.ts), which comments "the user can retry the switch" but the retry never works because `gatewaySwitch` is a module-global promise: once one switch hangs, every later `ensureGatewayProfile` awaits the same never-settling promise at the serialization point ## Suspected root cause `Promise.all([resolveConnectionForProfile(target), prepareGatewayForProfile(target)])` never settles (or `activate()` returns false on an epoch mismatch) and the rejection/hang is swallowed, leaving `gatewaySwitch` permanently pending. The new "rejected activation publishes NOTHING" guard (4e520f08) turns a failed/busy activation into a silent no-op with no retry path. Happy to run any diagnostic or test a proposed fix on this Windows machine.

signal.title: TUI and dashboard rebuild/reinstall on every launch — monorepo workspace lockfile mismatch
signal.text: ## Bug Description `hermes dashboard` and `hermes --tui` trigger a full TUI npm install and/or frontend rebuild on **every launch**, even when nothing has changed. This adds 30–120s of cold-start time. There are **three independent but related** causes: ### 1. `_tui_need_npm_install` — workspace lockfile scope mismatch `_tui_need_npm_install()` compares the root `package-lock.json` (1505 packages, covering ALL workspaces: desktop, web, bootstrap-installer, etc.) against `node_modules/.package-lock.json` (795 packages, only what `npm ci --workspace ui-tui` installed). The comparison finds ~490 "missing" packages that belong to other workspaces, and returns `True` on every launch. The content-based comparison was added to fix a previous mtime false-positive (see comment at line 1397), but it does not account for npm workspace scoped installs where the hidden lock only reflects the installed subset. ### 2. `_tui_need_rebuild` — `package-lock.json` in build inputs `_TUI_BUILD_INPUT_FILES` includes `"package-lock.json"`. The `_tui_need_rebuild()` function compares these inputs by mtime against `dist/entry.js`. Since `npm run build` updates `package-lock.json`, the dist is always "stale" after a build → rebuild loop. ### 3. `_web_ui_build_needed` — same `package-lock.json` mtime issue `_web_ui_build_needed()` checks if root `package-lock.json` is newer than `hermes_cli/web_dist/`. Same loop as #2: `npm run build` updates the lockfile → always stale → rebuild every time. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. `git clone` hermes-agent, `uv pip install -e .`, `npm install` 2. Run `hermes dashboard` — observe "Installing TUI dependencies…" and/or frontend rebuild 3. Quit, run `hermes dashboard` again — same thing happens ## Expected Behavior - TUI npm install should only run when `@hermes/ink` is actually missing or its version changed - Dashboard/TUI rebuild should only run when source files changed, not when `package-lock.json` was updated by the build itself ## Environment - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 - Python: 3.11.15 (uv-managed venv) - Node.js: v22.22.0 - Hermes Agent: v0.16.0 (editable install via `uv pip install -e .`) ## Root Cause The monorepo has npm workspaces (desktop, web, bootstrap-installer, shared, ui-tui). A scoped `npm ci --workspace ui-tui` only installs ~795 of the 1505 packages in the root lockfile. The staleness checks were written for a single-package layout and do not account for this gap. ## Suggested Fix 1. **`_tui_need_npm_install`**: The `@hermes/ink` sentinel (line 1423) already validates the critical TUI dependency. Replace the full lockfile content comparison with a simple mtime check against the hidden lockfile, relying on the ink sentinel for actual dependency validation. 2. **`_TUI_BUILD_INPUT_FILES`**: Remove `"package-lock.json"` — changes to dependencies are already captured by `"package.json"`. 3. **`_web_ui_build_needed`**: Remove the root `package-lock.json` mtime check (lines 4468–4471) — same reasoning.

signal.title: feat(bedrock): support service_tier and performanceConfig for cost/latency control
signal.text: Bedrock's Converse API accepts `serviceTier` and `performanceConfig` as top-level request fields, but Hermes never passed them through. This means users who relied on `service_tier=flex` in OpenClaw (or other frameworks) lose that ~50% cost savings when they migrate to Hermes. ## What this adds Two new config keys under `bedrock:` in config.yaml: ```yaml bedrock: service_tier: flex # priority | default | flex | reserved latency: optimized # standard | optimized ``` Both are optional. When empty/omitted, Bedrock uses its defaults (standard tier, standard latency). The values flow through the full stack: ``` config.yaml -> runtime_provider -> agent_init -> chat_completion_helpers -> transport -> build_converse_kwargs -> boto3 converse() ``` ## Files changed - `hermes_cli/config.py` -- new config keys with docs - `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` -- read config, attach to runtime dict - `agent/agent_init.py` -- store on agent at init time - `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` -- pass to transport - `agent/transports/bedrock.py` -- forward to build_converse_kwargs - `agent/bedrock_adapter.py` -- emit `serviceTier` and `performanceConfig` in API kwargs - `tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py` -- 4 new tests ## Testing 125 bedrock_adapter tests passing (Python 3.11 + 3.14). Closes #31322

signal.title: fix(bedrock): inherit modalities from foundation models for inference profiles
signal.text: `discover_bedrock_models()` hardcodes inference profiles (`us.*`, `global.*`) to TEXT-only modalities. Foundation models report their real `inputModalities`/`outputModalities` from `ListFoundationModels`, but `ListInferenceProfiles` doesn't return that field, so the profile entries were just stamped with `["TEXT"]`. The practical effect: Claude profiles like `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` support IMAGE input, but they show up as text-only. Anything that filters models by vision capability in the `/model` picker silently drops them. ## Fix After foundation models are discovered, build a small `{model_id: modalities}` map. When walking the inference profiles, resolve each one back to its base foundation model and inherit those modalities: 1. Pull the model ID out of the profile's ARN (`arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/<id>`) 2. If there's no ARN, strip the regional prefix (`us.anthropic.claude-v2` -> `anthropic.claude-v2`) 3. If neither resolves, keep the TEXT-only default ## Tests Three new cases in `TestInferenceProfileModalityInheritance` -- ARN-based inheritance, the regional-prefix fallback, and the no-match default. Full `test_bedrock_adapter.py` passes (121 tests) on Python 3.11. Reported by @ptlally in #7920.

signal.title: Telegram typing indicator reappears during genuinely idle windows in long-running sessions
signal.text: ## Bug Description The Telegram "typing…" indicator sticks/reappears intermittently even when the agent is completely idle (no active turn, no tool calls, no API calls in flight). It is not permanently stuck — it clears briefly during interactive prompts (e.g. while a `clarify` button is awaiting the user's tap) but reappears afterward with no corresponding agent activity in the logs. `/stop` does clear it once when invoked, confirming the underlying mechanism *can* be cleared, but it recurs on its own afterward without any new inbound message or agent activity. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Run a long-lived Telegram DM session with the agent (observed at ~300K+ tokens of conversation history, many prior turns). 2. Have a turn complete normally (final response delivered, confirmed via `gateway.run: response ready` log line). 3. Wait ~1-3 minutes with no further interaction. 4. Observe the Telegram chat header: the "typing…" indicator is visible despite zero agent activity in `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` during that window. 5. Sending `/stop` clears it for that instance, but it returns on a subsequent idle window. ## Expected Behavior Typing indicator should only be visible while the agent is actively processing a turn (API calls in flight, tool execution, or streaming a response), and should reliably clear the moment `gateway.run: response ready` fires — with no reappearance until a new inbound message starts a new turn. ## Actual Behavior Typing indicator reappears during idle windows with no corresponding log activity for the session. Suspected root cause candidates identified via static code review (not confirmed via live debugger attach): - `agent/turn_finalizer.py` spawns a background review thread (`_spawn_background_review`, comment: *"runs AFTER the response is delivered so it never competes with the user's task for model attention"*) that forks a new `AIAgent` and runs asynchronously in a separate thread named `bg-review`. This fork is invisible to the user (no visible response expected in the common case), but its execution window may overlap with the `run_generation`/typing-refresh bookkeeping in `gateway/run.py`, and if any refresh call outlives the true end of the visible turn, this could explain the observed reappearance. - The typing-refresh loop in `gateway/run.py` (`send_typing` calls around lines ~4727, ~4813, ~27151) is guarded by `ctx._run_still_current()` / `self._is_session_run_current(session_key, run_generation)`, which appears correctly designed to stop stale refreshes — but I was not able to fully trace whether the background-review thread's lifecycle is bound to the same `run_generation` token or has its own untracked typing calls. I want to flag explicitly: the above is code-reading analysis, not a confirmed root cause from a live repro with debugger attached. Happy to provide full session logs privately if that helps triage. ## Environment - Hermes Agent version: v0.20.2 (2026.8.16) - Platform: Telegram (DM) - Model: claude-sonnet-5, provider=anthropic - Session size at time of observation: ~296K-310K tokens, 400+ messages, long-running single session (not `/new`'d in a while) - Background review: enabled (default), triggered repeatedly during the session (visible in logs as `thread=bg-review`) - OS: macOS ## Additional context Log evidence (redacted chat id) showing idle gaps with no activity between a completed turn and the next inbound message, during which the indicator was reported stuck by the user: ``` 2026-08-19 07:57:17 INFO gateway.run: response ready: ... time=41.5s 2026-08-19 07:57:27 INFO gateway.platforms.base: [Telegram] Sending response (23 chars) ... 2026-08-19 07:58:12 INFO ... Cached user photo ... <- next inbound message, ~45s idle gap in between ``` User confirmed via live observation: indicator clears briefly *only* while an interactive `clarify` prompt is pending (user attention genuinely required, agent genuinely idle), then reappears once that resolves — even with zero subsequent inbound messages. Related to the documented "phantom is thinking" issue referenced in `gateway/slash_commands.py` (comment cites issue #32295) — that fix (`/stop` force-clearing on no-active-agent) does address a one-shot clear, but does not appear to prevent recurrence in a still-idle session.

signal.title: fix(tools): clarify execute_code terminal approval guidance
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Clarifies the approval interaction between direct `terminal` calls, `execute_code` wrappers, and raw subprocesses so the model does not wrap a single command to avoid review. A one-command `execute_code` wrapper obscures the command's intent and, in gateway/ask sessions, adds whole-script approval. A wrapped `hermes_tools.terminal()` call still runs the normal terminal command-level checks, while raw subprocess commands cannot be inspected individually. The schema therefore recommends calling `terminal` directly for one command. Interactive CLI sessions are not claimed to add an outer approval prompt. The standalone terminal schema carries equivalent generic guidance without naming `execute_code`, so it remains valid when the code-execution toolset is disabled. The `execute_code` schema names `terminal` only when that tool is actually enabled. ## Related Issue Fixes #52738 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [x] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `tools/code_execution_tool.py`: adds one precise, dynamically gated warning against single-command terminal/subprocess wrappers, with gateway/ask approval scope stated explicitly. - `tools/terminal_tool.py`: recommends direct terminal use for one command using cross-tool-safe, deployment-neutral wording. - `tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py`: covers the registered schema, both execution modes, mutually exclusive tool-availability branches, no duplicate guidance, terminal-disabled sessions, and an explicitly empty tool set. - `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py`: pins the standalone terminal guidance and absence of a hard-coded `execute_code` reference. ## How to Test 1. Run the focused approval/schema suites: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_code_execution.py tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py ``` Result: 144 passed. 2. Run static and cross-platform checks: ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check tools/code_execution_tool.py tools/terminal_tool.py tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py .venv/bin/python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py tools/code_execution_tool.py tools/terminal_tool.py tests/tools/test_code_execution_modes.py tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py git diff --check origin/main...HEAD ``` Result: Ruff passed, no Windows footguns found, diff check clean. 3. Duplicate-work checks: ```bash gh pr list --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --state all --search "52738" gh pr list --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --state all --search "execute_code terminal approval inner shell command schema guidance" ``` Both searches find no competing implementation. ## 2026-07-11 shepherding refresh Rebased both original human-authored commits onto current `main` (`6142203bd7`) after 2,217 upstream commits. Current main still lacks this approval-interaction guidance, so #52738 remains reproducible. Two private Grogu passes identified and this refresh repaired four concrete gaps in the original branch: duplicate wording inside the `execute_code` schema, an imprecise claim that wrapped `hermes_tools.terminal()` calls skip command-level checks, the missing standalone-terminal side of #52738, and an overbroad claim that whole-script approval applies outside gateway/ask contexts. Commit `b1fcac808` contains those corrections and expanded contract coverage. The issue's suggested inline annotation was implemented as a single paragraph before the available-tools list instead: this avoids repeating the same paid schema guidance beside the terminal stub while keeping it visible before tool selection. The existing user-facing approval-dialog text in `check_execute_code_guard` remains unchanged because it is constructed only after the gateway/ask gates where its one-shot description is accurate. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix - [x] I've run focused tests and all pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant tool descriptions/schemas are updated - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update N/A - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` update N/A - [x] Cross-platform impact considered and checked - [x] No dependency or configuration changes ## Screenshots / Logs Not applicable; this is model-facing schema guidance covered by tests.

signal.title: [Bug]: shared primary profile routes reload session history from the root store after #88734
signal.text: ## Bug Description A shared primary messaging adapter routed to a secondary profile under `gateway.multiplex_profiles` creates a split session after the scope-aware DB fix from #88734: - gateway routing/session metadata is read from the root/default `state.db`; - the routed `AIAgent` persists the real transcript to the secondary profile's `state.db`; - every following turn reloads an empty history from the root store, so the bot has same-session amnesia. This reproduces on current `main` (`e02d1e41fc`) with the default profile owning one WhatsApp/Baileys connection and an exact `gateway.profile_routes` rule routing a group to a secondary profile whose own WhatsApp adapter is disabled. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Enable `gateway.multiplex_profiles` on the default gateway. 2. Let the default profile own a shared primary WhatsApp adapter. 3. Add an exact `profile_routes` entry mapping one WhatsApp group to a served secondary profile. 4. Send a first message that causes several tool calls and a final response. 5. Reply in the same group with a follow-up that depends on the prior turn. 6. Inspect `agent.log` and both SQLite stores. Observed log shape on every follow-up: ```text Agent cache invalidated ... message_count changed (1 -> N), possible cross-process write conversation turn: session=<same-id> ... history=0 ``` For the same session id, the root store contained one metadata row while the secondary profile store contained the full transcript (64 rows in the live reproduction). No compression ran or failed. ## Expected Behavior After route resolution and authorization, session creation, transcript loading, turn leases, and agent persistence should all resolve the same secondary-profile store. A follow-up turn should receive the prior conversation history. The primary adapter's owner-scoped authorization/secret gate should remain under the default profile; only the routed conversation/session lifecycle should enter the target profile scope. ## Actual Behavior The first routed turn answers correctly because `_run_agent()` enters the secondary profile scope. The next turn calls `async_session_store.load_transcript()` while the shared primary handler is still pinned to the default profile, returns no replayable messages, and passes `conversation_history=[]` to the agent. A representative conversation became: ```text assistant: [returns the requested account] user: activate that account with the quarterly plan assistant: several accounts match; which exact one? user: [exact account name] assistant: what do you need for that account? ``` The last response occurred because the model only received the current message and quoted reply, not the preceding activation request. ## Affected Component Gateway (WhatsApp), Agent Core session history, multi-profile routing. ## Messaging Platform WhatsApp (the bug shape applies to any shared primary adapter using `profile_routes`). ## Debug Report A public debug upload is intentionally omitted because the live logs and transcript contain private business/account data. The reproduction evidence was collected locally from `agent.log`, `gateway.log`, and both SQLite stores, with identifiers redacted above. A hermetic regression test against temporary profile homes will accompany the PR. ## Operating System macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) ## Python Version Python 3.11.15 ## Hermes Version Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), current main `e02d1e41fc` ## Root Cause Analysis #88734 correctly changed `SessionStore._db` and `GatewayRunner._session_db` to resolve the active `HERMES_HOME` scope per access. Its invariant is sound, but the shared-primary route reaches the profile scope too late: 1. `_make_default_profile_message_handler()` intentionally pins the whole ingress/auth path to the default home (introduced by `76cf19fee1` so the primary adapter's token and prompt gate remain owner-scoped). 2. `_handle_message()` resolves/stamps `source.profile`, then calls `_handle_message_with_agent()` while still in that default scope. 3. `_handle_message_with_agent()` calls `get_or_create_session()` and `load_transcript()` before `_run_agent()`. 4. `_run_agent()` is the first point that enters `_profile_runtime_scope(_resolve_profile_home_for_source(source))`. 5. Therefore the gateway-side session lifecycle reads/writes root, while `AIAgent` writes the transcript to the routed profile. The existing `test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py` tests direct access inside an already-active profile override. It does not cover the shared-primary adapter path where the active scope remains default until the agent call. ## Proposed Fix Add a routed-profile wrapper around `_handle_message_with_agent()` (after ingress authorization and route stamping, before any session-store access), keeping its current implementation in an inner method. This scopes the complete session lifecycle without moving primary-adapter authorization/secret checks out of the owner profile. Add regression coverage that: - starts from the default/root scope; - routes a source to a secondary profile; - proves the session/runner DB handles seen by the inner turn are the secondary profile's handles; - proves the test fails with the wrapper removed; - keeps multiplex-off and primary/default routing behavior unchanged. ## Related Work / Duplicate Sweep - #88532 / #88734 fixed frozen-at-init DB handles and established physical per-profile stores. - #66887 tracks the broader historical storage-scope problem. - #69042 originally explored shared-WhatsApp profile isolation but narrowed to adapter startup only. - No open PR found for this post-#88734 residual shared-primary history-loading seam. ## PR - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR.

signal.title: fix(plugins): stop the security scanner from reading test trees
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? `plugin_guard` scans the whole plugin clone (`plugin_dir.rglob("*")`), and `EXCLUDED_DIRS` skipped caches and vendored dirs — but not `tests/`. A security-conscious plugin's test suite **should** contain adversarial fixtures: a test asserting the trust boundary holds round-trips the injection string verbatim, and the scanner reads it as the attack it is testing for. Any single `critical` finding makes the verdict `dangerous`, which `--force` explicitly cannot override — so scanning tests made exactly the plugins that test their security **unconditionally uninstallable** (#89610, reported downstream as yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin#67: a plugin with 3 criticals, 2 of them in test files, went from `dangerous` (cannot install) to `caution` (installs with confirmation) purely by excluding the test tree). The only workaround was obfuscating the payload strings (concatenating fragments so the scanner misses them) — which weakens real tests, teaches authors to hide strings from the scanner, and inverts the incentive: plugins that test their trust boundary get punished relative to plugins that don't test at all. Test fixtures are never loaded into an agent's context at runtime the way `README` or `plugin.yaml` are — the same distinction `CODE_EXEMPT_PATTERN_IDS` already draws for code files. This PR adds the conventional test-tree names (`tests`, `test`, `testing`, `spec`, `specs`, `fixtures`) to `EXCLUDED_DIRS`, alongside the existing cache/vendored skips. Production-code findings — including every critical in shipped code — are untouched and still fail closed exactly as before. ## Related Issue Fixes #89610 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `tools/plugin_guard.py` — `EXCLUDED_DIRS` gains the test/spec/fixture directory names, with a comment stating why fixtures are categorically different from shipped docs/config (never loaded into an agent's context; adversarial content is their purpose). - `tests/tools/test_plugin_guard.py` — `test_adversarial_test_fixtures_are_skipped`: a plugin whose `tests/` holds the issue's exact injection fixture (and a `spec/support fixtures/` file) still scans `safe` (fails on main: the fixture's `prompt_injection_ignore` critical makes the verdict `dangerous`). ## How to Test ```bash python -m pytest tests/tools/test_plugin_guard.py -q # Observed result: 16 passed python -m pytest tests/run_agent/test_authorization_gate.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py -q # Observed result: 80 passed ``` Fail-on-main check: with the guard change stashed, the new fixture test fails on main (`verdict == "dangerous"` from the test-file critical). Manual repro from the issue: scan a `git archive` of a plugin whose tests assert the trust boundary — on main the verdict is `dangerous` (uninstallable even with `--force`); with this change the test tree is skipped and the verdict reflects shipped code only. ## Checklist - [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines - [x] Self-review completed - [x] Comments explain intent (why fixtures are categorically different from shipped files) - [x] Corresponding changes documented via comments - [x] Tests added and passing (1 new; guard + plugin suites green) - [x] Single root cause, no unrelated changes

signal.title: fix(install): retry the HTTPS clone and degrade past repo-scoped 429s
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? GitHub throttles packfile generation **for this repository** with repo-scoped HTTP 429s that are not client IP rate limits: at the same moment an anonymous clone of a small public repo succeeds and `api.github.com/rate_limit` reports a full quota, but the single big pack behind `git clone --depth 1` dies mid-transfer with `RPC failed; HTTP 429 / expected 'packfile'` (#89624 — the repo is large at HEAD plus the thousands of auto-generated branches `install.sh`'s own comments call out; the same throttle hits the update path per #89287). The fresh-install `clone_repo()` HTTPS branch had **no retry and no fallback**: a clean unauthenticated machine exited 1 at the download stage and left a half-populated `~/.hermes` (`bin/`, `skills/`, `config.yaml`, no checkout). This PR makes the HTTPS clone stage degrade gracefully: 1. **Retry with backoff** — up to 4 direct attempts, sleeping `attempt × 5s` between them; each failed attempt removes its partial clone first (git refuses to clone into a non-empty directory). 2. **Blobless-partial fallback** — when every direct attempt fails, clone with `--filter=blob:none --single-branch` and materialize the working tree with `git reset --hard HEAD` (retried once). The server builds many small packs instead of one big one, which is exactly what got past the throttle in the issue's confirmed workaround. The hard reset is required: the partial clone's checkout contains missing-content placeholders until it runs. Unchanged: SSH-first ordering (fast-fail via `BatchMode`), the existing-installation update branch, and the `--commit` pin flow (the pin operates on whatever HEAD the clone produced). ## Related Issue Fixes #89624 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `scripts/install.sh` — `clone_repo()`'s HTTPS branch: bounded retry loop with backoff and inter-attempt cleanup, then the blobless-partial fallback with a (retried) hard reset to materialize the tree; comments name the throttle shape and why the fallback works. - `tests/test_install_clone_throttle_fallback.py` — new contract suite (text-contract style of the neighboring install tests): the retry loop with backoff exists; failed direct attempts clean the partial clone; the `--filter=blob:none` fallback + `git reset --hard HEAD` materialization exists; the fallback is gated on all direct attempts failing; the both-fail path still reports and exits 1. ## How to Test ```bash bash -n scripts/install.sh # Observed result: no syntax errors python -m pytest tests/test_install_clone_throttle_fallback.py -q # Observed result: 4 passed python -m pytest tests/test_install_no_initial_commit.py tests/test_install_autostash_conflict_recovery.py tests/test_install_diverged_update.py -q # Observed result: 8 passed, 1 skipped (neighboring clone/install contracts unchanged) ``` Fail-on-main check: with the installer change stashed, all four new tests fail on main (no retry loop, no fallback, no cleanup between attempts).
