signal.title: feat(gateway): add P2P federation heartbeat for multi-device task relay
signal.text: ## feat(gateway): P2P federation — heartbeat, task relay, and Phase 24 Sweeper review fixes Peer-to-peer federation for multi-device Hermes: heartbeat, offline task relay with consensus, capability-based routing, and an operational layer (health monitoring + aircraft-lost SOS) so the federation actively keeps every member healthy. > **Status: 23 phases complete. SSH-verified on 2 real devices over Tailscale (MacBook Pro controller ↔ Mac Mini member). 220 unit tests pass. CI clean (all 30 check runs green).** --- ## What this PR adds ### Core federation (Phases 1-21) - **Heartbeat + death detection** — every device broadcasts liveness; a peer is confirmed dead after 3 consecutive failures (CRITICAL-3, avoids false positives). - **Task relay with Raft-lite consensus** — offline device's tasks are atomically claimed by surviving peers (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` closes the TOCTOU race); progress streamed via checkpoints so a relayed task resumes from the last checkpoint. - **Discovery** — `auto` mode uses mDNS (stdlib socket, zero deps); `lan` mode uses explicit peer WebSocket URLs. No Tailscale required for LAN use. - **Capability matching + compute pool** — GPU/CPU/memory-aware routing. - **Security** — TLS (self-signed OK for LAN), HMAC-SHA256 message signing, auth_token, IP whitelist, audit log with HMAC chain, secret store. ### Phase 22 — Ops layer The federation now *operates* the fleet, not just relays tasks: 1. **Health monitoring (`HealthMonitor`)** - Every heartbeat carries a health snapshot: gateway_up, federation_connected, cpu_load, memory, disk_free, hermes_version. - Weighted `health_score` (0..1) per peer; full matrix via ops API. 2. **Lost-contact SOS (`LostContactSOS`) — "aircraft lost" escalation** - Escalation windows: `soft (<60s)` → `confirmed (<300s)` → `critical (>=300s)`. - Each escalation broadcasts an `OPS_ALERT` to surviving peers; on revival a `recovery` alert fires automatically. - `on_assist` hook lets operators plug remote-recovery actions (SSH probe, remote gateway restart on the lost host). 3. **Stable connectivity** - **Fixed:** outbound peer connections now use a permissive *client* TLS context for LAN self-signed certs. The server context has no CA chain, so verifying against it failed across machines (`CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`). Peer auth stays enforced via auth_token + message signing. - Exponential backoff reconnect (2^retry, max 10) preserved; latency tracked. 4. **New message types:** `OPS_HEALTH`, `OPS_ALERT`, `OPS_SOS`, `OPS_ASSIST_ACK`. 5. **New API endpoints** (auth-protected): - `GET /api/federation/ops/health` — per-peer health matrix - `GET /api/federation/ops/alerts` — recent ops alerts - `GET /api/federation/ops/summary` — aggregate fleet overview ### Bug fixes carried from real-device deployment While deploying v3 across two machines these merge bugs were found & fixed: - `compute_score` was used as an attribute instead of a method; `FederationComputePool` gained a proper `compute_score()`. - `FederationAdapter.send()` was missing (cluster/leader-election call it) — added delegate to the connection manager. - `_federation_config` ref removed in favor of `getattr(config, 'api_port', 18766)`. - `load_gateway_config()` now maps the `federation:` section (was silently dropped → gateway never started federation). - `gateway/run.py` passes `require_auth/tls_cert/tls_key/ip_whitelist` to the adapter (previously `TLS=no` even with `require_tls: true`); federation start errors now log at `error` level instead of debug. --- ### Phase 24 — Sweeper Review Fixes **Automated review findings** from the upstream agent sweep — all resolved: | # | Finding | Status | Detail | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `FederationConfig` missing `resolve_db_path()` | ❌ Outdated | Already defined in `config.py:2806` | | 2 | `_claim_task()` only logs, no dispatch | ✅ Fixed | v1: logs only; v2/v3: `adapter.claim_and_execute()` called | | 3 | TOCTOU — idle-check before `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` | ✅ Fixed | `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` moved to first statement (Phase 21) | | 4 | Config types inconsistent; no e2e tests | ✅ Acknowledged | Startup integration test added (see E2E section) | | 5 | Task relay has no Kanban dispatcher bridge | ✅ Fixed | `_default_handler()` now creates a Kanban task (`initial_status='ready'`) — local `_kanban_dispatcher_watcher` picks it up and spawns a real worker | | 6 | Dual-writer SQLite in `shared_db` v1 | ✅ Fixed | Single-writer election via advisory lock file (`federation.db.writer.lock`); only the elected writer runs `_detect_offline()` + `_claim_task()` | **Two architectural improvements from Phase 24:** *Federation → Kanban bridge* (`federation_relay.py:_default_handler`): Federated tasks are now backed by real Kanban tasks. The handler creates a Kanban task with the federation `task_id` as idempotency key (`fed:<id>`) and `initial_status='ready'`. The local `_kanban_dispatcher_watcher` detects the ready task on its next tick and calls `dispatch_once()` → `spawn_fn` → real worker. This keeps federation and Kanban fully decoupled while sharing the execution pool. *Single-writer SQLite* (`federation_heartbeat.py:_run_shared_db_loop`): `shared_db` v1 mode now elects one writer via `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` on a separate lock file. The elected writer runs `_detect_offline()` and `_claim_task()`. Non-writers only call `_heartbeat()` (read-mostly). A stale lock (>5 min without a heartbeat) is seized by the next writer candidate — transparent failover. --- ## Who should enable this Federation is for you if you run Hermes on **more than one machine** and want: - Tasks that were running on a machine that went offline **resume automatically** on another machine in your fleet - A **fleet-wide ops dashboard** showing every machine's health, connectivity, and alerts - **Zero-config peer discovery** (on LAN or Tailscale) without manually configuring IP addresses You can wait if you only run Hermes on one machine, or if you don't need task continuity when a machine goes offline. --- ## Platform compatibility | Platform | Federation mode | Secret storage | Health snapshot | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | **macOS** | `auto` (mDNS), `lan`, `shared_db` | macOS Keychain ✅ | ✅ CPU, RAM, disk | Full support | | **Linux** | `auto` (mDNS), `lan`, `shared_db` | Encrypted file fallback ✅ | ✅ CPU, RAM, disk | Full support | | **Windows** | `lan` only (mDNS not supported) | Encrypted file fallback ✅ | ✅ CPU, RAM, disk | `auto` auto-falls back to `lan` | > **mDNS note:** `auto` mode uses UDP multicast on `224.0.0.251:5353`. This works natively on macOS and Linux. On Windows it falls back to `lan` mode automatically — no manual change needed. ### Platform-specific notes - **macOS Keychain** — `federation.cluster_secret` is stored in your login Keychain via the `security` CLI. You will be prompted to allow access on first use. - **Linux** — Falls back to an AES-256-GCM encrypted file at `~/.hermes/federation/secrets.db`. No keyring daemon required. - **Windows** — mDNS (Zeroconf) is not available natively. Federation detects this and switches to `lan` mode automatically. Use explicit `peers:` URLs or Tailscale. - **`shared_db` mode** — Uses a SQLite file synced via file-sharing (iCloud Drive on macOS, SMB on Windows, NFS on Linux). **Not required for v2/v3** — only use it if you prefer file-based sync over WebSocket connections. --- ## Quick-start guide ### Step 1 — Enable federation Add to your `config.yaml`: ```yaml federation: enabled: true mode: auto # recommended for most users auth_token: your-secret-token ws_port: 18765 require_auth: true tls_cert: ~/.hermes/fed/cert.pem tls_key: ~/.hermes/fed/key.pem ``` ### Step 2 — Generate TLS certificates ```bash # Create the cert directory mkdir -p ~/.hermes/fed # Generate a self-signed certificate (valid for LAN use) openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:prime256v1 \\ -keyout ~/.hermes/fed/key.pem \\ -out ~/.hermes/fed/cert.pem \\ -days 365 -nodes \\ -subj "/CN=federation" ``` > Self-signed certs work fine on LAN. For Tailscale or VPN-based setups, you can also use Tailscale WireGuard or Let's Encrypt certificates. ### Step 3 — Choose your discovery mode | Your setup | Recommended mode | What to set | |---|---|---| | Machines on the **same LAN** | `auto` | No additional config needed — mDNS finds peers automatically | | Machines on **Tailscale VPN** | `lan` | Set `peers: ["wss://<tailscale-ip>:18765"]` on each machine | | Machines on **different LANs** | `lan` | Same as above, use public IP or domain with port-forwarding | | **2–3 machines**, simple setup | `shared_db` | Set `db_path: ~/hermes-federation/federation.db` (iCloud Drive / SMB / NFS) | ### Step 4 — Restart and verify ```bash # Restart your gateway hermes gateway restart # Check federation status hermes federation status # Expected output: # { # "mode": "auto", # "device_id": "my-macbook", # "peers": [ # { # "device_id": "mac-mini", # "status": "online", # "health_score": 1.0 # } # ] # } ``` ### Step 5 — (Optional) Enable ops alerts ```yaml federation: # ... other config above on_lost_contact: notify # or "relay" to auto-relay tasks ``` --- ## Verifying end-to-end ### Simulate a peer going offline ```bash # On machine B (the peer), stop the gateway hermes gateway stop # On machine A (the controller), within 30s you should see: # - ops alert in dashboard: "peer mac-mini → confirmed offline" # - tasks from machine B are offered to other peers ``` ### Test task relay Create a long-running task on machine A, then stop machine A's gateway. The task should resume on machine B within `offline_threshold_s` (default: 30s). ### Check audit log ```bash hermes federation audit --peer mac-mini --since 1h ``` --- ## Troubleshooting | Problem | Likely cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | Peers not discovered | mDNS blocked by firewall | Open UDP 5353, or switch to `lan` mode with explicit peer URLs | | TLS handshake fails | Self-signed cert not trusted | Ensure `tls_cert` is the same file on all machines, or set `allow_insecure: true` for testing | | Auth rejected | `auth_token` mismatch | Ensure `auth_token` is identical on all peers | | `shared_db` mode not syncing | File not accessible | Check that the SQLite file is reachable from all machines (iCloud Drive, SMB, NFS) | | Windows: no peers found | mDNS not supported | Use `lan` mode with explicit `peers:` list | | Health score shows 0.0 on Linux | `getloadavg()` not available | This is normal — the score degrades gracefully to 0.0; federation still works | --- ## Config ```yaml federation: enabled: true mode: auto # auto (mDNS) | lan (explicit peers) | shared_db (v1) ws_port: 18765 auth_token: <shared-secret> require_auth: true tls_cert: ~/.hermes/fed/cert.pem # self-signed OK for LAN tls_key: ~/.hermes/fed/key.pem offline_threshold_s: 30 heartbeat_interval_s: 60 peers: [] # lan mode: ["wss://<PEER_IP>:18765"] ``` --- ## Tests - `tests/gateway/test_federation_phase{3,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,16}.py` — core phases. - `tests/gateway/test_federation_ops.py` — Phase 22: health monitor, death+revival, SOS escalation, local health collection (4 tests). - `tests/gateway/test_federation_heartbeat.py` — heartbeat + death detector. - `tests/gateway/test_federation_v2.py` — v2 protocol tests. - **Total: 220 tests, all pass.** ### Field verification (real devices, Tailscale LAN) ``` MacBook Pro (controller) ↔ Mac Mini (peer), mode=lan, wss://, TLS + auth: - WS connect OK, TLS handshake OK - Peer visible in controller ops matrix: {<MEMBER_HOST>: {federation_connected: true, health_score: 1.0}} - Heartbeat health snapshots flowing every 60s ``` --- ## Security design - TLS mandatory by default (`require_tls: true`); `allow_insecure` opt-in only. - HMAC-SHA256 signature over `msg_id:msg_type:timestamp:payload` — verified on both inbound and outbound paths. - auth_token + `X-Federation-Auth` header; IP whitelist; rate limiting. - Audit log with HMAC chain (20 event types). - Outbound TLS uses a permissive client context ONLY for LAN self-signed certs; peer authenticity is enforced by signed messages, not TLS chain alone.

signal.title: fix(browser): keep agent-browser as a managed Hermes dependency
signal.text:
## Problem

Hermes treated agent-browser as npx-only while CLI-backed consumers such as scheduled Fidelity acquisition required a stable executable on PATH. Workspace refreshes could remove a local install or leave a dangling global link, causing cron failures before browser work began.

## Change

- install agent-browser into Hermes' managed Node prefix during setup
- let dependency reconciliation and doctor repair/flag the managed CLI
- keep agent-browser outside the workspace dependency graph

signal.title: fix(update): --stay-on-branch so desktop product updates end on main
signal.text: ## Who should enable this Users of **Hermes Desktop** (the packaged app, macOS/Linux) whose install lives in a git checkout that sits on a non-main (feature) branch: - Desktop Update button reports success but the app never advances past the old version - `hermes version` keeps saying "Update available: N commits behind" after clicking Update - You develop on feature branches but use the Desktop product for daily driving — updates must end on main, not strand on your WIP branch CLI-only users are unaffected unless they opt into `--stay-on-branch` (the flag is additive; default CLI behavior is unchanged). ## Platform compatibility | Platform | Compatibility | |---|---| | macOS | ✅ Target platform (in-app updater + CLI update path) | | Linux | ✅ Compatible (same POSIX in-app updater path) | | Windows | ✅ Unchanged (Windows uses the updater-exe hand-off path; no branch-pinning there) | ## Quick-start guide 1. `hermes update` (or pull this PR branch) 2. Desktop: click Update — the in-app updater now always passes `--branch <tracked> --stay-on-branch`, so the checkout ends on the tracked branch (default main) 3. CLI: to force the same behavior, run `hermes update --stay-on-branch` 4. Verify: after update, `git branch --show-current` shows the tracked branch (main), and the desktop build reflects the new code ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | Desktop stuck at old version after Update | Old behavior re-pinned to the feature branch | Upgrade to this fix; updater now stays on the tracked branch | | `hermes update --stay-on-branch` left WIP behind | Autostash preserved for manual recovery | Check `git stash list`; the pre-switch stash is kept intentionally | | CLI update switched back to feature branch | Default CLI behavior (no flag) | Use `--stay-on-branch` to stay on the target branch | | Desktop on Windows unchanged | Windows updater-exe path | Expected — no branch-pinning existed there | --- ## Summary Fix a real field bug: **Hermes Desktop can never update past the old version when the git checkout sits on a non-main (feature) branch.** The CLI update pipeline refreshes `main`, but the desktop update flow re-pins to the current branch and the post-update rebuild packages the stale feature-branch code. ## Problem (with evidence) A desktop user whose checkout was on `feat/aide-squared-evolution` observed: - `hermes update` (from the desktop Update button) reported success every time, - the packaged desktop app never advanced (stuck at the old build), - `hermes version` kept reporting `Update available: 528 commits behind`. Root cause is a 3-link chain: 1. **CLI**: `hermes update` switches back to the pre-update branch after pulling ("keep me where I was working" — correct for a developer CLI, wrong for a product updater). The switch-back lives in the `commit_count == 0` path of `_cmd_update_impl` (`git checkout current_branch`). 2. **Desktop in-app updater**: `applyUpdatesPosixInApp` *branch-pinned* the update to whatever branch the checkout was on, so on a non-main checkout it told `hermes update --branch <feature>` to update the *feature branch*, not `main`. 3. **Rebuild**: `hermes desktop --build-only` runs *after* the update, so it packaged the stale feature-branch code — the desktop binary never contained the new `main` code. ## Fix | Area | Change | |---|---| | CLI `hermes update` | New `--stay-on-branch` flag: after the update the checkout **stays on the update target branch** (default `main`) instead of switching back. Any stash created by the pre-switch autostash is **preserved for manual recovery** rather than auto-applied onto the target branch (auto-applying would contaminate `main` with feature-branch WIP). | | Desktop in-app updater (macOS/Linux) | `applyUpdatesPosixInApp` no longer branch-pins to the current checkout. It always passes `--branch <tracked> --stay-on-branch`, where `<tracked>` is the configured update branch (default `main`, self-healed via existing `resolveHealedBranch`). | | Desktop manual-command fallback | The no-staged-updater path surfaces the same explicit command (`hermes update --branch main --stay-on-branch`) instead of branch-pinning the displayed one-liner. | **Developer CLI behavior is unchanged**: plain `hermes update` still returns you to the branch you started on, with stash auto-restore exactly as before. The new flag is opt-in and only the desktop passes it. ## Safety design - **Stash contamination guard**: when `--stay-on-branch` ends on a different branch than the pre-update HEAD, the autostash is *not* re-applied (that would write feature-branch WIP onto `main`). The user gets explicit recovery guidance: `git stash apply <ref>` on their branch. Both the `commit_count == 0` path and the `commit_count > 0` finally path honor this. - **No remote mutation**: this change only alters local checkout/branch handling; it never pushes, force-pushes, or rewrites history. - **Existing self-heal kept**: `resolveHealedBranch` still falls back to `main` when the configured branch no longer exists on origin. ## Tests / self-test CLI (`tests/hermes_cli/test_cmd_update.py`, 3 new tests): 1. default behavior still switches back to the feature branch; 2. `--stay-on-branch` updates main and does **not** switch back; 3. with a stash present, `--stay-on-branch` keeps it (no `_restore_stashed_changes` call) and prints `git stash apply` guidance. Ran: - `pytest test_cmd_update.py test_update_autostash.py test_update_yes_flag.py test_update_post_pull_syntax_guard.py test_update_venv_health.py test_update_hangup_protection.py` → **49 passed** - `ruff check` on changed Python files → clean - `tsc -p . --noEmit` + `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit` → clean - `eslint electron/main.ts` → clean - `vitest run --project electron` → 937 passed / 1 failed. The one failure (`git-review-ops` untracked-dir payload) **reproduces with this change stashed** — a local-git-environment artifact (git version behavior on untracked dirs), not this change. ## Verification on a real checkout The bug was reproduced and fixed on the reporter's actual machine: after `hermes update --branch main --stay-on-branch`, `hermes version` went from `v0.19.1 · 528 commits behind` to `v0.20.0 · Up to date`, and the packaged desktop was rebuilt from current `main`.

signal.title: Bug Report: Hermes Client cancels local LLM streams after ~1.5s during prompt evaluation / reasoning (Triggering `<unused49>` token loop)
signal.text: ### Bug Report: Hermes Client cancels local LLM streams after ~1.5s during prompt evaluation / reasoning (Triggering `<unused49>` token loop) #### Summary Following a recent Hermes update, requests routed to a local Ollama backend fail consistently. Hermes issues a client-side cancellation (`cancel task`) after approximately 1.4 to 1.6 seconds while the local model is still evaluating the system prompt / generating initial reasoning chunks. This triggers a broken retry loop (4 continuation attempts) and outputs raw `<unused49>` token artifacts. Direct execution via the Ollama CLI (`ollama run`) runs without issues and produces complete, fluent responses. --- #### Environment - **Host OS:** Linux (x86_64) - **Client:** Hermes Agent (CLI `hermes chat` and Desktop Wrapper) both V 0.20.1 - **Backend:** Ollama (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`) - **Model:** Gemma 4 (26B) with custom parameters (`num_ctx 131072`, `num_predict 16384`) --- #### Timeline & Background 1. **Prior Stable State:** The setup ran out-of-the-box for days with fast response times (~50 tokens/s) and zero stream interruptions. 2. **Trigger:** A routine Hermes update was installed on the morning of August 15. No configurations in Ollama or the underlying GGUF/Modelfile were modified. 3. **Onset:** Beginning midday on August 15 and continuing to date, all chat sessions (CLI and GUI) fail immediately with stream truncation. --- #### Observed Behavior & Logs **Hermes Output:** ```text ● Hallo George, wie ist dein Status? Initializing agent... ──────────────────────────────────────── ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response truncated — stream ended before completion ⚠ Response still truncated after 4 continuation attempts — keeping the partial response received so far. <unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49><unused49>... Ollama Backend Log (journalctl -u ollama): Plaintext ollama[14322]: slot operator(): id 1 | task 64 | new prompt, n_ctx_slot = 131072, task.n_tokens = 16862 ollama[14322]: [GIN] | 200 | 1.621478725s | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/v1/chat/completions" ollama[14322]: srv stop: cancel task, id_task = 64 ollama[14322]: slot release: id 1 | task 64 | stop processing: n_tokens = 16894, truncated = 0 Root Cause Analysis Premature Client-Side Timeout / Empty-Chunk Dropping: Hermes sends a large system prompt (~17k tokens from tool schemas / core capabilities). Evaluating ~17k tokens on local hardware naturally takes 1.5–2.5 seconds before the first text token can be emitted. During this initial prefill/thinking window, the stream contains content: "" chunks (or reasoning deltas). Hermes interprets this as an abandoned stream and sends an active abort (cancel task) after ~1.5s. Context Corruption from Auto-Continuation: After the premature client abort, Hermes triggers 4 automated continuation attempts. Because the initial turn was severed mid-generation, the model context becomes corrupted, causing Gemma's tokenizer to emit separator token ID 49 (<unused49>). Expected Behavior Hermes must not drop or cancel active SSE streams during the prompt evaluation (prefill) or reasoning phase of local endpoints. Client-side first-token timeouts should be fully configurable or respect request_timeout / stream_timeout settings rather than enforcing a hardcoded ~1.5s threshold. Incomplete stream handling should fail gracefully instead of corrupting the context into an <unused49> continuation loop. Hermes is unusable this way!

signal.text: ## Bug In Bot Mode (desktop app with multiple bot profiles), the Routines (cron jobs) pane always shows the **default profile's** cron jobs regardless of which bot is selected in the roster. ## Setup - 7 profiles configured as bots via `ui_meta.hermes-bots` in `profile.yaml` - 4 bot profiles (blog-writer, apk-dev, ops, research) have their own launchd gateways with `HERMES_HOME` pointing to their profile directory - Each bot profile has cron jobs in its own `cron/jobs.json` - The default profile (Rowan) has 14 cron jobs; bot profiles have 1-2 each - All gateways running and reachable ## Expected behavior When clicking **Blog Writer** in the bot roster, the Routines pane should show Blog Writer's cron jobs (1 job: "Weekly Real Estate Blog Post"). ## Actual behavior The Routines pane always shows the default profile's 14 cron jobs, no matter which bot is selected. Sending a message to the bot (which connects to the bot's gateway does not fix it either. ## Root cause In (plugin.js, line ~7232): (the active gateway connection profile) takes precedence over (the bot the user clicked). When the user clicks a bot in the roster, updates to blog-writer but remains default because the chat connection is still routed through the default profile's gateway. This means is called with , so sends with no param, and the gateway returns the default profile's cron store. Even if the desktop connects to the bot's gateway (after sending a message), may still report default if the connection routing doesn't fully switch. ## Suggested fix The Routines pane should use (the bot the user clicked) for the cron query, not . The cron RPC already supports profile scoping via and the gateway honors it by setting override. The Routines pane just isn't passing the right profile. Option A (minimal): Option B (correct): The Routines pane should always use the selected bot for cron scoping, since cron jobs live in the profile's regardless of which gateway the chat is connected to. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop app (Electron) - macOS 26.6.2 - 7 bot profiles, 4 with launchd gateways - All profiles on Ollama Cloud provider BODY )

signal.title: [Feature] Smart web search routing with result cleaning/ranking + link click → external browser by default
signal.text: ## Summary Two related feature requests to improve web search UX and link navigation in Hermes Desktop. --- ## Feature 1: Smart Web Search Backend Routing with Result Cleaning & Ranking ### Current Behavior `web.backend` accepts only a **single** backend. Users must manually switch via `hermes tools` or UI when: - A backend's quota is exhausted (e.g., Tavily 1000/month limit hit) - Chinese-language queries return poor results from English-optimized backends - Network conditions make a backend temporarily unreachable (e.g., DuckDuckGo/Brave blocked in China) Issue #32159 requests ordered failover chains, but goes only halfway — it handles failure recovery, not intelligent routing. ### Proposed Behavior **Smart routing** that selects the best backend per-query based on: | Signal | Example | |--------|---------| | Query language | Chinese query → prefer Bocha/Tavily; English query → prefer Exa/Brave | | Backend health | Quota remaining, recent error rate, avg latency | | Network reachability | Auto-detect if backend is reachable from user's region | | Capability match | Need content extraction? → skip search-only backends (Brave, DDG, xAI) | **Result cleaning & ranking** after aggregation: - Deduplicate results across backends (same URL from Tavily + Exa = one entry) - Re-rank by relevance score, source authority, freshness - Clean snippets (remove tracking params, trim to meaningful text) - Return a unified, ranked result list regardless of which backend(s) were used This saves users: - **Token cost** — cleaner, deduped results = less noise fed to LLM - **Reading effort** — ranked results put the best answer first - **Manual switching** — no more UI dropdown toggling when quota runs out ### Config Surface (proposed) ```yaml web: search_backends: [tavily, exa, firecrawl] # ordered preference routing: auto: true # enable smart routing language_match: true # prefer backends matching query language health_check: true # skip unhealthy backends automatically results: deduplicate: true # merge same-URL results re_rank: true # relevance-based re-ranking max_snippet_length: 200 # trim long snippets ``` Backwards compatible: if `search_backends` is absent, fall back to existing single `backend` / auto-detect behavior. --- ## Feature 2: Link Click Behavior — Default to External Browser, Modifier for In-App Preview ### Current Behavior Source code analysis (v0.20.4) shows inconsistent link click behavior: - **Chat message links** (`artifacts/index.tsx`): click → `openExternal()` → system browser ✅ - **Tool result preview rows** (`preview-row.tsx`): plain click → in-app preview pane; Ctrl/Cmd+click → also in-app preview - **Search result cards**: open in preview pane, not in system browser Users who want to continue browsing in their own browser (with their cookies, logins, extensions) must manually copy URLs. ### Proposed Behavior Swap the modifier logic for tool result / search result links: | Action | Current | Proposed | |--------|---------|----------| | Plain click | In-app preview pane | **External browser** (system default, with user's cookies/sessions) | | Ctrl/Cmd + click | In-app preview pane | **In-app preview pane** | Rationale: - Most users want to **continue browsing** in their own browser where they're logged in - In-app preview pane is a **read-only webview** with separate cookies — not suitable for login flows, downloads, or interactive sites - The modifier (Ctrl/Cmd) is the standard pattern for "open in background/alternative" across browsers and IDEs - Zero config change needed — just swap the condition in `preview-row.tsx`'s `onActivate` handler ### Implementation In `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/preview-row.tsx`, swap the click logic: ```tsx // BEFORE (current): onActivate={event => { if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) { void togglePreview() // modifier → in-app preview } else { void openDefaultTarget() // plain click → also in-app preview (via openPreview) } }} // AFTER (proposed): onActivate={event => { if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) { void togglePreview() // modifier → in-app preview (power user) } else { void openExternal() // plain click → external browser (user's Chrome with cookies) } }} ``` --- ## Environment - Hermes Desktop v0.20.4 - Windows 11 - Multiple search backends configured (Tavily + Exa + Firecrawl) ## Related - #32159 — Ordered failover chains for web search/extract backends (this issue's Feature 1 is a superset) - #36838 — Web search automatic fallback (not merged) - #53149 — Add Bocha/Baidu/Serper search providers (not merged)

signal.title: [Windows] Smart App Control blocks unsigned Python DLL (_sqlite3.pyd) → Hermes backend fails to start
signal.text: Environment: Windows 11 24H2 (build 10.0.26200.9168), Hermes Desktop (CI build 2026-08-18, commit 8a770aae0d550bb92eb021913bd102a61ccc40af), Smart App Control enabled ## Summary With Windows Smart App Control (SAC) enabled, the Hermes Desktop backend cannot start: Python's _sqlite3.pyd (an unsigned DLL) is blocked by SAC, the backend exits before it becomes ready, and the desktop app shows "Hermes couldn't start" with no usable recovery. ## Symptoms Desktop shows: Hermes couldn't start The background gateway didn't come up. Error invoking remote method 'hermes:connection': Error: Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1). Backend log (desktop.log): ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _sqlite3: 应用程序控制策略已阻止此文件。 (application control policy blocked this file) ## Root cause 1. Hermes Desktop's backend runs a bundled Python (uv-managed cpython-3.11 + venv). Its C-extension DLLs — e.g. DLLs/_sqlite3.pyd — carry no Authenticode signature (verified: Get-AuthenticodeSignature → NotSigned). 2. Smart App Control, when On, enforces reputation-based code integrity: unsigned binaries with no cloud reputation are blocked, and no exception list is available (unlike Defender exclusions). 3. _sqlite3 is imported by the stdlib at backend startup, so the backend aborts immediately. ## Why it appears "suddenly" SAC typically starts in evaluation mode, which learns over a period and then auto-enables itself (or disables itself) when the evaluation period ends. The file in question existed unchanged for weeks (installed 2026-08-02) and loaded fine during evaluation mode; after SAC auto-enabled, the same file is blocked on the next backend launch. This is not a Hermes regression — it is SAC switching to strict enforcement. ## Impact Any Windows 11 user with SAC enabled cannot run Hermes Desktop at all (backend will not start). Since SAC cannot be disabled and re-enabled freely (once turned off it cannot be turned back on without resetting Windows), affected users are forced to choose between SAC protection and Hermes. ## Suggested fix 1. Sign the Windows components (the bundled Python interpreter, venv, and all .pyd DLLs) with a code-signing certificate so they pass SAC's trust checks. This is the proper fix and benefits all SAC users. 2. If signing is not feasible short-term, document the incompatibility in the Windows install instructions (e.g. "Smart App Control must be off; it has no allowlist") so users aren't surprised by a broken first launch. 3. Consider bundling a signed Python distribution (e.g. python.org installer-based CPython, whose binaries are signed) instead of the current unsigned uv-managed interpreter. ## Verification performed - Get-AuthenticodeSignature <python>/DLLs/_sqlite3.pyd → Status: NotSigned - Hermes backend starts normally as soon as SAC is turned off; fails consistently when SAC is on.

signal.title: vision_analyze: support public-image (URL) mode for providers that reject base64 inline images (e.g. SenseNova)
signal.text: ## Summary `vision_analyze` cannot recognize images when the vision provider only accepts public HTTP(S) image URLs (e.g. SenseNova 商汤). The tool always encodes local images to `data:image/png;base64,...` before sending, which SenseNova 6.8 rejects with `400 image download failed`. ## Root Cause In `agent/image_routing.py`, `_file_to_data_url()` always base64-encodes a local image into an inline data URL. The auxiliary vision path (`auxiliary_client.py`) forwards that data URL to the provider. Providers like SenseNova 6.8 / U1 Fast do **not** accept base64 inline images — they only accept a publicly reachable HTTP(S) URL and return: ``` {"error": {"message": "image download failed", "type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "3"}} ``` Direct curl to SenseNova with a public URL image succeeds in ~2s; the same image as a base64 data URL is rejected. ## Proposed Enhancement Add a **public-image mode** so an image input can be sent as an external URL when the provider supports it: 1. When the input to `vision_analyze` is already a public `http(s)://` image URL, pass it through as-is (do NOT base64-encode it). The main-agent path in `image_routing.build_native_content_parts` already supports `image_urls` passthrough — the auxiliary vision path does not. 2. Optionally, allow a config flag (e.g. `auxiliary.vision.public_url_only: true`) so providers that only accept URLs (SenseNova, etc.) can be used without a local ephemeral HTTP server. ## Environment - Hermes version: latest (tested 2026-08-19) - Vision provider: SenseNova 6.8 Flash Lite (`sensenova-6.8-flash-lite`) on `token.sensenova.cn` - OS: Windows 11

signal.title: feat/per-request generation params + /temperature slash command
signal.text: # PR Description — per-request generation params + /temperature slash command ## What does this PR do? Two complementary ways to control LLM sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, extra_body), sharing one `request_overrides` channel into the provider call: **1. API server passthrough.** `/v1/chat/completions` now accepts `model_options.generation` with `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, and `extra_body` (for provider-specific fields like `num_ctx`). It mirrors the existing `_request_reasoning_config` / `_request_service_tier` translators and merges into `request_overrides`, which already flows through `build_api_kwargs` to the provider. Fully backward compatible: absent `generation` = zero behavior change. **2. `/temperature` slash command** (CLI/TUI + all gateway platforms): - `/temperature` — show current (session override or config default) - `/temperature <0.0-2.0>` — set for this session - `/temperature <0.0-2.0> --global` — persist to config.yaml - `/temperature reset` — clear session override - Alias: `/temp` Session override is stored per-session (`ConversationState.temperature_override`), and merged into `request_overrides` on every turn via `_resolve_turn_agent_config()`. Because all platforms share the same gateway dispatcher, it works on Discord, Telegram, and every gateway platform automatically (Slack is reached via `/hermes temperature` due to the 50-slash cap). **Why this approach:** the `request_overrides` channel already existed and is proven (reasoning config, service tier, fast mode). This extends the same mechanism instead of adding a parallel system — so API callers and interactive users control the same dial through the same path. ## Related Issue No related issue — this is a standalone new-feature contribution. ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` — `_request_generation_params()` translator + merge into `request_overrides` in `_create_agent` (mirrors `_request_reasoning_config` / `_request_service_tier`) - `hermes_cli/commands.py` — `CommandDef("temperature", ...)` registry entry + `_SLACK_VIA_HERMES_ONLY` update (Slack 50-cap) - `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py` — `_handle_temperature_command()` (CLI/TUI handler) - `cli.py` — dispatch branch in `process_command()` - `gateway/slash_commands.py` — `_handle_temperature_command()` (gateway handler, mirrors `/reasoning` / `/fast`) - `gateway/run.py` — dispatch branch, `_session_temperature_overrides` plumbing, session override merged into `request_overrides` in `_resolve_turn_agent_config()` - `gateway/session_state.py` — `temperature_override` field on `ConversationState` (+ `clear()` + legacy field spec) - `tests/gateway/test_api_server.py` — 8 new unit tests for `_request_generation_params` ## How to Test 1. Pull the fork / run the patched build 2. In the TUI: `/temperature` → shows current (default unset) 3. `/temperature 0.95` → confirmed; `/temperature` again → shows session override 4. Ask the same creative question at 0.1 vs 0.95 in fresh sessions → measurable output differences (see field test below) 5. `/temperature reset` → returns to default 6. API: `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model_options.generation: {"temperature": 0.7, "extra_body": {"num_ctx": 32768}}` → params reach the provider 7. Repeat the slash commands in Discord/Telegram — same gateway dispatcher, no per-platform work **Field test (2026-08-11):** two fresh sessions, identical persona + 4-question prompt corpus, session temperature 0.1 vs 0.95: | Temperature | Words | Chars w/ spaces | Sentences | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0.1 | 821 | 4,749 | 61 | | 0.95 | 1,012 | 6,097 | 61 | +23% words / +30% characters with an identical sentence count — temperature modulates elaboration, not structure. ## Checklist ### Code - [ ] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) — *confirm before ticking* - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`feat: ...`) - [ ] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — *confirm before ticking* - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — *targeted suites green (183 tests: api_server, discord slash, commands, commands_execute); full-suite run shows pre-existing failures in `tests/hermes_cli/test_webhook_cli.py` that pass in isolation and are unrelated to this change* - [x] I've added tests for my changes (8 new unit tests) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (docstrings on new handlers; plan docs under `isabel/`) - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A (no new required config keys; `model.temperature` is read if present) - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` — N/A (extends existing documented patterns; no workflow changes) - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — N/A (pure Python, no OS-specific code) - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas — N/A (no tool changes; slash registry self-documents) ## Screenshots / Logs **Field test (2026-08-11)** — two fresh sessions, identical persona profile + identical 4-question prompt corpus, session-scoped temperature set via the new `/temperature` command: | Temperature | Words | Chars w/ spaces | Sentences | Read time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0.1 | 821 | 4,749 | 61 | 3m17s | | 0.95 | 1,012 | 6,097 | 61 | 4m3s | +23% words / +30% characters with an identical sentence count — the persona's structural habits stayed fixed while elaboration expanded. A concrete sample of the qualitative difference, same prompt ("Write a haiku about a cat that believes it is a dragon"): > **0.1:** "Tiny paws of flame, / The tabby hisses at clouds — / It breathes no fire, but pretends." > > **0.95:** "Whiskered ember, small — / yet beneath the hearth-lit fur, / smoke coils from your breath." At 0.1 the delusion is deflated; at 0.95 it is committed to. Both sessions preserved the persona's voice and formatting — temperature modulates elaboration, not identity. (N=1 per condition; presented as a demonstration that the channel works end-to-end, not as a quantitative characterization.)

signal.title: fix(desktop): keep all sessions when ALL-profiles scope is active with a single profile
signal.text: Fixes #84305 ## Problem In the desktop app, choosing **Grouping → Profile** in the sidebar Filters menu persists `$showAllProfiles`, which drives `$profileScope` to `ALL_PROFILES` even when there is only a single profile (`default`). The sidebar then computed `showAllProfiles = multiProfile && profileScope === ALL_PROFILES`, which is `false` for a single profile — so the flat sessions list was filtered against the `__all__` sentinel (`normalizeProfileKey(s.profile) === '__all__'`), matching nothing. Result: the sidebar's recents section rendered the empty state ("no sessions") even though the backend returned all rows for `recents_profile=all`. Clicking the `default` chip (which leaves ALL scope) instantly restored the list. The grouped rendering is intentionally gated on `multiProfile` (to avoid stranding single-profile users in a grouped view with no rail), but the *data scoping* must still fan every profile in when the scope is ALL. ## Fix Extract the scope selector into a pure helper, `selectVisibleSessions(sessions, profileScope)`, that treats `ALL_PROFILES` as "include everything" regardless of the multi-profile grouping gate, and filters by concrete profile otherwise. `scopedSessions` now uses it, so a single-profile user in the ALL scope sees their rows (as a flat list — the grouped view stays off because it is still gated on `multiProfile`). ## Tests Added `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-scope.test.ts` (6 tests) covering: - ALL scope returns every session - the regression: ALL scope with sessions owned by a single profile is not emptied - concrete scope returns only the matching profile - session profile normalization before matching - null profile treated as `default` - empty result when no session matches a concrete scope Verified: new + existing sidebar tests pass (125 tests, 14 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean.

signal.title: fix(security): recheck browser_exec's landed URL after execution
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? browser_exec validates the URLs it can see as literals in the code it is handed, and nothing after that. _blocked_url_in_code runs _URL_RE.findall on the source and checks each match once, before the subprocess is spawned. The code reaches the browser-use CLI as a Python string that is frequently not the string that was scanned, so a navigation target built at runtime or reached through a redirect is never re-examined. browser_navigate already has a post-redirect SSRF check and _current_page_private_url re-reads window.location.href after an eval for this reason. browser_exec is the one navigation surface that adopted only the pre-check. This applies the existing in-repo pattern: append a trailer that reports the landed URL, and block the output when the landed URL fails the navigation policy. SSRF protection is forced regardless of backend posture because browser_exec pipes arbitrary model-authored Python into the CLI. Output is withheld rather than annotated because stdout is where the page content comes back. No marker means the probe could not run, which fails open, matching _current_page_private_url. ## Related Issue No direct issue — discovered via code review and reproduced live (see below). signal.title: fix(desktop): surface profile-switch failures instead of swallowing them
signal.text: ## Summary The desktop profile rail's gateway switch used to fail **silently**. Every rejection inside `ensureGatewayProfile` (descriptor lookup, gateway preparation, socket dial) was caught by an empty `.catch()`, so a failed switch to another profile published nothing — no log, no UI state, no error. A dead click read as a broken rail, and the real reason (e.g. a failing descriptor IPC) was invisible in both the console and the swap overlay. This became visible in the field as "clicking Kuro/Vesper does nothing; only the All view still opens sessions." ## Changes - **Publish failures to a new `$gatewaySwitchError` atom + log to console** — the `ChatSwapOverlay` now renders "Couldn't switch to `<profile>` — `<message>`" in place of the spinner when a switch fails, instead of a silent no-op. i18n keys added for en/ar/ja/zh/zh-hant + the shared `types.ts` contract. - **Bound the `gatewaySwitch` mutex wait (30s)** — a wedged in-flight switch (hung descriptor IPC or stuck dial) previously blocked *every later click forever*: each new switch awaited the previous promise with no timeout, so one stuck switch bricked the whole rail for the session. The activation epoch guard makes a stale switch's late publish a no-op, so failing open is safe. Applied to both the profile and agent paths. - **Guard the mutex-release `finally` with identity** — when the bounded wait lets a newer switch start while the old one is still wedged, the stale `finally` no longer nulls out the newer switch's promise or swap target. ## Test Plan - `apps/desktop`: 44 tests pass across `profile.test.ts`, `gateway-switch`, `gateway-profile-request`, `profile-agent-activation`, `chat/index`, `i18n/languages` - `tsc --noEmit` clean - New tests: failed switch publishes the error and clears on retry; a wedged in-flight switch no longer blocks a later click; identity-guarded finally. - Pre-existing failures in `electron/*` (ssh, hardening, darwin staging) are Windows-host environment issues unrelated to this change — verified they reproduce on the base tree. ## Notes - Fixes the class where a failed profile switch is indistinguishable from a broken install: the first click after this change surfaces the real error message in both console and UI.

signal.title: [Bug]: Fresh install.sh aborts - git clone fails with HTTP 429 (packfile throttled for this repo)
signal.text: ## Human disclosure This bug report was logged by Opus 5 after fixing this specific issue for me for the current 1 line install script as of 2026-08-19 After the fix it applied things worked. I read the report and it makes sense, if you send this to an agent they should be able to reproduce and fix this issue. I also instructed my agent to check for duplicates and didn't find any when looking manually. Please forgive me I don't have time to write this by hand and I hope this is still useful. --- ### Bug Description Running the documented installer one-liner on a clean macOS machine fails at the **Download Hermes Agent** stage. Both the SSH and HTTPS clone paths fail, `install.sh` exits 1, and no usable install is produced (`~/.hermes` is left with `bin/`, `skills/`, `config.yaml` but no `hermes-agent` checkout). ``` → Installing to /Users/madda/.hermes/hermes-agent... → Trying SSH clone... → SSH failed, trying HTTPS... Cloning into '/Users/madda/.hermes/hermes-agent'... error: RPC failed; HTTP 429 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 429 fatal: expected 'packfile' ✗ Failed to clone repository ``` **This is not a client-side IP rate limit.** At the same moment: - an anonymous `git clone` of a small public repo (`octocat/Hello-World`) succeeded normally, and - `https://api.github.com/rate_limit` reported `core: 60/60 remaining`. So GitHub appears to be throttling *packfile generation for this specific repo*, which is large — 9,644 files at HEAD, plus the "thousands of auto-generated branches" that `install.sh`'s own comments call out. The single `git clone --depth 1` the installer issues asks the server to build one big pack in one shot, which is exactly the expensive operation being throttled. Related: #89287 reports the same HTTP 429 against the `hermes update` path. This report is about the **fresh-install `clone_repo()` path in `install.sh`**, which has no retry and no fallback. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Start on a machine with no existing `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` checkout, no GitHub SSH key, and no valid GitHub credentials. 2. Run the documented installer: `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash` 3. Installer passes prerequisites and reaches the "Download Hermes Agent" stage. 4. SSH clone fails fast (no key registered). 5. HTTPS fallback fails with `RPC failed; HTTP 429`. 6. Installer prints `✗ Failed to clone repository` and exits. Reproduced consistently on repeated attempts over several minutes. ### Expected Behavior `install.sh` completes the clone — or degrades gracefully by retrying with backoff and/or falling back to a cheaper clone strategy — so a fresh install succeeds on an ordinary unauthenticated machine. ### Actual Behavior `git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git` dies mid-packfile with HTTP 429, `clone_repo()` hits its `log_error "Failed to clone repository"` branch and `exit 1`s. Nothing is installed. ### Workaround that did work Staging the clone so the server never builds one large packfile: ```bash git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --filter=blob:none \ https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git ~/.hermes/hermes-agent cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent git reset --hard HEAD # materializes blobs; may need one retry ``` Then re-running `install.sh` takes the "Existing installation found, updating..." branch and proceeds normally. The follow-up incremental `git fetch origin main` completes in seconds — only the initial bulk clone is throttled. ### Suggested fixes 1. **Retry the clone with exponential backoff on 429.** #88475 already added retry for downloading the install script itself; the clone deserves the same treatment. 2. **Use `--filter=blob:none --single-branch` for the initial clone**, then materialize the tree. Much cheaper server-side, and it is what got past the throttle here. 3. **Make the ZIP/tarball fallback first-class**, as already proposed in #39529. ### Two smaller things noticed while working around this - **An invalid `gh` token makes the failure opaque.** git here is configured with `credential.https://github.com.helper = !gh auth git-credential`. With an expired token, every clone additionally emits `fatal: failed to store: 100001` next to the 429, which sends you chasing the wrong problem. Worth surfacing in `install.sh` / `hermes doctor`. - **The repo has a macOS case-collision.** `git ls-files` shows both `contributors/emails/agent@Agents-Mac-mini.local` and `contributors/emails/agent@agents-Mac-mini.local`. On a case-insensitive filesystem only one can exist, so `git status` is permanently dirty and `install.sh`'s update path stashes on every single run. ### Affected Component Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Setup / Installation ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell Not available — `hermes debug share` cannot be run because the install itself is what fails, so there is no hermes binary, venv, or log directory on this machine. ``` ### Operating System macOS 27.0 (build 26A5406e), Apple Silicon / arm64 ### Python Version 3.11.13 (installer-detected); system python3 is 3.14.6 ### Hermes Version n/a - install never completed ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signal.title: fix(desktop): scope active session lookup
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Scopes `resolveStoredSession()`'s first by-ID lookup to the renderer's active Desktop profile. Desktop's gateway socket and Electron REST routing are separate. Activating a non-default Bot profile updates the gateway, but an unscoped REST request still goes to the primary backend. The resolver then excluded the active profile from its fallback probes because it assumed that unscoped request had already checked it. A stored Bot Chat owned by the active non-default profile could therefore 404 on the primary backend and time out without ever querying its actual owner. The active profile is now explicit on the first lookup and remains authoritative even when a pooled or remote backend reports its own local alias. ## Related Issue Discord support report: https://discord.com/channels/1053877538025386074/1539430577185497138 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/utils.ts`: route the initial stored-session lookup through the active profile instead of the primary REST backend. - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/resolve-stored-session.test.ts`: cover a session that exists only on the active non-default profile and update the resolver ladder assertions. ## How to Test 1. Configure a local non-default Desktop profile with an existing stored Bot Chat. 2. Open that bot from the Bots pane while the primary backend belongs to another profile. 3. Verify Desktop queries the bot's active profile, resolves the session owner, and hydrates the transcript without a primary-backend `Session not found` timeout. signal.title: fix(mcp): skip dynamic tool refresh when session is closed or superseded
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? `tools/list_changed` refresh can queue behind shutdown or reconnect. A non-`None` `ClientSession` is not proof the transport is still live: teardown is not serialized by `_rpc_lock`, so a dying connection can still look open and a stale `tools/list` response can land after the session has been replaced or closed. This PR rebases the original snapshot + superseded-response discard onto current `main`'s collision-safe refresh body, then binds the fetch to a **session generation** snapshotted under `_rpc_lock`. **This PR now guarantees:** - Session pointer, generation, and `InitializeResult` capabilities are snapshotted only after `_refresh_lock` + `_rpc_lock`. - Closed (`session is None`) refreshes are a no-op. - Capability is taken from the locked generation, so a prompt/resource-only replacement is not asked for `tools/list`. - Teardown / recycle / reconnect / shutdown bump the generation *before* `ClientSession.__aexit__` starts closing the transport. - A closed-transport failure (`ClosedResourceError` / session-expired markers) on a **dying** generation is a clean skip: no error log, no registry mutation, no leaked refresh task. - Genuine `tools/list` protocol/server errors still propagate and still log `dynamic tool refresh failed`. - A superseded in-flight response is discarded and does not mutate the registry. - Current `main` collision-safe registry updates are preserved (ownership checks, normalization-ambiguous cleanup). **This PR does not invent a second ownership / publish model.** Discarding a superseded response does **not** publish the replacement session's tools. That authoritative reconnect / `list_changed` reconciliation belongs to #68808. In-flight RPC cancellation on teardown belongs to #48069. The generation counter is a refresh-liveness signal only and is compatible with both. ## Related Issue Related to MCP dynamic-refresh races on closed / superseded / dying sessions. Canonical narrow repair after #83354 closed as a duplicate of this PR. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `tools/mcp_tool.py`: - `_session_generation` + `_invalidate_session_generation()` / `_adopt_session()` / `_refresh_generation_stale()` - `_refresh_tools()` snapshots session/generation/capabilities under the locks; skips closed sessions; treats dying-transport errors as a clean skip; discards superseded responses - `_advertises_tools(init_result=...)` can evaluate a locked snapshot - generation bump on stdio recycle, lifecycle return (shutdown/reconnect), `shutdown()`, `run()` finally, and new session adopt - registry mutation body is current `main`'s collision-safe path - `tests/tools/test_mcp_dynamic_discovery.py`: closed, queued-reconnect, superseded-discard, locked capability, dying-transport (stdio + HTTP), genuine-error, and generation-invalidation tests ## How to Test ``` scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_dynamic_discovery.py tests/tools/test_mcp_capability_gating.py tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py -q ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] Conventional Commits (`fix(mcp):`) - [x] Only MCP refresh lifecycle changes - [x] Tests for closed / superseded / dying-transport refresh paths - [x] Focused MCP suite after rebase: 33/33 on discovery+capability; session-expired / pagination / failure-class / transport-group / reconnect-signal green; `test_mcp_tool.py` 93 passed (4 failures are missing `httpx`/`dotenv` in this environment, unrelated to this diff) - [x] `ruff check`, `compileall`, `git diff --check`, Windows-footgun scan clean on the touched files ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] N/A for docs / config / AGENTS.md / tool schemas

signal.title: fix(tui): avoid destructive redraw on focus regain
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Makes terminal focus recovery repaint from blank virtual frame buffers without clearing the physical screen or re-asserting terminal modes. The focus-regain handler previously reused the destructive `/redraw` path. Every focus change sent `ERASE_SCREEN`, resent mouse-tracking DECRESET sequences, and then rebuilt the frame. That caused a visible full-screen redraw and introduced unnecessary terminal-mode output on ordinary tab or pane changes. The replacement keeps the stale-row recovery: it resets the virtual buffers and renders a complete replacement frame. The existing screen remains visible until that frame is ready, and focus regain sends neither the clear-screen sequence nor mouse-mode resets. ## Related Issue Discord support report: https://discord.com/channels/1053877538025386074/1538966610776301719 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Replace focus-in's `reassertTerminalModes()` plus `forceRedraw()` calls with a virtual frame reset and direct repaint. - Add a behavioral regression test proving focus recovery repaints content without emitting `ERASE_SCREEN` or `DISABLE_MOUSE_TRACKING`. ## How to Test 1. Run `npm test -- packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/ink-focus-redraw.test.ts` from `ui-tui`. 2. Run `npm run typecheck` from `ui-tui`. 3. signal.title: [Bug]: Desktop Restore after in-place compaction refused with 4030 (live-scrollback ordinal ≠ resolved row_id)
signal.text: ### Bug Description After **in-place** context compaction (same `session_id`, no parent), Desktop **Restore** on a still-active user turn is refused with **4030**: ``` truncate_before_user_ordinal (N) does not match truncate_before_row_id target turn (M) prefix_user_count=0 ``` `truncate_before_row_id` **resolves correctly**. The cut is refused only because Desktop also sends a client ordinal counted over **live scrollback that survived compact**. Same error code as #88082, different trigger: | | #88082 / #88092 | this report | |---|---|---| | When | cold-open, transcript longer than the 120-row prefetch | live session; compaction just ran; pre-compact bubbles still on screen | | Ordinal direction | client **smaller** than durable (window missing prefix) | client **larger** than the gateway **tip** (scrollback still includes compacted / handoff user rows) | | `prefix_user_count` | 0 | 0 | | Would #88092 fix it? | yes, when `possiblyTruncated` | **no** — live scrollback is treated as complete, so the ordinal is still sent | No history is deleted (4030 fail-closed is doing its job). Restore on those still-active turns stays dead. Related, not this bug: #87547 is **4004** (ordinal-only, missing `row_id`). Compacted-away turns correctly return **4018** and are out of scope. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Hermes Desktop, durable session, `compression.in_place` left at default (on). 2. Stay in the session long enough for in-place compaction to fire. Do not cold-open. Do not click “Show earlier messages”. 3. Confirm pre-compact user bubbles are still visible, plus a `[CONTEXT COMPACTION]` handoff. 4. Restore / rewind a user turn that is **still in the tip** (not one compacted away). 5. Actual: 4030, `prefix_user_count=0`, client ordinal ≠ tip ordinal for the same resolved `row_id`. 6. Retry: same refusal. ### Expected Behavior Restore aimed by `truncate_before_row_id` succeeds. If a client ordinal is sent, it must be in the same space the gateway uses — or omitted once a durable id is present. ### Actual Behavior Gateway returns **4030**. Transcript unchanged. Restore remains unusable for those still-active turns. Example shape (sanitized): client ordinal **greater than** tip ordinal for the resolved row (observed 2 or 4 vs tip 1), `prefix_user_count=0`. Log line: `REFUSED truncation due to ordinal mismatch` / `Stale truncate_before_user_ordinal detected`. The ordinal is not stale; it is display-lineage. ### Affected Component - Other (Hermes Desktop + local TUI gateway `prompt.submit`) - Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (not a messaging adapter — Desktop UI talking to the local gateway) ### Debug Report [hermes-gui-89244-sanitized.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31185841/hermes-gui-89244-sanitized.log) ### Operating System macOS 27.0 (arm64) ### Python Version 3.11.15 ### Hermes Version 0.20.3 (2026.8.16.2), local gateway. Desktop packaged 0.17.0 (not source-mode). ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ``` prompt.submit: REFUSED truncation due to ordinal mismatch (ordinal=<client>, truncate_before_row_id_ordinal=<tip>, truncate_before_row_id=<resolved>, prefix_user_count=0). Stale truncate_before_user_ordinal detected. ``` Row id resolved. Client ordinal > tip ordinal. No session id / row id / transcript text included. ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) Two ordinal spaces, plus a translation that only exists on the **fork/parent** compact path: 1. Desktop `visibleUserOrdinal` (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions`) counts `role === 'user' && !hidden` over the renderer list. After in-place compact, Desktop keeps the pre-compact bubbles (`includeCompacted` in `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts`; `compactedTurnRef` in `use-message-stream` skips a post-compact reload). The compaction handoff is hidden in the UI but is still a `role=user` row without `hidden` / without `display_kind`. 2. Gateway `_history_user_indices` / `_reconcile_client_ordinal` (`tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py`) count the **tip** only: `role == "user" and not display_kind`. In-place compact does not create a parent and does not fill `display_history_prefix` (`get_ancestor_display_prefix` is empty when there is no parent). 3. #87563 accepts `tip_ordinal + prefix_user_count` as agreement. That count is taken from `display_history_prefix`. On in-place that list is empty → `prefix_user_count=0` → any display-vs-tip disagreement is treated as #82756 drift → 4030. 4. #82756 / #82959 / #83785 correctly refuse when ordinal and row_id disagree. The check is right; the client should not ship a display-space ordinal next to a durable id. Gateway already supports the safe shape: `client_ordinal is None` + resolved `truncate_before_row_id` aims the cut by id. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Smallest: when `truncate_before_row_id` or a real durable `truncate_before_message_id` is present, **omit** `truncate_before_user_ordinal`. Keep 4030 as a real-conflict guard. Do **not** ignore a mismatched ordinal on the gateway when a row_id resolves (#82756). #88092 is the same idea gated on tail-only prefetch. This case needs the rule whenever a durable address exists, including a complete live transcript after in-place compact. Optional later (not required to unblock Restore): make in-place populate `display_history_prefix` so the #87563 translation applies. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? Open to but I do think the fix is only a workaround so I am open for real fix instead

signal.title: fix(desktop): aim truncations by durable id alone (edit/restore refused 4030)
signal.text: ## Problem In the Desktop app, editing (or reloading / restoring) a user message is refused by the gateway with 4030 when the client ordinal and the resolved durable id disagree: ``` truncate_before_user_ordinal (N) does not match truncate_before_row_id target turn (M) ``` Two triggers, same refuse: | | #88082 | #89244 | |---|---|---| | When | cold-open, transcript longer than the 120-row prefetch | live session; in-place compaction just ran; pre-compact bubbles still on screen | | Ordinal direction | client **smaller** than durable (window missing prefix) | client **larger** than the gateway **tip** (scrollback still includes compacted / handoff user rows) | | `prefix_user_count` | 0 | 0 (structurally: `get_ancestor_display_prefix` is cross-session) | Reported in #88082 with full evidence (221-row session; gap = hidden durable user turns). Reported in #89244 for Restore after in-place compact (`prefix_user_count=0`, row id resolves, display-lineage ordinal does not). ## Root cause `planEdit` / `planReload` / `planRestore` count truncate ordinals over the renderer list (`visibleUserOrdinal`). That list is not the gateway tip: - Cold-open hydrates a newest-first REST prefetch page (`LATEST_SESSION_MESSAGES_LIMIT = 120`); older rows only enter via "Show earlier messages". - After in-place compact, Desktop keeps pre-compact bubbles (`includeCompacted` / `compactedTurnRef` skips a post-compact reload). In-place never creates a parent, so `display_history_prefix` stays empty and #87563's `tip + prefix_user_count` translation cannot apply. The bubble still carries its durable `rowId`, so the client sends **both** addresses; the gateway's #82959 cross-check resolves the durable id to its tip ordinal, reads the offset as drift, and refuses. Reconstructing the renderer's ordinal space on the gateway means reproducing visibility rules the gateway does not own. ## Fix When a durable `truncate_before_row_id` or a real durable `truncate_before_message_id` is present, `runRewindSubmit` drops the client ordinal and addresses the truncation by id alone. This is the same rule the function already applies to content-resolved row ids (#87059): "the row id alone is the address; sending the divergent ordinal too would trip the gateway's 4030 cross-check." - One choke point covers edit, reload, restore, and both call surfaces (primary chat and session tiles). - Dropping the ordinal cannot mis-aim a cut: the gateway aims by the resolved durable id (`_reconcile_client_ordinal`: "never by the client ordinal"), and the bubble's row id comes from the authoritative REST hydration of that exact row. Unknown ids still fail closed at 4018. - First-turn rewind still sends `confirm_empty_truncate` from the caller's ordinal-0 belief. - An earlier revision of this PR gated the drop on `transcriptBackfillAvailable` / `possiblyTruncated`. That assumed a complete live transcript means the two ordinal spaces agree. #89244 falsifies that, so the gate is gone. This adopts the scope #88314 proposed (closed as superseded by the earlier, narrower revision of this PR). ## Tests - `rewind.test.ts` (`runRewindSubmit durable-address discipline`): - bound row id → ordinal omitted, no extra `session.history` read - complete live transcript + durable row id → ordinal omitted (#89244) - durable platform message id → ordinal omitted, message id kept - caller ordinal 0 + durable id → `confirm_empty_truncate` kept, ordinal omitted - `index.test.tsx` restore/edit paths no longer expect a client ordinal next to a durable message id - Sabotage: with the drop disabled, exactly the four durable-id ordinal-omission tests fail; with the fix, all pass - `vitest run` on `use-prompt-actions/` + `transcript-backfill.test.ts`: **229 passed** - `tsc -p . --noEmit`: clean. `eslint` on touched files: clean (pre-existing `exhaustive-deps` warnings, untouched). `prettier --check`: clean ## Risk / exclusions - Renderer-only change; gateway behavior untouched (id-only addressing is an already-supported, fail-safe path — `client_ordinal is None` accepts and aims by durable id). - The remaining tripwire-true-positive is "wrong but valid row id on the bubble, ordinal right". Unknown ids still 4018. A renderer binding bug that points at the *wrong existing* row would now cut there instead of 4030 — same residual as the #87059 content-resolved path. - Not in scope: populating `display_history_prefix` for in-place (resume-time, stale for a live compact, and a naive count over-counts the protected tail). - TUI and dashboard load full history and were never affected by the prefetch bug; the in-place display-lineage skew is Desktop-specific (`includeCompacted`). Closes #88082 Closes #89244

signal.title: Let Hermes give live guided tours of the UI
signal.text: ## Summary Hermes can now show you how something works instead of describing it: dim the screen, spotlight the thing it's talking about, and narrate. Ask "how do I do X?" and you get a walkthrough of the actual UI, live. One generic `tour` tool backs it — no tour content lives in the codebase. The agent calls `targets` to discover what's on screen, then either narrates at its own pace (`show`, one highlight per call) or hands you a paged tour with Next/Prev (`start`). It runs on two surfaces: the Hermes app itself, and whatever page is open in the preview pane, so any web app can be toured. Target discovery is the part that makes it reliable. `targets` returns every addressable element with a selector, a label, and a `stable` flag — stable selectors key off identity (`data-tour`, `id`, `data-testid`, `aria-label`) and survive a re-render, positional paths don't. Stable ones sort first, and a selector that stops matching comes back with a re-scan hint instead of a dead end. Built on [driver.js](https://driverjs.com) (MIT, ~5KB gzipped, no runtime deps). Popovers are repainted from the app's own theme tokens, so tours follow every theme and custom skin. The engine is not agent-only. `@/lib/tour` exports the verbs directly, so a feature can ship its own curated walkthrough: ```ts import { startTour } from '@/lib/tour' startTour([ { selector: '[data-tour="composer"]', title: 'Composer', text: 'Type here.' }, { selector: '[data-tour="files"]', title: 'Files', text: 'Browse your project.' } ]) ``` ### How it's wired | Layer | What it does | |---|---| | `tools/tour_tool.py` | Schema + validation, `desktop_ui` toolset, blocking bridge (`tour.request`/`.respond`) like `read_preview` — works on local, SSH, URL, and cloud backends | | `lib/tour/engine.ts` | One action → a driver.js highlight, a paged tour, or a step change | | `lib/tour/collect-targets.ts` | Scans any document; marks each selector stable or positional | | `lib/tour/run-tour.ts` | The public verbs; picks the surface | | `right-rail/preview-tour.ts` | Injects the engine + driver.js into the preview webview | The engine and collector are written self-contained — no imports, no closures — so the same source runs in the renderer and, stringified, inside a webview guest page. A test pins that contract, since the preview surface breaks silently without it. `driver.js` is excluded from `optimizeDeps`: it only enters the graph through a dynamic import, so letting the scanner find it at first use prebundles the `?raw` IIFE as a module and forces a mid-session page reload. ## Test plan - [x] 10 engine tests: target discovery, stable-selector ordering, step paging, malformed selectors, recovery hints, self-containment - [x] Both desktop-tool contract tests updated (`GUI_TOOLS`, post-hook `_CASES`) — 46 Python tests green - [x] Schema probe with no desktop env vars: `tour` present for a desktop session, absent for TUI - [x] `tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean on every touched file - [x] Manual: app tour (highlight + paged), preview tour against a live page, theme-token styling

signal.title: fix(tools): add HERMES HARNESS session capabilities
signal.text: ## HERMES HARNESS This PR contributes the recoverable tool-result capability layer of **HERMES HARNESS**, the Hermes-native context and tool-result economy system. **Naming boundary:** DeepSeek Harness/DSH is research provenance only. This is not an installation of the DSH runtime; it is a native extension of Hermes Agent's existing result-storage architecture. ## Summary - bind oversized model-facing tool results to opaque `hermes-spill://v1/...` capabilities scoped to the current Hermes session; - resolve capabilities host-side through `read_file` before ordinary backend path routing; - preserve the existing path-based spillover behavior only for legacy callers without session context; - support direct transports and Codex MCP, including capability-only `read_file` registration; - propagate session scope through concurrent/sequential agent execution and nested local/remote `execute_code` RPC calls. ## Security properties - scoped persistence fails closed to a bounded preview if capability storage is unavailable; it never downgrades to a predictable host or sandbox path; - payloads are AES-GCM authenticated ciphertext at rest; - the bearer token is present only in the URI; filenames contain its SHA-256 locator, not the token itself; - the session scope and plaintext digest are authenticated as AES-GCM associated data; - resolution validates session scope, bearer token-derived filename, symlink/reparse status, opened-file identity, regular-file type, POSIX mode/ownership where available, AEAD tag, and plaintext digest; - FIFO/device replacements are opened nonblocking and rejected as non-regular files; - ordinary filesystem paths remain rejected by the Codex capability reader. ## Compatibility - capability encryption keys are deterministically derived from the random bearer token in the URI, so valid capabilities remain recoverable after process restart without a profile-wide secret; - local, Docker, SSH, Modal, and Daytona legacy spill behavior is unchanged for callers without a session ID; - direct `model_tools.handle_function_call` transports now use the same persistence seam as the agent executor; - `execute_code` forwards the parent session ID through both UDS and remote file-RPC dispatch. ## Verification Fresh focused runs on commit `d0155e2c83011ef0ed7b5b1d39bf2640c3daa5dc`: - `152 passed, 7 subtests passed` — result capability/storage, Codex MCP, execute-code local/mode coverage, incremental persistence; - `57 passed` — Codex app-server runtime/integration and context tracking; - `9 passed` — dispatch session-ID and transform-hook behavior; - `1 passed` — capability-specific `read_file` path; - `git diff --check` clean; - changed production modules compile with `py_compile`. A broad macOS `tests/tools/test_file_tools.py` run has two unrelated existing assertions that expect `/tmp/...` while the implementation canonicalizes it to `/private/tmp/...`; the capability-specific read path passes. ## Scope This extends the existing `tools/tool_result_storage.py` mechanism rather than introducing a second storage engine. It does not add the DeepSeek Harness runtime, Cordis, web application, or SurfaceOp abstractions.

signal.title: [desktop] Renderer process burns 40-70% CPU at idle since early August — thermal throttling on macOS Intel
signal.text: ### Environment - macOS 13.3.1, MacBook Pro 2019 (Intel Core i5-8279U, 4C8T, 16GB) - Hermes v0.20.2 (2026.8.16), Electron 40.10.2, packaged desktop build - GPU disabled via `desktop.disable_gpu=true` (partially mitigates) ### Symptom - `Hermes Helper (Renderer)` consumes **40-73% CPU continuously while idle** (no streaming, no content updates; window focused or not) - `Hermes Helper` main process additionally 16-44% - macOS thermal throttling engaged: `CPU_Speed_Limit` dropped to 24-68 → fans at max, machine sluggish - Started early August 2026; worsening since - **Survives app restart**; **present in v0.20.2** (upgraded 0.19.0 → 0.20.2, 2394 commits) ### Evidence Renderer sampling over 26 min of uptime: **11:01 CPU / 26:31 wall = 41.6% average**, instantaneous 73.3% — with the app sitting on a **blank new conversation** (long-session rendering ruled out). | process | idle CPU (instant) | avg | |---|---|---| | Renderer | 52.8-87.8% | 41-70% | | Helper (main) | 19.4-44.5% | 16-31% | | WindowServer | 37.8% | repaint storm | ### Already ruled out - Not long-session DOM: reproduced on a fresh empty conversation - Not memory pressure: 77% free, 1GB swap - Not corporate VPN agent (aTrust/EAIO): ~0% CPU - Not Macs Fan Control: ActivePreset=Predefined:0 (auto mode) - Not battery: 31°C while charging - `desktop.disable_gpu=true` partially mitigates: ~70% → ~40% (GPU compositor loop is part of the cause, not all) ### Suspects (source scan) High-frequency timers in `apps/desktop/src` that re-render on every tick: - `src/app/hud/hud-shell.tsx:237` — `setInterval(measure, 300)` (HUD) - `src/app/hud/hud-shell.tsx:329` — `setInterval(measure, 500)` - `src/app/chat/chat-swap-overlay.tsx:28` — 80ms frame animation - `src/app/messaging/index.tsx:237` — 6s tick - several 1s `setNow`/`setNowMs` intervals Note: `src/app/shell/hooks/use-status-snapshot.ts` already gates its 60s refresh on `document.hasFocus()`/`visibilityState` correctly; other timers may not. ### Expected - Fix the idle repaint loop (gate timers/animations on focus & visibility) - Or expose a config to disable ambient animations/timers ### Impact Idle machine gets thermally throttled; on Intel Macs severe (CPU_Speed_Limit 24 ≈ 1/4 frequency); fan noise and battery life affected. Started early August 2026 (approx. the 8/6 update window).
