signal.title: [Bug]: Desktop Bot Mode times out loading session history when opening a Bot
signal.text: ## Bug Description Opening any Bot from the Hermes Desktop Bot Mode roster often fails with a session-history timeout. The error appears during the initial “waking up” flow: > Couldn't open the Bot's chat > Timed out loading the Bot profile's session history Clicking Retry usually opens the Bot successfully. This reproduces with newly created Bots, so it does not appear to be caused by a corrupted Bot Chat or a large conversation history. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Run Hermes Desktop on Windows 11. 2. Create a fresh Bot using Bot Mode. 3. Use a custom SOUL.md or a short role description. 4. Disable Composio MCP. 5. Leave the Bot's default canonical `Bot Chat` session. 6. Close and reopen Hermes Desktop. 7. Click the Bot in the Bots roster. 8. Observe the session-history timeout. 9. Click Retry. 10. The Bot opens successfully. ## Expected Behavior Clicking a Bot should open its canonical `Bot Chat` directly after the Bot backend becomes ready. A temporary profile-backend wake-up delay should be retried internally and should not surface as a session-history error to the user. ## Actual Behavior The Desktop Bot Mode UI times out while loading the Bot profile's session history. Retry usually succeeds. ## Evidence - The issue reproduces with more than one newly created Bot. - Composio MCP was disabled, but the issue remained. - The Bot profile's state database contained only 1 session and 4 messages. - The same canonical Bot Chat opened successfully through the CLI: `hermes -p hongsam chat --in C:/Users/hyj53 -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q` - The CLI returned `HONGSAM_BACKEND_OK`. - This indicates that the Bot profile, model authentication, session database, and canonical session are valid. - The failure appears specific to the Desktop Bot Mode open/resume path. ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 - Hermes version: 0.20.4 - Surface: Hermes Desktop - Feature: Bot Mode - Provider: openai-codex - Model: gpt-5.6-luna - Bot profile: hongsam - MCP: Composio disabled ## Related Issues Possibly related to #88146, but the current problem reproduces with fresh Bots and presents specifically as a session-history loading timeout. ## Additional Investigation The local Bot Mode plugin's `openBotCanonicalChat` path was tested with a local patch that attempts to open the stored canonical session directly before calling `session.list`. The timeout behavior was still observed after creating a fresh Bot, suggesting this may involve the Desktop plugin/runtime version or profile-backend prewarm path rather than only the session-list fallback logic.

signal.title: fix(desktop): disable native window shadow on Quick Entry
signal.text: ## Summary Quick Entry (the global-hotkey mini composer, ⌘⇧Space) shows a visible **border-like ring** behind the card on macOS. **Root cause**: the window is `transparent: true` and the card renders its own CSS `boxShadow` (see `quick-entry-app.tsx`). With `hasShadow: true`, the OS draws a **rectangular** shadow around the entire window bounds instead of following the card's rounded corners — so a rectangle-shaped shadow ring shows through the transparent backdrop around the card. **Fix**: `hasShadow: false` on the Quick Entry window, matching the pet overlay and other transparent floating windows (which already use `false`). The card keeps its own CSS shadow, so the visual depth is preserved — just without the broken rectangular ring. ## Screenshot Before: rectangular shadow ring visible around the card's rounded corners. After: clean card, only the CSS shadow remains. ## Test Plan - [ ] ⌘⇧Space summons Quick Entry with no border-like ring behind the card - [ ] Card still has its intended CSS shadow - [ ] No regression to other transparent overlays (pet overlay etc.)

signal.title: fix: read deprecated cwd vars from .env file, not os.environ
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes a false-positive in the startup deprecation warning: `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` claimed `TERMINAL_CWD` / `MESSAGING_CWD` were "found in .env" by reading **`os.environ`**, not the `.env` file. Hermes bridges `terminal.cwd` into `TERMINAL_CWD` in the process environment at startup (gateway config bridge), so an `os.environ` read falsely triggers the warning even when: - the user never wrote the deprecated var to `.env`, and - the `.env` line is commented out (e.g. `# TERMINAL_CWD=.`). ## Root cause `hermes_cli/config.py` → `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()`: ```python terminal_cwd_env = os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD") # reads env, not .env ... if terminal_cwd_env and not config_has_explicit_cwd: # "TERMINAL_CWD=... found in .env — this is deprecated." ``` The comment in the original code even says "likely from .env" — it never checks the file. Since Hermes itself injects `TERMINAL_CWD` into the environment (resolving the `.` placeholder to `Path.home()` and bridging terminal config to `TERMINAL_*` vars), every startup with `terminal.cwd: .` in config.yaml and a Hermes-injected env emits a spurious migration warning. ## Fix Read the deprecated vars from the **`.env` file** via the existing `load_env()` helper (which skips comment/blank lines), not from `os.environ`: - `.env` entry present → warning still fires (migration is genuinely needed). - Only ambient env var / Hermes bridge → no warning. ## Tests Added/updated in `tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py`: - `test_messaging_cwd_triggers_warning` — env vars set but only `.env` content matters; `TERMINAL_CWD` absent from `.env` must not warn. - `test_both_deprecated_vars_warn` — both vars in `.env` warn. - `test_terminal_cwd_ignored_when_config_has_explicit_cwd` — explicit `terminal.cwd` in config.yaml suppresses the warning. - `test_env_var_without_dotenv_entry_does_not_warn` — **regression**: `TERMINAL_CWD` in `os.environ` (Hermes bridge) but absent from `.env` must not warn. Verification: - `tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py`: 4 passed. - End-to-end with a temp `HERMES_HOME`: env-only var → no warning; `.env` entry → warning emitted with correct hint. - Broader `tests/hermes_cli -k "config or env or dotenv or cwd"`: 917 passed; 32 failures reproduce independently of this change (browser-install / venv-health tests, pass when run in isolation).

signal.title: feat(clarify): ask multiple independent questions in one call
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? The `clarify` tool gets an optional `questions` parameter. The agent can ask 2-5 independent questions in one call. Before this change, the agent asked one question per call. Each extra question cost a full round-trip, and composite questions caused a combinatorial explosion of choices (#18450). The user answers the questions in any order. If the prompt times out part-way on the TUI or the CLI, the answers the user already locked are kept: the tool result carries them with a `timed_out` flag, and unanswered entries stay blank. This lets the agent tell a deliberate skip from an absent user. Behavior per surface: - **Desktop**: one card shows every question. Picks and typed answers stage locally, and one **Confirm and continue** button (enabled once every question has an answer) submits the whole batch. Staged answers stay editable until that confirm. Skip cancels the whole batch. - **TUI and CLI**: a compact status list (`✓` answered / `▸` active / `·` pending) with the active question always expanded. Enter locks the active answer and moves to the next unanswered question. Tab and Shift-Tab cycle the questions in both directions, with wrap. A locked answer renders on its own indented line in a distinct color under its question. On the CLI, a re-visited question restores the earlier selection, a typed answer stays visible next to the Other row, and Enter on an answered Other prefills the input for editing. - **Messaging platforms**: the batch falls back to the existing single-question prompt, one question at a time. If the user stops responding, the remaining questions are not sent. **cli** **tui** **desktop** The single-question path is byte-identical to the previous behavior on every surface. Wire protocol: one `clarify.request` carries the question list with server-generated per-question ids. `clarify.respond` gets an optional `question_id` that locks or overwrites one answer. A respond without `question_id` keeps its existing meaning (cancel). The reconnect replay snapshot carries the locked answers, so a reattached client restores its state. The update-in-place shape also leaves room for a follow-up that persists interim answers in the session database. This PR also fixes a duplicate-card bug found during testing: the desktop hydration-race merge correlated the `tool.start` row and the `clarify.request` row through the top-level `question` text, which a batch payload does not have, so the batch card mounted twice. The correlation key for a batch now comes from the joined per-question texts. Related work: PR #70129 proposes a separate `clarify_form` tool for the same issue. This PR extends the existing tool instead, so no new core tool ships on every API call. Deferred to follow-ups, by design: interim answer persistence in the session database, TUI multi-select, a desktop checkbox affordance for multi-select, and the CLI answer-restore behavior on the TUI. ## Related Issue Fixes #18450 Closes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/70129 ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `tools/clarify_tool.py` — the `questions` schema parameter, batch validation, batch dispatch, and a sequential fallback loop for legacy callbacks. signal.title: [Feature]: Support multiple independent questions in clarify tool
signal.text: ## Problem or Use Case The `clarify` tool currently accepts only one `question` parameter (a single string). When the agent needs to ask the user multiple independent questions, the only workaround is to concatenate them into one composite question and offer composite choices (e.g. combining "How do you feel?" + "What color do you like?" into one question with choices like "Feeling good, likes blue" / "Feeling tired, likes red" — each choice encoding answers to both questions). This does not scale: 2 questions x 4 choices each = 16 composite options; 3 questions x 3 choices each = 27. The UX degrades rapidly and the agent effectively cannot batch more than 2 small clarification needs at once. Real-world example from use: agent wants to ask (1) user preference on approach A vs B, and (2) user availability timeline. These are independent dimensions — forcing them into a single composite question is unnatural and the combinatorial explosion of choices makes it impractical. ## Proposed Solution Add an optional `questions` array parameter alongside the existing single-`question` parameter. Each question object has its own `question` text and optional `choices` array. The rendering layer (CLI prompt_toolkit, TUI, gateway adapters) presents them as separate widgets/forms, and the tool returns an array of answers keyed by question index or id. Example schema addition: ```json { "questions": { "type": "array", "description": "Multiple independent questions to ask at once. Use instead of single-question when you have 2+ independent clarification needs.", "maxItems": 5, "items": { "type": "object", "properties": { "id": { "type": "string", "description": "Short identifier for matching responses (e.g. 'approach', 'timeline')" }, "question": { "type": "string", "description": "The question text" }, "choices": { "type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "maxItems": 4, "description": "Up to 4 answer choices. Omit for open-ended text input." } }, "required": ["question"] } } } ``` Backward compatibility: the existing single-`question` parameter remains untouched. When `questions` is present, it takes precedence and the single-question parameter is ignored. ## Alternatives Considered 1. **Composite question + composite choices (current workaround)**: Works for 2 small questions but does not scale. 3+ questions become combinatorially impossible. 2. **Multiple sequential `clarify` calls**: Works but wastes conversation turns and context tokens. The agent cannot efficiently batch multiple independent clarification needs. 3. **Free-text multi-question with no structured choices**: Loses the structured choice UX that makes `clarify` useful. Harder for the agent to parse free-form multi-answer responses reliably. 4. **Agent-side heuristics to skip unnecessary questions**: Not always applicable — sometimes multiple independent decisions genuinely need user input. ## Feature Type New tool ## Scope Medium (few files, under 300 lines) ## Contribution - [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

signal.title: fix(desktop): paginate archived sessions
signal.text: ## Summary - paginate the all-profile archived-session query instead of stopping at 200 rows - share the pagination helper between Settings → Archived Conversations and the sidebar Archived view - expose the backend `offset` parameter through `listAllProfileSessions` - allow aggregate pages to reach rows beyond the old 500-row per-profile source window Closes #88438 ## Root cause Both archived-session surfaces called `listAllProfileSessions(200, ..., 'only')` once, so every row after the first 200 remained invisible. The backend already reported the true `total` and accepted `offset`, but its aggregate query capped each profile's source window at 500 rows. That made a later request such as `offset=500` return an empty page even when the profile had 577 archived sessions. `listEveryArchivedSession()` now requests 200-row pages until the accumulated rows reach the backend total. The aggregate route includes the requested offset in its per-profile source window, so later pages remain reachable. Only the source window needed to produce an explicitly requested page can exceed 500. Recents and command-palette limits are unchanged.

signal.title: fix: /goal turn counter stuck at 0 when streaming is enabled
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes a bug where `/goal` turn counter stays at `0` forever when streaming is enabled (the default). When `streaming.enabled=true`, `_handle_message_with_agent()` delivers the response via streaming chunks and returns `None`. The goal continuation hook in `_handle_message()` then tries to extract `_final_text` — but `None` is neither `dict` nor `str`, so `_final_text` stays empty and the entire goal evaluation block is skipped: - `evaluate_after_turn()` is **never called** - `turns_used` stays **0 forever** - `/goal status` always shows `0/N turns` - Goal judge never runs → goal never completes ## Root Cause `gateway/run.py` — streaming path `return None` discards the response text that the goal hook needs. The goal continuation hook only handles `dict` and `str` return types, missing the `None` case. ## Fix Three changes in `gateway/run.py`: 1. **`__init__`** (~L5654): Initialize `self._last_streamed_response: Dict[str, str]` — a one-shot, session-scoped stash. 2. **`_handle_message_with_agent` streaming exit** (~L17299): Before `return None`, stash `response` text keyed by `session_key`. 3. **`_handle_message` goal hook** (~L14937): When `_agent_result is None`, recover text via `pop(_quick_key, "")` — one-shot consumption ensures no stale entries. This preserves the existing behavior (return `None` to avoid double-delivery) while making the response text available to the goal continuation hook. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) ## How to Test 1. Enable streaming (`streaming.enabled=true`) 2. Set a goal: `/goal complete this task` 3. Send a message to the agent 4. Check `/goal status` — before fix: `0/N turns`, after fix: `1/N turns` 5. Goal judge now runs and can reach `done` verdict ## Verification Tested on live instance + unit tests: - Before fix: `turns_used=0`, `last_turn_at=0.0`, no goal judge calls in logs - After fix + gateway restart: `turns_used` increments normally, goal can reach `done` verdict - 6 tests pass (including 2 new regression tests for the streaming `None` path) ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] N/A — no config keys, tool schemas, or architecture changes

signal.title: [Bug] Desktop: re-opening the already-focused session from the Bots panel hangs forever (never times out)
signal.text: # [Bug] Desktop: re-opening the already-focused session from the Bots panel hangs forever (never even times out) ## Summary Clicking a session row in the Bots panel freezes the pane with no error and no recovery when the target session is the one **already focused on the main surface**. It does not fail — it never settles at all, so it does not even reach the 20s hydration timeout. For an actively-used profile this is the *common* case, not an edge case: the bot roster previews the profile's most recent session, which is exactly the session the user has open. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (2026.8.18), desktop build 2026-08-18T22:24Z - Windows 11, local gateway, 4 local profiles (multiplex, Telegram) - Reproduced across app restarts and a full machine reboot ## Repro 1. Open a chat in profile `X` on the main surface and leave it focused. 2. Open the Bots panel and select agent `X` → its session list. 3. Click the row for that same session (it is the newest, so it is at the top). **Expected:** the conversation is shown (it is already open — a no-op is fine). **Actual:** the pane freezes indefinitely. No error toast, no Retry, no timeout. Gateway log for the click — connection accepted, never closed: ``` 20:15:54 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:50522 (no matching "ws closed" — the open never settles) ``` Contrast with a click that *does* fail (different pinned session, not focused), which reaches the timeout and surfaces the stranded-session UI: ``` 20:10:00 ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:58150 20:10:43 ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:58150 ← ~43s: hydration timeout path ``` ## Root cause `apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts` — `waitForFocusedSessionHydration()` resolves only from inside `check()`, and `check()` runs on atom **change**: ```ts unbinds.push($activeGatewayProfile.listen(check)) unbinds.push($selectedStoredSessionId.listen(check)) unbinds.push($activeSessionId.listen(check)) unbinds.push($messages.listen(check)) ``` These are **global** atoms (`store/session.ts:567`), so when the requested session is the focused one they already hold their target values. The initial `check()` at the end of the function does fire, but `openSession()` was called with `intent: 'main'` on a surface that is already in that exact state, so no atom transitions and no listener fires again. The awaited promise therefore never settles. The `setTimeout` that would reject it is armed, but the pane is already wedged by the in-flight open, so the user sees an indefinite freeze rather than the intended timeout → Retry surface. Callers: `plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js:7425` (`openProfileSession`) and `plugin.js:2993` (`openStoredBotChat`), both with `awaitHydration: true`. ## Fix Settle immediately when the requested open is already satisfied, before awaiting a transition that cannot happen. The guard uses the *same* four-part predicate as the hydration check, so a genuinely stale or blank surface still takes the resume path (i.e. it does not reintroduce #89206): ```ts if ( options.awaitHydration && normalizeProfileKey($activeGatewayProfile.get()) === targetProfile && $selectedStoredSessionId.get() === storedSessionId && Boolean($activeSessionId.get()) && (!expectHistory || $messages.get().length > 0) ) { return } ``` ## Verification - `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean. - `node --test src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/*.test.mjs` — 279/279 pass (276 before, plus 3 new). - New test `reopen-focused-session-hang.test.mjs` is sabotage-verified: 3/3 **fail** with the guard removed, 3/3 pass with it. - `npx vitest run --project ui` — 4866/4870 pass. The 4 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (locale thousands separators under pt-BR, e.g. `1.234.567` vs `1,234,567`); verified identical on a pristine checkout of the same commit. ## Related - #89206 (closed) — blank Bot Chat; same surface, opposite direction. The fix there added the hydration wait this bug hangs on. - #68594 — desktop profile switch resumes previous session.

signal.title: fix(gateway): preserve history for shared primary profile routes
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Shared primary messaging adapters can route a turn to a secondary profile, but the gateway previously loaded that turn history from the adapter owner root store. This change keeps the complete routed turn lifecycle in the selected profile scope while preserving owner-scoped authorization and secrets. Without the fix, follow-up messages lose prior context and can produce incorrect responses even though the transcript was persisted successfully. ### Symptom A secondary profile served through a shared primary adapter answers the first message, but later messages in the same session reload an empty history. The root `state.db` receives session metadata while the routed profile `state.db` receives the transcript. ### Impact Users of `gateway.multiplex_profiles` with shared primary adapters can experience same-session amnesia on routed conversations. Follow-up requests that depend on earlier turns may ask for information already provided or act on the wrong context. ### Bug Cause **Trigger:** `gateway/run.py` / `GatewayRunner._handle_message_with_agent` when a shared primary adapter stamps a secondary `source.profile`. **Causal chain:** 1. The primary adapter correctly performs ingress authorization and route stamping in its owner profile scope. 2. Session creation and transcript loading begin before the old code enters the routed profile scope, so lazy session DB handles resolve to the owner/root store. 3. The agent later persists messages in the secondary profile store, splitting one conversation across two databases and leaving the next turn with no history. **Why it is wrong:** Session creation, transcript loading, post-turn bookkeeping, durable-marker cleanup, and agent persistence are one profile-local lifecycle, but the scope boundary previously began too late and ended too early. **Working sibling / contrast:** Single-profile gateways already use one storage scope for the entire turn and remain on their existing path. **Ruled out:** Compression is not responsible. The regression reproduces the split with no compression and verifies the exact session and transcript rows in real temporary SQLite stores. ### Fix The gateway now enters the routed profile scope after owner authorization and route stamping, then retains it through agent execution, post-turn hooks, and durable active-turn cleanup. Regression tests cover a two-turn shared-primary route with distinct owner/routed secrets and stores, plus the post-turn and cleanup scope boundaries. ### Upgrade note Conversations already split by this bug may start a new routed session after upgrading. Their transcripts remain present in the secondary profile's `state.db`; however, the old routing entry is in the root store while the transcript-side session row lacks the gateway peer metadata required for an unambiguous automatic rebind. This affects only conversations created while the bug was present. New turns stay entirely in the routed profile store. ## Related Issue Closes #89346 ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `gateway/run.py` - keep multiplexed session handling, post-turn bookkeeping, and durable cleanup in the routed profile scope, and unwind claimed state if profile scope setup fails. - `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py` - verify two routed turns reload history from the secondary profile store while the root store stays empty. - `tests/gateway/test_gateway_command_dispatch_minimal.py` - verify agent execution, post-turn hooks, and cleanup retain the routed home and secret scope. ## How to Test 1. Run the focused gateway regression suite: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py tests/gateway/test_gateway_command_dispatch_minimal.py tests/gateway/test_active_turn_recovery.py tests/gateway/test_64674_multiplex_primary_token_scope.py -q ``` 2. Confirm all 40 tests pass. 3. Run `uv run ruff check gateway/run.py tests/gateway/test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py tests/gateway/test_gateway_command_dispatch_minimal.py` and `git diff --check`. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this is not a duplicate - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix - [x] I ran the relevant repository test entry and all 40 focused tests pass - [x] I added tests for my changes - [x] I tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant documentation: N/A - no user-facing configuration or API changed - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A - no config keys changed - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md`: N/A - no architecture or workflow contract changed - [x] Cross-platform impact considered - existing profile ContextVar and path abstractions are used - [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A - no model tool behavior changed ## Screenshots / Logs N/A - this is a gateway storage-scope fix covered by deterministic SQLite and lifecycle regression tests.
